sources.title: Mormon’s Map
sources.author: John L. Sorenson
sources.publisher: Foundation for Ancient Research and Mormon Studies (FARMS), Brigham Young University
sources.summary: Sorenson builds a relative map from statements in the Book of Mormon. He reads “up” and “down” as elevation. He turns travel days into rough miles. He later compares the model with real lands.
sources.limitations: Sorenson calls his map simplified and partial. His figures do not all share one scale. His mile figures are estimates that may be off by about a quarter. Chapter 6 links the shape to Middle America; this app leaves that step out.
sources.license: Copyrighted book. This app gives page references and short summaries only. Read the full text at the source link.

sources.title: The Book of Mormon (bcbooks/scriptures-json, bom-4)
sources.author: Benjamin Crowder, editor of the data file
sources.summary: The reading text comes from a public-domain data file. It follows the 1981 edition with the 2013 corrections. Chapter summaries and footnotes are not included.
sources.limitations: Small caps appear as capital letters. Italics are not marked.
sources.license: The data file is in the public domain.

sources.title: Leaflet
sources.author: Volodymyr Agafonkin and contributors
sources.summary: Leaflet draws the map. This app uses a flat grid of miles, not a globe.
sources.limitations: The software does not add facts to the map.
sources.license: BSD 2-Clause license. See dist/vendor/leaflet-LICENSE.txt.

sources.title: Across Arabia with Lehi and Sariah
sources.author: Warren P. Aston
sources.publisher: Journal of Book of Mormon Studies 15, no. 2
sources.summary: Aston follows the family from Jerusalem to the coast of Oman. He compares each stage with the land of Arabia.
sources.limitations: The text gives directions and travel times, not coordinates. Every camp after Jerusalem is a proposal.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives short original summaries only.

sources.title: A New Candidate in Arabia for the Valley of Lemuel
sources.author: George D. Potter
sources.publisher: Journal of Book of Mormon Studies 8, no. 1
sources.summary: Potter describes a stream in a canyon east of the Gulf of Aqaba. He proposes it as the river Laman.
sources.limitations: Other researchers propose other valleys. No inscription names the valley.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives short original summaries only.

sources.title: The Place That Was Called Nahom: New Light from Ancient Yemen
sources.author: S. Kent Brown
sources.publisher: Journal of Book of Mormon Studies 8, no. 1
sources.summary: Brown reports an altar in Yemen that names the tribe Nihm. He links the name to Nahom.
sources.limitations: The altar shows the name in the region. It does not mark Ishmael’s grave.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives short original summaries only.

sources.title: The Arabian Bountiful Discovered? Evidence for Nephi’s Bountiful
sources.author: Warren P. Aston
sources.publisher: Journal of Book of Mormon Studies 7, no. 1
sources.summary: Aston describes a green inlet on the south coast of Oman. He compares it with Nephi’s description of Bountiful.
sources.limitations: Aston says the site may not be the exact place. Other researchers prefer a different inlet.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives short original summaries only.

sources.title: Terrain Tiles and Natural Earth
sources.author: Mapzen, USGS, NOAA, and Natural Earth contributors
sources.summary: The Old World relief uses measured elevation data. Coasts and rivers come from Natural Earth.
sources.limitations: The data shows the land today. Coasts and rivers have changed since Lehi’s time.
sources.license: Open data. Terrain: Mapzen, USGS, and NOAA. Natural Earth is in the public domain.

sources.title: Book of Mormon Onomasticon
sources.author: BYU Library and contributors
sources.publisher: Harold B. Lee Library, Brigham Young University
sources.summary: The Onomasticon studies the names in the Book of Mormon. Its entries list possible Hebrew, Egyptian, and other roots.
sources.limitations: Name meanings are proposals, not certainties. Entries often give more than one possible root.
sources.license: Copyrighted reference. This app gives short summaries only. Read each entry at the source link.

sources.title: Book of Mormon Pronunciation Guide
sources.author: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
sources.summary: The Church edition lists how to say each Book of Mormon name.
sources.limitations: The guide gives English pronunciation. It does not give name meanings.
sources.license: Copyrighted Church text. This app links to it.

sources.title: Scripture Central KnoWhy articles
sources.author: Scripture Central (formerly Book of Mormon Central)
sources.summary: Short research articles explain a Book of Mormon passage, name, or custom.
sources.limitations: Each article gives one research view. Some views are debated.
sources.license: Copyrighted articles. This app gives short summaries only.

sources.title: Has an Artifact That Relates to the Book of Mormon Been Found? (KnoWhy 103)
sources.author: Book of Mormon Central
sources.summary: The article reviews a Jerusalem stamp seal of Malkiyahu, son of the king. It asks whether he could be Mulek.
sources.limitations: The seal does not name the king. Malkiyahu was a common name, so the link to Mulek is a proposal.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Was Nephi’s Slaying of Laban Legal? (KnoWhy 256)
sources.author: Scripture Central
sources.summary: The article reads 1 Nephi 4 against ancient Israelite law. It draws mainly on John W. Welch.
sources.limitations: The article gives one legal reading. It does not claim that modern law would excuse the act.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Why Did the Nephites Call their Divine Compass Liahona? (KnoWhy 743)
sources.author: Scripture Central
sources.summary: The article reviews proposals for the meaning of the name Liahona.
sources.limitations: Each meaning is a proposal. Scholars agree only on parts of the name.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Why Did the Nephites Stay in Their Tents during King Benjamin’s Speech? (KnoWhy 80)
sources.author: Scripture Central
sources.summary: The article compares Benjamin’s gathering with the Israelite Feast of Tabernacles. It draws on work by Terrence Szink and John Welch.
sources.limitations: The text never says why the people stayed in tents. The festival link is an inference from parallels.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Why Are There Men Named Alma in the Book of Mormon? (KnoWhy 760)
sources.author: Scripture Central
sources.summary: The article argues that Alma is an ancient Semitic name for men. It reviews finds from Ebla and the Bar Kokhba period.
sources.limitations: Some readings of the ancient name are debated. The article comes from a group that defends the Book of Mormon.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: How Was Abinadi a Prophet like unto Moses? (KnoWhy 731)
sources.author: Scripture Central
sources.summary: The article lists parallels between Abinadi before Noah and Moses before Pharaoh.
sources.limitations: The parallels come from scholarly reading. The text does not state most of them.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: How Were the Amlicites and Amalekites Related? (KnoWhy 109)
sources.author: Book of Mormon Central
sources.summary: The article reviews the manuscript spellings of both names. It reports Royal Skousen’s view that the two groups were one people.
sources.limitations: The Alma 2 part of the original manuscript is lost. The link is a proposal, and some scholars reject it.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Why Did Moroni Quote the Patriarch Jacob about a Piece of Joseph’s Coat? (KnoWhy 154)
sources.author: Book of Mormon Central
sources.summary: The article explains the title of liberty as a war banner. It compares it with ancient inscribed banners.
sources.limitations: The banner comparisons are parallels, not proof. The Jacob story is not in the Bible.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: How Old Were the Stripling Warriors? (KnoWhy 161)
sources.author: Book of Mormon Central
sources.summary: The article weighs views on the age of Helaman’s young soldiers.
sources.limitations: The text gives no ages. Scholars disagree on the age range.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Why You Should Care About the Nephite Weights and Measures System (KnoWhy 322)
sources.author: Book of Mormon Central
sources.summary: The article explains the Nephite units of gold, silver, and grain in Alma 11. It compares them with an old Mesopotamian law code.
sources.limitations: The comparison shows a parallel in form. It does not show a direct link.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: Why Did the People Cut Down the Tree after Hanging Zemnarihah? (KnoWhy 192)
sources.author: Book of Mormon Central
sources.summary: The article compares the felled tree in 3 Nephi 4 with Jewish rules on hanging.
sources.limitations: The Jewish sources it cites come from after Lehi’s time. The link is a proposal.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

sources.title: The Prophetic Laments of Samuel the Lamanite
sources.author: S. Kent Brown
sources.publisher: Journal of Book of Mormon Studies 1, no. 1
sources.summary: Brown reads two laments in Samuel’s sermon in Helaman 13. He compares them to biblical laments.
sources.limitations: The poetic structure is one scholar’s reading of the text.
sources.license: Copyrighted article. This app gives a short summary only.

chapterMaps.title: Lehi warns Jerusalem
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi, a son of Lehi, begins his record in Jerusalem. His father, Lehi, prays and sees God in a vision. Lehi reads a heavenly book about Jerusalem's destruction. He warns the people and speaks of a coming Messiah. Some people in Jerusalem seek to kill him.

chapterMaps.title: A family leaves Jerusalem
chapterMaps.summary: The Lord tells Lehi to leave Jerusalem. Lehi takes his family into the wilderness. Laman and Lemuel, Nephi's older brothers, complain. Nephi prays and seeks God's help. The Lord promises Nephi a land if he obeys.

chapterMaps.title: The search for the plates
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi sends his sons back to Jerusalem for a set of brass plates. Laban, a powerful man in the city, keeps those plates. Laban refuses their request and takes their property. Laman and Lemuel strike their younger brothers. An angel tells them to return.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi brings back the records
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi enters Jerusalem and finds Laban drunk. The Spirit tells him to kill Laban. He takes the plates with help from Laban's servant, Zoram. Zoram agrees to join the family.

chapterMaps.title: Sariah sees her sons return
chapterMaps.summary: Sariah, Lehi's wife, fears that her sons have died. Their return strengthens her trust in the Lord. Lehi reads the brass plates and learns his family line. The family keeps the records for its journey.

chapterMaps.title: Why Nephi writes
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi explains the purpose of his record. He leaves out his family's full genealogy. He wants readers to come to God and be saved. He tells later writers to preserve things of worth.

chapterMaps.title: Ishmael's family joins the journey
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi sends his sons back for the family of Ishmael, a man in Jerusalem. Ishmael's daughters will become the sons' wives. Some rebel on the journey back. Nephi escapes the ropes that bind him. The families return to Lehi and give thanks.

chapterMaps.title: Lehi's dream of the tree
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi describes a tree with desirable fruit. He invites his family to eat it. People follow an iron rod, lose their way, or mock others. Lehi urges Laman and Lemuel to obey the Lord.

chapterMaps.title: Two sets of plates
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi describes two sets of records. One holds the history of kings and wars. The other gives more space to religious teaching. He trusts the Lord's purpose for both.

chapterMaps.title: Lehi speaks of the Messiah
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi foretells Jerusalem's fall and the coming Messiah. He describes a prophet who will baptize the Messiah. He compares scattered Israel to broken olive branches. Nephi wants to learn these things for himself.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi sees the Savior
chapterMaps.summary: The Spirit shows Nephi the tree from Lehi's dream. An angel shows him Mary and the Son of God. Nephi sees Christ's ministry, baptism, and death. He learns that the great building represents the world's pride.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi sees his descendants
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi sees wars among his descendants. He sees destruction before Christ visits the survivors. Generations live in peace before pride and war return. His people's destruction follows.

chapterMaps.title: Records cross the sea
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi sees nations beyond the promised land. He sees people cross the sea and receive a book. An angel describes truths lost from that record. Other records will make the Lamb's teachings known.

chapterMaps.title: Two churches and a covenant
chapterMaps.summary: An angel describes the choices facing the Gentiles. He shows Nephi two opposing churches. God's covenant people receive power despite their small numbers. Nephi leaves part of the vision for another writer.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi answers his brothers
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi finds his brothers disputing Lehi's words. He explains Israel's scattering and later gathering. He identifies the iron rod as God's word. He also explains the river and final judgment.

chapterMaps.title: Hunger on the journey
chapterMaps.summary: The families marry and receive a guiding instrument. Nephi's broken bow leaves them without food. He makes another bow and asks where to hunt. Ishmael dies, and further complaints lead to the Lord's correction.

chapterMaps.title: The command to build a ship
chapterMaps.summary: The family reaches a coast called Bountiful. The Lord tells Nephi to build a ship. His brothers mock him, and he recalls God's help to Moses. God's power shakes them when they oppose Nephi.

chapterMaps.title: The voyage and the landing
chapterMaps.summary: The family finishes the ship and sails. Nephi's brothers bind him during the voyage. A storm ends after they release him. They reach the promised land and begin to plant crops.

chapterMaps.title: Records and the suffering Savior
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi explains how he makes and uses his plates. He foretells the Savior's rejection and suffering. He recalls prophets who testified about Christ. He reads to his brothers from Isaiah, a prophet of ancient Israel.

chapterMaps.title: The Lord calls Israel to leave Babylon
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi quotes Isaiah's words to the house of Israel. The Lord rebukes false claims of faithfulness. He declares his power and purpose. He calls his people to leave Babylon.

chapterMaps.title: The Lord remembers Zion
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah describes a servant called to gather Israel. The Lord promises help to scattered people. Zion fears that the Lord has forgotten her. He promises to remember and rescue her children.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi explains the gathering
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi explains Isaiah's words to his brothers. Israel will scatter and later receive God's help. The Lord will defeat those who fight his people. Nephi urges obedience and endurance.

chapterMaps.title: Lehi's final counsel
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi recalls the Lord's help on the journey. He warns his sons about disobedience in the promised land. He asks them to support Nephi. He also blesses Zoram, Laban's former servant, and his descendants.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob hears about freedom and redemption
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi speaks to Jacob, a son born in the wilderness. He teaches about suffering and redemption. He explains why opposition allows people to act. He describes Adam and Eve's choice. He urges his sons to choose life through the Messiah.

chapterMaps.title: Lehi blesses Joseph
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi speaks to his youngest son, Joseph. He recalls Joseph of Egypt's promise about a future seer. Records from different peoples will join together. Lehi asks Joseph to follow Nephi's words.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi's prayer after Lehi's death
chapterMaps.summary: Lehi blesses his descendants before he dies. Nephi recalls the Lord's goodness but grieves over his sins. He asks God to help him resist evil. His prayer ends with trust in God.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi's people settle apart
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi leaves his brothers because they seek his life. His followers settle in a land they call Nephi. They build a temple and work the land. Nephi describes their records, worship, and later conflicts.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob speaks about scattered Israel
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob, Nephi's younger brother, teaches from Isaiah about Israel's future. He speaks of Jerusalem's loss and the Savior's rejection. Israel will gather when its people believe in Christ. The Lord will defend those who wait for him.

chapterMaps.title: The servant trusts the Lord
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob quotes the Lord's questions about Israel's separation. A servant describes suffering without turning back. He trusts the Lord to defend him. The passage warns those who follow their own light.

chapterMaps.title: Zion is called to awake
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah asks the people to remember Abraham and Sarah. The Lord promises comfort and lasting salvation. Jerusalem must awake after suffering. Zion is called to rise from captivity.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob explains resurrection and judgment
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob teaches that Christ rescues people from death. All will rise and face God's judgment. He warns against sins and pride in learning or wealth. He invites his hearers to turn to the Lord.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob describes Israel's return
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob speaks again about Christ and Israel. He foretells Christ's rejection and the scattering of the Jews. The Lord promises their return when they believe. Jacob asks his hearers to choose God.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi introduces Isaiah's words
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi records selected teachings from Jacob. He says that he, Jacob, and Isaiah have seen the Redeemer. He takes joy in God's promises and mercy. He introduces more words from Isaiah.

chapterMaps.title: Nations come to the Lord's house
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah sees nations coming to the Lord's house. He describes a future end to war. He then warns Judah about wealth, idols, and pride. The Lord's day will bring the proud low.

chapterMaps.title: Judgment comes upon Jerusalem
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah describes the loss of food and good rulers. The Lord judges leaders who take from the poor. Isaiah also condemns the pride of Zion's daughters. Jerusalem faces mourning and loss.

chapterMaps.title: The Lord shelters the survivors
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah describes survivors after Jerusalem's suffering. The Lord cleanses the city of blood and impurity. Those who remain in Zion are called holy. The Lord gives them shelter from heat and storms.

chapterMaps.title: The vineyard bears bad fruit
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah sings about a vineyard that bears bad fruit. The vineyard represents Israel and Judah. He condemns greed, drunkenness, and calling evil good. An invading people approaches the land.

chapterMaps.title: Isaiah receives a call
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah sees the Lord in the temple. A burning coal cleanses his lips. He accepts a call to speak to an unresponsive people. The vision also describes a remnant after destruction.

chapterMaps.title: Isaiah speaks to Ahaz
chapterMaps.summary: Judah fears an attack from the kings of Syria and Israel. Isaiah tells Ahaz, the king of Judah, that their plan will fail. He gives the sign of Immanuel. He also warns about the coming power of Assyria.

chapterMaps.title: Assyria threatens the land
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah names a child as a sign of coming loss. Assyria will overwhelm Syria and Israel. The Lord warns against fear and false counsel. Isaiah looks to God's testimony while darkness spreads.

chapterMaps.title: Light and judgment
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah announces light for people in darkness. He describes a child who will rule with peace. The passage then turns to Israel's pride and injustice. God's judgment continues against the people.

chapterMaps.title: Assyria's pride is judged
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah condemns laws that harm the poor. Assyria serves as an instrument of judgment but boasts of its power. The Lord will punish that pride. A remnant of Israel will return.

chapterMaps.title: A ruler and a gathered people
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah describes a ruler from the family of Jesse, King David's father. He will judge fairly and defend the poor. Peace will reach even the animal world. The Lord will gather scattered Israel.

chapterMaps.title: A song of thanks
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah gives a song for the day of deliverance. The people thank the Lord for comfort. They praise him as their strength and salvation. They call others to make his deeds known.

chapterMaps.title: Babylon faces destruction
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah announces a judgment against Babylon. Armies gather for a day of terror. Babylon's pride and power will fall. The passage describes its lasting ruin.

chapterMaps.title: The fall of a proud ruler
chapterMaps.summary: Isaiah promises rest for Israel. A song mocks the fallen king of Babylon. The Lord also announces judgment against Assyria. Philistia, a land near Judah, receives a warning about further danger.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi explains his witness of Christ
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi explains why Isaiah can be hard to understand. He foretells Jerusalem's loss and the Jews' return. He testifies that salvation comes through Christ. He teaches his people to keep the law while looking to Christ.

chapterMaps.title: Christ and the future of Nephi's people
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi foretells Christ's visit after signs and destruction. Pride will later destroy his people. He warns against churches built for gain. He teaches that God invites all people to receive his goodness.

chapterMaps.title: A sealed book and a work of God
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi describes a future book and its sealed words. A learned man refuses to read the sealed record. The Lord gives his words to another reader. God promises a work that overturns human pride.

chapterMaps.title: Warnings about false teaching
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi describes churches that dispute and teach false ideas. He warns against pride, easy excuses for sin, and spiritual sleep. The devil uses anger and false peace. God continues to teach those who receive his words.

chapterMaps.title: The Lord speaks to more than one nation
chapterMaps.summary: The Lord answers those who reject additional scripture. He remembers the Jews and their record. He speaks to people in many nations. Their records will come together.

chapterMaps.title: Scattered peoples receive the gospel
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi describes people receiving the record and believing in Christ. Descendants of his people will learn their history. Jews and Gentiles will join God's covenant through repentance. The passage looks toward peace and revealed truth.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi teaches the path of Christ
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi recalls the Savior's baptism. He teaches repentance, baptism, and receiving the Holy Ghost. These acts begin the path toward eternal life. Followers must continue with faith, hope, and love.

chapterMaps.title: Words of Christ and prayer
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi answers questions about what follows baptism. Christ's words tell believers what to do. The Spirit will also guide them. Nephi tells them to pray before they act.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi closes his record
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi explains his care for his people. He trusts God to make his written words useful. He asks readers to believe in Christ. He ends with a warning to those who reject his words.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob receives the small plates
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi gives his younger brother Jacob charge of the small plates. Jacob must preserve important religious teachings. A new king rules after Nephi's death. Jacob and his brother Joseph teach against growing sins.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob condemns pride and unfaithfulness
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob speaks with grief about his people's sins. He condemns pride in wealth and mistreatment of others. He then rebukes unauthorized plural marriages. He describes the pain caused to wives and children.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob addresses the pure in heart
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob asks the pure in heart to trust God. He warns the unrepentant Nephites of destruction. He praises the Lamanites' faithfulness to their families. He tells the Nephites to remember their own sins.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob writes about faith in Christ
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob explains why his people preserve records. He describes prophets who trusted Christ before his coming. He asks readers to receive God's counsel. He introduces a question about Israel's rejected foundation.

chapterMaps.title: Zenos's story of the olive trees
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob quotes Zenos, an ancient prophet of Israel. Zenos tells of a vineyard and its olive trees. Its lord and servants tend, prune, and graft the trees. Good fruit later becomes corrupt. A final effort preserves good fruit before the vineyard's end.

chapterMaps.title: Jacob explains the vineyard's warning
chapterMaps.summary: Jacob applies Zenos's words to his hearers. God will again work to gather Israel. Jacob asks the people to repent while mercy is offered. He warns of judgment and ends his teaching.

chapterMaps.title: Sherem challenges Jacob
chapterMaps.summary: Sherem, a skilled speaker, denies that Christ will come. Jacob defends his witness and refuses to seek a sign. Sherem receives a sign, confesses, and dies. Jacob later gives the plates to his son Enos.

chapterMaps.title: Enos prays for his people
chapterMaps.summary: Enos, Jacob's son, prays and receives forgiveness for his sins. He then prays for the Nephites and Lamanites. The Lord promises to preserve the records. Enos describes his ministry and hope in the Redeemer.

chapterMaps.title: A people preserved through warning
chapterMaps.summary: Jarom, the son of Enos, writes briefly about the Nephites. Prophets call them to repentance and faith in the coming Messiah. They defend themselves against repeated attacks. Jarom gives the plates to his son Omni.

chapterMaps.title: Records reach Benjamin
chapterMaps.summary: Five descendants of Jacob keep the small plates in turn. They are Omni, Amaron, Chemish, Abinadom, and Amaleki. Amaleki, the last of them, tells how Mosiah leads faithful Nephites north. They find the city of Zarahemla and a people who left Jerusalem with Mulek. Mosiah becomes king of both peoples and reads a stone from an earlier people. Amaleki gives the plates to King Benjamin, Mosiah's son.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon joins the records
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon, a later prophet, makes a shorter record from many Nephite records. He finds Nephi's small plates and joins them to his record. He recalls King Benjamin's battles and the work of prophets. Their efforts restore peace among the people.

chapterMaps.title: Benjamin prepares his sons
chapterMaps.summary: King Benjamin, the Nephite king in Zarahemla, teaches his sons from the preserved records. He explains why those records matter. He chooses his son Mosiah, named after Benjamin's father, as the next king. Mosiah calls the people together to hear Benjamin.

chapterMaps.title: Benjamin speaks about service
chapterMaps.summary: Benjamin addresses families gathered near the temple. He recalls serving them without seeking wealth. He teaches that service to others serves God. He warns against rebellion and urges obedience.

chapterMaps.title: An angel's message about Christ
chapterMaps.summary: Benjamin recounts an angel's message. Jesus Christ will suffer, die, and rise. His sacrifice offers salvation to those who repent. Benjamin teaches humility and warns of judgment.

chapterMaps.title: Forgiveness and care for the poor
chapterMaps.summary: The people ask for mercy and receive forgiveness. Benjamin teaches them to remember God's greatness and goodness. He asks them to teach their children and help the poor. He warns them to watch their thoughts, words, and deeds.

chapterMaps.title: The people make a covenant
chapterMaps.summary: The people say that Benjamin's words have changed their hearts. They covenant to obey God. Benjamin calls them children of Christ. He asks them to remain faithful to the name they have received.

chapterMaps.title: Mosiah begins to rule
chapterMaps.summary: Benjamin records the names of those who made the covenant. He appoints priests and makes Mosiah king. Benjamin later dies. Mosiah works the land and seeks his people's peace.

chapterMaps.title: Ammon finds Limhi's people
chapterMaps.summary: Years earlier, a man named Zeniff led a group back to the land of Nephi. King Mosiah sends sixteen men to find Zeniff's people. Ammon, a strong man of Zarahemla, leads the search. He reaches Shilom and meets King Limhi, Zeniff's grandson. Limhi learns that Zarahemla still exists. He urges his people to trust God.

chapterMaps.title: Limhi asks about the unknown records
chapterMaps.summary: Ammon teaches Limhi's people. Limhi describes a search party that found ruins and metal plates. He asks whether someone can read them. Ammon explains that King Mosiah is a seer who can translate them.

chapterMaps.title: Zeniff returns to Nephi
chapterMaps.summary: Zeniff, Limhi's grandfather, begins his own record. He recalls his desire to settle in the land of Nephi. King Laman, a Lamanite ruler, gives his people Nephi and Shilom. They rebuild and farm the land. They later defend themselves against a Lamanite attack.

chapterMaps.title: Zeniff defends his people
chapterMaps.summary: Zeniff prepares weapons and guards. A Lamanite army attacks after years of peace. He describes the beliefs that drive their hatred. His people prevail, and he later gives the kingdom to his son Noah.

chapterMaps.title: Noah rejects Abinadi's warning
chapterMaps.summary: King Noah, Zeniff's son, rules with heavy taxes and corrupt priests. He builds richly while his people become wicked. Abinadi, a prophet among them, warns that bondage will follow unless they repent. Noah and the people reject him.

chapterMaps.title: Abinadi answers the priests
chapterMaps.summary: Abinadi returns and warns again of judgment. The people take him to Noah. The priests question him about Isaiah. He challenges their conduct and teaching of God's commandments.

chapterMaps.title: Abinadi teaches the commandments
chapterMaps.summary: Noah orders Abinadi's death, but God's power protects him. Abinadi continues to teach the commandments. He says the law alone cannot save people. He points to the coming Redeemer.

chapterMaps.title: Isaiah's suffering servant
chapterMaps.summary: Abinadi quotes Isaiah's account of a suffering servant. The servant bears others' grief and sins. He suffers without answering his accusers. His death and offering benefit many.

chapterMaps.title: Abinadi explains Christ's redemption
chapterMaps.summary: Abinadi teaches that God will come to redeem his people. He describes Christ's suffering and victory over death. He identifies those who receive the first resurrection. He also speaks of messengers who publish peace.

chapterMaps.title: Resurrection and the final judgment
chapterMaps.summary: Abinadi warns that all people will face God. He explains how Christ overcomes death. People will rise to receive judgment for their works. He asks the priests to teach redemption through Christ.

chapterMaps.title: Abinadi dies and Alma believes
chapterMaps.summary: Alma, one of Noah's young priests, believes Abinadi and asks Noah to release him. Noah sends servants to kill Alma. Abinadi refuses to withdraw his testimony. He dies by fire after warning his killers.

chapterMaps.title: Alma gathers believers at Mormon
chapterMaps.summary: Alma secretly teaches Abinadi's words. Believers gather at Mormon, a place with a fountain of pure water. They receive baptism there. Alma organizes priests and teaches unity and care for others. The group flees after Noah discovers them.

chapterMaps.title: Noah falls and Limhi rules
chapterMaps.summary: Gideon, a strong man who opposes Noah, attacks the king as a Lamanite army arrives. Noah flees, leaving many families behind. His people later kill him by fire. Noah's son Limhi becomes king under a tribute agreement.

chapterMaps.title: An abduction brings another attack
chapterMaps.summary: Noah's former priests take Lamanite daughters from Shemlon, a nearby Lamanite land. The Lamanites blame Limhi's people and attack. Limhi learns the cause and spares their wounded king. The king returns with them and restores peace.

chapterMaps.title: Limhi's people seek deliverance
chapterMaps.summary: Limhi's people suffer under Lamanite control. Repeated attempts to fight free fail. They humble themselves and receive some relief. Ammon's arrival from Zarahemla gives them hope of escape.

chapterMaps.title: Limhi's people escape
chapterMaps.summary: Limhi and Ammon seek a way out of bondage. Gideon proposes getting the guards drunk. The people leave with their families, flocks, and records. They reach Zarahemla while their pursuers become lost.

chapterMaps.title: Alma's people settle in Helam
chapterMaps.summary: Alma and his believers flee from Noah's army. They settle in a land they call Helam. Alma refuses to become their king. A lost Lamanite army finds them and Noah's former priests. Amulon, the leader of those priests, gains authority over Alma's people.

chapterMaps.title: Alma's people leave bondage
chapterMaps.summary: Amulon burdens Alma's people and forbids their prayers. They pray silently, and the Lord strengthens them. The Lord causes their guards to sleep. They escape through the wilderness and reach Zarahemla.

chapterMaps.title: The communities join in Zarahemla
chapterMaps.summary: Mosiah gathers the people and reads the records of the returning groups. The people grieve and rejoice at what they hear. Alma teaches and baptizes Limhi's people. Churches are organized throughout the land.

chapterMaps.title: Alma seeks guidance about sin
chapterMaps.summary: Some younger people reject the church's teachings. Alma brings their cases to Mosiah, who returns them. Alma prays and receives instructions from the Lord. He teaches repentance and removes those who refuse it.

chapterMaps.title: Alma and Mosiah's sons change
chapterMaps.summary: Alma's son, also named Alma, works against the church. Four sons of King Mosiah join him. An angel stops them and calls the younger Alma to repent. He recovers after the people pray and describes his change. The men begin to repair the harm they caused.

chapterMaps.title: Mosiah's sons ask to preach
chapterMaps.summary: Mosiah's sons, Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni, ask to teach the Lamanites. The Lord tells Mosiah to let them go. Mosiah translates the records found by Limhi's people. He gives the younger Alma charge of the sacred records.

chapterMaps.title: Judges replace the kings
chapterMaps.summary: Mosiah explains the dangers of rule by a wicked king. He proposes judges chosen by the people. The people accept, and the younger Alma becomes chief judge. Mosiah and the elder Alma die.

chapterMaps.title: Nehor's teaching and trial
chapterMaps.summary: Nehor, a man who preaches for money, kills Gideon. Gideon is an old man who once helped free Limhi's people. Alma, the chief judge, judges Nehor under the law. Persecution continues after Nehor's death. Church members share their goods and care for the poor.

chapterMaps.title: Amlici's rebellion reaches the Sidon
chapterMaps.summary: Amlici, a follower of Nehor's ideas, wants to become king. The people reject him. His followers rebel and join a Lamanite army. Alma leads the Nephites in battles near Zarahemla and the river Sidon. The enemy retreats into Hermounts, a wilderness of wild beasts.

chapterMaps.title: The cost of rebellion
chapterMaps.summary: The Nephites bury their dead after the battles. The record describes the Amlicites' identifying marks. Another Lamanite attack follows. The chapter closes by linking each person's choices to their reward.

chapterMaps.title: Alma leaves the judgment seat
chapterMaps.summary: War leads many people to humble themselves. Later wealth brings pride and neglect of the poor. Alma sees that the church needs correction. He gives the judgment seat to Nephihah, a wise church elder. Alma then leaves to preach.

chapterMaps.title: Alma asks about changed hearts
chapterMaps.summary: Alma reminds Zarahemla's people of their fathers' deliverance. He asks whether their hearts have changed. He warns against pride, envy, and mistreatment of others. He calls both church members and others to repentance.

chapterMaps.title: Alma goes to Gideon
chapterMaps.summary: Alma puts the church in Zarahemla in order. Those who repent receive baptism. The people meet, fast, and pray for those outside the church. Alma crosses the river Sidon to teach in the land of Gideon.

chapterMaps.title: Alma teaches Gideon about Christ
chapterMaps.summary: Alma speaks to the people in Gideon. He foretells Christ's birth and suffering for his people. He asks them to repent and receive baptism. He urges faith, hope, charity, and care for God's commandments.

chapterMaps.title: Alma meets Amulek
chapterMaps.summary: Alma teaches in the land of Melek. He then goes north to the city of Ammonihah. The people reject him. An angel sends him back, and Amulek, a man of Ammonihah, welcomes him. The two men prepare to preach together.

chapterMaps.title: Alma warns Ammonihah
chapterMaps.summary: The people challenge Alma's authority and words. He recalls the Lord's help to their ancestors. Their knowledge makes their rejection especially serious. He warns of destruction and the coming Son of God.

chapterMaps.title: Amulek gives his witness
chapterMaps.summary: Amulek tells how an angel led him to welcome Alma. He confirms Alma's words. Lawyers try to trap him through questions. He warns that the prayers of the righteous preserve the city.

chapterMaps.title: Amulek answers Zeezrom
chapterMaps.summary: The record explains the judges' pay and money system. Zeezrom, a skilled lawyer in Ammonihah, offers Amulek money to deny God. Amulek refuses and teaches about Christ. He explains resurrection and judgment.

chapterMaps.title: Alma explains judgment and redemption
chapterMaps.summary: Alma exposes the purpose of Zeezrom's questions. He teaches about softened and hardened hearts. He describes judgment and the fall of Adam. He asks the people to repent and enter God's rest.

chapterMaps.title: Priests teach the way to God's rest
chapterMaps.summary: Alma explains the calling of priests. Their teaching points people toward the Son of God. He recalls Melchizedek, an ancient king of Salem. Melchizedek's people repented after he taught them. Alma urges his hearers to repent before the Lord comes.

chapterMaps.title: Believers suffer and the prison falls
chapterMaps.summary: The people cast out believing men and burn women, children, and scriptures. Alma and Amulek witness the deaths and suffer in prison. They pray for strength. The prison falls, and they escape.

chapterMaps.title: Zeezrom is healed in Sidom
chapterMaps.summary: Alma and Amulek find refugees in the land of Sidom. Zeezrom asks for healing and expresses faith in Christ. Alma heals him, and he receives baptism. Alma establishes the church and later takes Amulek home.

chapterMaps.title: Ammonihah falls and captives return
chapterMaps.summary: Lamanites destroy Ammonihah and take captives from nearby lands. Alma tells Zoram, the Nephite chief captain, where to find the enemy. The army recovers the captives near the Sidon. Alma and Amulek continue to teach throughout the land.

chapterMaps.title: Ammon serves in Ishmael
chapterMaps.summary: Alma meets Mosiah's sons after their mission. The account returns to their journey among the Lamanites. Ammon, one of Mosiah's sons, goes to the land of Ishmael. He becomes a servant of Lamoni, the Lamanite king there. He protects the king's flocks from attackers.

chapterMaps.title: Lamoni hears Ammon's teaching
chapterMaps.summary: Lamoni hears what Ammon did for his servants. He wonders whether Ammon is the Great Spirit. Ammon teaches him about God, creation, and redemption. Lamoni prays for mercy and falls to the earth.

chapterMaps.title: Lamoni's household awakens
chapterMaps.summary: Lamoni's wife asks Ammon about her husband. Lamoni awakens and testifies of the Redeemer. His household experiences God's power. Abish, a Lamanite servant who already believes, gathers the people. Many believe and receive baptism.

chapterMaps.title: Ammon helps free his brothers
chapterMaps.summary: Ammon and Lamoni travel toward Middoni to free Ammon's brother Aaron and his companions. They meet Lamoni's father, the king over all the Lamanite lands. He commands his son to kill Ammon. Ammon resists the king and spares his life. The king permits his son's freedom and the prisoners' release.

chapterMaps.title: Aaron teaches and suffers imprisonment
chapterMaps.summary: Aaron, Ammon's brother, teaches in a Lamanite city called Jerusalem. He then teaches in the village of Ani-Anti. Many reject his words. He and his companions suffer in prison in Middoni. After their release, they continue teaching while Ammon serves Lamoni's people.

chapterMaps.title: Aaron teaches the king; Mormon describes the lands
chapterMaps.summary: Aaron teaches Lamoni's father about God and redemption. The king prays and falls to the earth. Aaron raises him, and the household believes. Mormon, the editor of the record, then describes the lands. He names the seas, the wilderness, and the narrow neck.

contextNote.title: Why Mormon pauses to describe the land
contextNote.text: The king sends his message throughout his lands (verse 27). Mormon then explains their borders. The wilderness separates Nephi from Zarahemla. Bountiful guards the route north (verses 33–34). This geography explains the Nephites’ place of refuge.

chapterMaps.title: Converted communities take a new name
chapterMaps.summary: The king protects the missionaries throughout his lands. Many Lamanites believe and give up rebellion. The record names communities that accept the teaching. The converts take the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies.

chapterMaps.title: The people bury their weapons
chapterMaps.summary: Enemies prepare to attack the converted Lamanites. Their new king, Lamoni's brother, asks them to keep their promise against killing. They bury their weapons and refuse to fight. Many attackers repent after killing people who offer no resistance.

chapterMaps.title: War and further conversions
chapterMaps.summary: Lamanite armies attack the Nephites and destroy Ammonihah. Some descendants of Noah's priests suffer death. Many Lamanites later join the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Mosiah's sons rejoice in the mission's results.

chapterMaps.title: Ammon gives thanks for the mission
chapterMaps.summary: Ammon recalls the missionaries' hardships and the many converts. Aaron warns him against boasting. Ammon gives the credit to God's strength and mercy. He rejoices that God remembers every people.

chapterMaps.title: The people of Ammon receive Jershon
chapterMaps.summary: Renewed attacks threaten the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Ammon asks the Lord whether they should leave. The Nephites give them Jershon and provide protection. They become known as the people of Ammon.

chapterMaps.title: Loss and hope after battle
chapterMaps.summary: A great battle follows the settlement in Jershon. Many families mourn their dead. Some grieve without hope, while others trust God's promises. The record recalls the missionaries' work and its results.

chapterMaps.title: Alma rejoices in the work given to him
chapterMaps.summary: Alma wishes he could speak with an angel's power. He then accepts the work God has given him. He rejoices in the repentance of others. He also celebrates his companions' success among the Lamanites.

chapterMaps.title: Korihor challenges belief in Christ
chapterMaps.summary: Korihor, a man who preaches against Christ, comes to Zarahemla. He teaches that no Christ will come. The people of Gideon bind him. Their leaders send him to Alma, the high priest in Zarahemla. Korihor demands a sign and loses his ability to speak. He confesses his deception. He later dies among the Zoramites, a group of Nephite dissenters.

chapterMaps.title: Alma sees the Zoramites' worship
chapterMaps.summary: The Zoramites, Nephite dissenters led by a man named Zoram, live in Antionum. Alma leads companions there to teach them. They see the Zoramites repeat a prayer from a high stand. The prayer rejects Christ and claims special favor. Alma prays for strength and for the people's return.

chapterMaps.title: Alma compares faith to a seed
chapterMaps.summary: Poor Zoramites seek help after being excluded from their worship places. Alma teaches them about humility and faith. He asks them to test the word like a planted seed. Patient care can bring its fruit.

chapterMaps.title: Prayer and belief in the Son
chapterMaps.summary: The people ask how to worship and exercise faith. Alma recalls the prayers of Zenos, an ancient prophet, outside worship buildings. He cites prophets who testified of God's Son. He asks them to believe and nourish that word.

chapterMaps.title: Amulek teaches redemption and daily prayer
chapterMaps.summary: Amulek teaches that Christ's sacrifice brings redemption. He asks the people to pray in daily life. Prayer must go with care for those in need. He warns them against delaying repentance.

chapterMaps.title: The believers leave Antionum
chapterMaps.summary: The Zoramites expel those who believe the missionaries. The people of Ammon welcome them in Jershon. Threats follow, and the people of Ammon move to Melek. Alma gathers his sons to give each one counsel.

chapterMaps.title: Alma tells Helaman about his change
chapterMaps.summary: Alma asks his son Helaman to remember God's deliverance. He recalls his rebellion and the angel's visit. Calling on Jesus brings relief from his anguish. He spends his later life teaching others.

chapterMaps.title: Helaman receives the sacred records
chapterMaps.summary: Alma gives Helaman charge of the records. He explains how small means can accomplish great things. He warns against sharing the secret acts in the Jaredite record. He compares Christ's guidance to the family's guiding instrument.

chapterMaps.title: Alma counsels Shiblon
chapterMaps.summary: Alma praises his son Shiblon's faithfulness during the mission. He recalls his own deliverance through Christ. He tells Shiblon to avoid pride and control his desires. He sends him back to teach the people.

chapterMaps.title: Alma corrects Corianton
chapterMaps.summary: Alma rebukes his son Corianton for abandoning his mission. Corianton went after Isabel, a harlot among the Zoramites. His conduct has harmed the Zoramites' response to the teaching. Alma tells him to repent and repair his wrongs. He explains why they proclaim Christ before his coming.

chapterMaps.title: Alma answers questions about resurrection
chapterMaps.summary: Alma addresses Corianton's concern about the dead. He distinguishes the state of spirits from resurrection. God's power will reunite body and spirit. All will face judgment after they rise.

chapterMaps.title: Restoration follows people's choices
chapterMaps.summary: Alma explains restoration to Corianton. Resurrection restores the body, and judgment answers people's works and desires. Restoration does not turn wickedness into happiness. Alma urges mercy, justice, and good conduct.

chapterMaps.title: Alma explains justice and mercy
chapterMaps.summary: Corianton questions the punishment of sinners. Alma explains the fall, human choice, and repentance. Christ's sacrifice allows mercy without removing justice. Alma asks his son to repent and return to teaching.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni prepares an ambush near Manti
chapterMaps.summary: Zerahemnah, a Lamanite commander, leads an army against the Nephites. Moroni, the young chief captain of the Nephites, prepares defenses. These defenses cause the enemy to leave Antionum for Manti. Moroni places troops on both sides of the Sidon. The Nephites surround the enemy, and Moroni stops the killing.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni offers terms to Zerahemnah
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni asks the enemy to surrender its weapons and promise peace. Zerahemnah refuses the promise. Fighting resumes after he attacks Moroni. The survivors finally accept the terms and leave.

chapterMaps.title: Helaman receives counsel and teaches
chapterMaps.summary: Alma asks Helaman about his faith. He foretells the future destruction of the Nephites. Alma leaves and is not seen again. Helaman and his companions organize churches as pride spreads.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni opposes Amalickiah
chapterMaps.summary: Amalickiah, a Nephite dissenter, seeks to become king with support from other dissenters. Captain Moroni raises a written pledge of freedom and faith. The people covenant to defend those commitments. Amalickiah escapes while many of his followers return.

chapterMaps.title: Amalickiah takes the Lamanite throne
chapterMaps.summary: Amalickiah uses deception to control a Lamanite army. He arranges the death of Lehonti, a Lamanite leader. His servants kill the Lamanite king and blame others. Amalickiah marries the queen and becomes king.

chapterMaps.title: Preparations for another war
chapterMaps.summary: Amalickiah stirs the Lamanites against the Nephites. Moroni strengthens cities and places defenses at weak points. Mormon describes Moroni's faith and care for freedom. The Nephites prepare for war despite their desire for peace.

chapterMaps.title: The defenses hold at Ammonihah and Noah
chapterMaps.summary: Lamanite armies find Ammonihah strongly defended. They turn to the city of Noah and find defenses there too. Their attack fails with heavy losses. The Nephites give thanks and enjoy peace.

chapterMaps.title: New defenses and Morianton's flight
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni strengthens the frontier and establishes eastern cities. The people of two cities, Lehi and Morianton, dispute land. Morianton, their leader, takes his people toward the land northward. Teancum, a Nephite commander, stops them at the narrow pass. Pahoran, the son of Nephihah, later becomes chief judge.

contextNote.title: Why the narrow pass matters
contextNote.text: Morianton plans to take his followers north (verse 29). Moroni fears that Bountiful will join them (verse 32). Teancum reaches the pass before they can leave. The pass limits their escape, so both armies meet there.

chapterMaps.title: Division and an attack along the east coast
chapterMaps.summary: The king-men, who want a king, divide the Nephites. Moroni suppresses them as Amalickiah attacks eastern cities. The army reaches the borders near Bountiful. Teancum enters its camp and kills Amalickiah.

contextNote.title: Division opens the eastern front
contextNote.text: The king-men refuse to help defend the country (verse 13). Moroni must oppose them while Amalickiah advances. Cities along the east seashore fall before Teancum stops the army. The chapter joins internal division with danger at the borders.

chapterMaps.title: The Nephites retake Mulek
chapterMaps.summary: Ammoron, Amalickiah's brother, becomes the Lamanite king and continues the war. Moroni and Teancum plan to draw troops out of the city of Mulek. Teancum retreats toward Bountiful while other troops take the city. The pursuing Lamanites are surrounded and captured.

contextNote.title: Leaving the city removes its protection
contextNote.text: The Lamanites refuse to fight outside Mulek (verse 20). Teancum draws them toward Bountiful with a smaller force. Moroni takes the city while they pursue him. Their chase leaves them trapped between Nephite armies (verses 31–32).

chapterMaps.title: Helaman leads young men to war
chapterMaps.summary: Prisoners work on defenses near Bountiful. Trouble continues on the western front. The people of Ammon consider breaking their promise against fighting. Two thousand of their sons enlist instead. Helaman, Alma's son, becomes their leader.

chapterMaps.title: Letters about the prisoners
chapterMaps.summary: Ammoron proposes an exchange of prisoners. Moroni asks for Nephite families as well as soldiers. He demands that the invaders leave the land. Ammoron accepts the exchange terms but rejects Moroni's demands for peace.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni frees prisoners at Gid
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni refuses to proceed with the exchange. He sends wine to the guards at the city of Gid through a Lamanite servant. The prisoners receive weapons while the guards sleep. The Nephites take the city without killing the guards.

chapterMaps.title: Helaman reports the battle near Antiparah
chapterMaps.summary: Helaman writes to Moroni about the western war. His young soldiers join Antipus, a Nephite commander, at the city of Judea. They draw the enemy away from Antiparah. They fight after Antipus falls, and all Helaman's young men survive.

chapterMaps.title: Cumeni falls and the young soldiers stand
chapterMaps.summary: Helaman's army receives reinforcements and takes Cumeni. A large group of prisoners attempts to escape. Lamanites attack the Nephites while part of the army is away. Helaman's young soldiers hold firm, and none of them dies.

chapterMaps.title: Helaman retakes Manti
chapterMaps.summary: Helaman's army waits for supplies and men. They pray for strength and receive assurance. Gid and Teomner, two of Helaman's officers, hide near Manti. They take the city while Helaman draws its army away. Helaman ends his letter with concern about limited government support.

chapterMaps.title: Nephihah falls before help arrives
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni rejoices at Helaman's letter and asks for help. A growing Lamanite force attacks Nephihah. The city falls, and survivors flee to Moroni. He fears that the government has failed his armies.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni sends a sharp letter
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni writes to Pahoran, the chief judge. He accuses Pahoran and the government of neglecting the armies. He recalls the soldiers who have died without help. He demands supplies and troops. He threatens action if the government continues to refuse.

chapterMaps.title: Pahoran explains the rebellion
chapterMaps.summary: Pahoran tells Moroni that king-men have driven him from Zarahemla. He is gathering supporters in Gideon. He accepts Moroni's concern without anger. He asks Moroni to come and help restore the government.

chapterMaps.title: The government returns and the war ends
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni joins Pahoran and defeats the rebels in Zarahemla. The Nephites retake Nephihah and other eastern cities. Teancum kills Ammoron but dies during the attempt. Peace returns, and Helaman teaches until his death.

chapterMaps.title: Ships, migration, and the records
chapterMaps.summary: Shiblon, Helaman's brother, receives the records after Helaman's death. Many people move to the land northward. Hagoth, a ship builder, builds ships by the west sea. Shiblon later gives the records to Helaman's son, also named Helaman.

chapterMaps.title: A divided government leaves Zarahemla exposed
chapterMaps.summary: Three sons of Pahoran, the late chief judge, compete for the judgment seat. Kishkumen, a hired murderer, kills Pahoran's son, the chosen ruler. Coriantumr, a Nephite dissenter, leads a Lamanite army into Zarahemla. Moronihah, Captain Moroni's son, and Lehi, another captain, surround the invaders. They retake the city.

chapterMaps.title: A plot against Helaman fails
chapterMaps.summary: Helaman, the son of the earlier Helaman, becomes chief judge. Kishkumen plots to kill him with support from Gadianton, a leader of secret robbers. Helaman's servant discovers the plan and kills Kishkumen. Gadianton's group escapes into the wilderness.

chapterMaps.title: People move north and the church grows
chapterMaps.summary: Many people settle in the land northward. The record describes their building materials and records. The church gains many members during years of peace. Pride returns, and Helaman's son Nephi later becomes chief judge.

chapterMaps.title: The Nephites lose the land southward
chapterMaps.summary: Dissenters join the Lamanites in renewed war. The Nephites retreat to Bountiful and fortify a line. Moronihah recovers some land as prophets call the people to repent. The people recognize that their own sins have weakened them.

contextNote.title: A smaller country to defend
contextNote.text: The Nephites lose Zarahemla and retreat to Bountiful (verses 5–6). They fortify a line to defend their north country. Mormon connects their losses to injustice and pride (verses 11–12). Their later strength depends on repentance as well as defenses.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi and Lehi teach among the Lamanites
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi leaves the judgment seat to preach with his brother Lehi. They travel from Bountiful through Gid, Mulek, Zarahemla, and Nephi. God's power protects them in prison. Many Lamanites believe and return occupied lands.

chapterMaps.title: Peace gives way to secret violence
chapterMaps.summary: Lamanites and Nephites trade and travel in peace. Many Lamanites teach the Nephites. Murders and secret agreements then spread among the Nephites. The Lamanites oppose the robbers while Nephite leaders support them.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi mourns over Zarahemla
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi returns and finds corrupt leaders in power. He prays on his garden tower. A crowd gathers, and he calls them to repentance. He warns that rejection of God will bring destruction.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi announces the chief judge's murder
chapterMaps.summary: Corrupt judges challenge Nephi's warning. He recalls prophets who testified of Christ. He tells the crowd that their chief judge has been murdered. He identifies the judge's brother as the killer.

chapterMaps.title: The murderer's confession confirms Nephi's words
chapterMaps.summary: Men find the chief judge dead and are accused of murder. Nephi is also accused. He tells the judges how to question Seantum, the judge's brother. Seantum confesses, leaving the people divided about Nephi.

chapterMaps.title: Nephi receives power and returns to preach
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi walks home after the murder inquiry. The Lord praises his faithfulness and gives him sealing power. He returns to warn the people. They resist, and conflict increases.

chapterMaps.title: Famine interrupts the war
chapterMaps.summary: Nephi asks for famine to stop the people's fighting. Hunger leads them to repent and remove the robbers. He prays for rain, and the land recovers. Prosperity later gives way to new robber bands and growing pride.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon reflects on human forgetfulness
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon compares human pride with creation's obedience to God. People often forget the Lord when they prosper. The earth and its elements obey his command. Mormon closes with repentance, grace, and final judgment.

chapterMaps.title: Samuel warns from the city wall
chapterMaps.summary: Samuel, a Lamanite prophet, comes to preach in Zarahemla. The Nephites cast him out. He returns and speaks from the city wall. He warns of destruction unless the people repent. He condemns their love of riches and rejection of prophets. He asks them to seek mercy before it is too late.

chapterMaps.title: Samuel gives signs of Christ's birth and death
chapterMaps.summary: Samuel announces signs of Christ's birth in five years. He describes darkness and destruction at Christ's death. He teaches that Christ's death makes resurrection possible. He urges the people to choose repentance and life.

chapterMaps.title: Samuel contrasts two peoples' choices
chapterMaps.summary: Samuel warns the Nephites about their knowledge and rebellion. He describes Lamanites who now keep God's commandments. Their faith has led them to bury their weapons. He warns that unrepentant Nephites will face destruction.

chapterMaps.title: People accept or reject Samuel's warning
chapterMaps.summary: Some listeners seek baptism from Nephi. Others try to kill Samuel, who escapes. Signs and wonders increase. Many explain them away and continue in unbelief.

chapterMaps.title: The sign of Christ's birth
chapterMaps.summary: Unbelievers threaten those waiting for Samuel's promised sign. Nephi, the son of the earlier Nephi, prays for his people. The Lord promises that the sign will come. A night without darkness confirms Christ's birth. Belief spreads, but later dissent weakens some families.

chapterMaps.title: Unbelief returns and war spreads
chapterMaps.summary: The people begin to forget the signs. They count their years from Christ's birth. Robber bands threaten both Nephites and Lamanites. The two peoples join in defense, but divisions continue.

chapterMaps.title: Lachoneus gathers the people
chapterMaps.summary: Giddianhi, the robbers' leader, demands that Lachoneus surrender. Lachoneus, the Nephite governor, refuses and gathers his people with supplies and flocks. Gidgiddoni, the chief captain, prepares defenses between Zarahemla and Bountiful. The people repent and prepare to withstand an attack.

contextNote.title: Gathering changes the defense
contextNote.text: Lachoneus refuses the robbers’ demand and gathers his people. They bring food and flocks into one defended area (verses 13–14). Gidgiddoni rejects an attack in the wilderness (verse 21). The people prepare to wait for the robbers instead.

chapterMaps.title: The gathered people defeat the robbers
chapterMaps.summary: The robbers find the abandoned lands without food. Giddianhi attacks the gathered people and dies. Zemnarihah, the next robber leader, tries a siege and later retreats. The defenders capture him and give thanks for their deliverance.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon explains his record and purpose
chapterMaps.summary: The people repent after the robbers' defeat. Prisoners receive a chance to leave their former ways. Mormon explains his work in preserving the records. He looks toward Israel's gathering through Jesus Christ.

chapterMaps.title: Peace breaks under pride and secret plots
chapterMaps.summary: The people return to their lands and rebuild. Wealth and rank divide them. Some judges secretly kill people who testify of Christ. Their allies plot to destroy the governor and establish a king.

chapterMaps.title: The government falls into tribal rule
chapterMaps.summary: The governor's murder destroys the central government. Families divide into tribes. Jacob, a leader of the secret plotters, takes his group northward and becomes its king. Nephi teaches with power, and many receive baptism.

chapterMaps.title: Storm, destruction, and darkness
chapterMaps.summary: The people await the sign of Christ's death. A great storm destroys cities, roads, and land. Zarahemla burns, and the city of Moroni sinks into the sea. Earth covers the city of Moronihah. Darkness follows, and survivors mourn their refusal to repent.

impacts.text: The great city Zarahemla caught fire.
The city of Moroni sank into the sea.
Earth was carried on the city of Moronihah.

chapterMaps.title: Christ calls the survivors to return
chapterMaps.summary: A voice names cities destroyed for their wickedness. The speaker identifies himself as Jesus Christ. He invites the survivors to come to him and receive healing. He asks for a broken heart and a repentant spirit.

impacts.text: The Lord burned the great city Zarahemla.
The Lord sank the great city Moroni.
The Lord covered the city Moronihah with earth.
The Lord sank the city of Gilgal.
Waters came up in the place of Onihah.
Waters came up in the place of Mocum.
Waters came up in the place of Jerusalem.
The Lord sank Gadiandi in the earth.
The Lord sank Gadiomnah in the earth.
The Lord sank Gimgimno in the earth.
The Lord burned the city of Laman.
The Lord burned the city of Josh.
The Lord burned the city of Gad.
The Lord burned the city of Kishkumen.

chapterMaps.title: The darkness ends
chapterMaps.summary: Silence follows Christ's words. He calls the people to gather as children under his protection. The darkness lifts and the earth becomes still. Mormon prepares to describe the Savior's ministry to the survivors.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus appears at Bountiful
chapterMaps.summary: People gather near the temple in Bountiful. The Father introduces his Son, and Jesus descends. The people touch his wounds and witness his resurrection. He calls disciples and teaches baptism without dispute.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus teaches his people how to live
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus blesses those who receive his disciples and believe. He teaches about humility, mercy, and peace. He calls the people to reject anger and unfaithfulness. He asks them to love their enemies and follow God's example.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus teaches private worship and trust
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus warns against giving, praying, or fasting to gain praise. He gives a pattern for prayer. He teaches forgiveness and treasure in heaven. He asks his chosen disciples to trust the Father's care.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus teaches judgment and a firm foundation
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus warns against judging others while ignoring one's own faults. He tells the people to ask God and treat others well. He warns about false prophets. He compares obedient hearers to a house built on rock.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus explains the law and his other sheep
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus says that he has fulfilled the law of Moses. God's remaining promises will still be fulfilled. He identifies this people as other sheep he mentioned in Jerusalem. They have heard his voice and belong to his flock.

chapterMaps.title: Other peoples and Israel's gathering
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus speaks of still other sheep who will hear him. He describes the Gentiles receiving his gospel. He warns that unbelief can cost them that blessing. He promises to remember his covenant with Israel.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus heals and blesses the children
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus tells the people to ponder and prepare for more teaching. Seeing their desire, he stays to heal the sick. He prays for them and blesses their children. Angels gather around the children in fire.

chapterMaps.title: Bread, wine, and prayer
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus gives the people bread and wine. He teaches them to remember him and obey his commandments. He tells them to pray together and welcome others. He gives further instructions to the disciples before departing.

chapterMaps.title: The people pray as Jesus returns
chapterMaps.summary: The people gather again with the twelve disciples. The disciples teach, baptize, and pray for the Holy Ghost. Jesus returns and prays to the Father. He rejoices in the people's faith.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus speaks about the covenant with Israel
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus again gives the people bread and wine. He teaches about Israel's gathering and the promised land. He identifies them as children of the covenant. He quotes promises about Jerusalem's redemption.

chapterMaps.title: A record becomes a sign of gathering
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus gives a sign of Israel's coming gathering. His words will reach the descendants of this people through the Gentiles. He warns the unrepentant and promises help to believers. He describes a New Jerusalem and God's work among all nations.

chapterMaps.title: The Lord promises peace to his people
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus quotes Isaiah's promise to a once-desolate people. They are told to enlarge their tent for returning children. The Lord promises lasting kindness and a covenant of peace. He promises protection against their enemies.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus asks that the records be complete
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus commands the people to study Isaiah. He examines their records with Nephi. The record lacks a prophecy from Samuel the Lamanite about people rising from the dead. Jesus tells them to add it and teaches from the scriptures.

chapterMaps.title: Malachi's words about return and judgment
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus gives the people words from Malachi, an ancient prophet of Israel. The Lord will come and cleanse his servants. He calls the people to return and bring their tithes. A record preserves those who fear and remember him.

chapterMaps.title: Malachi's words about the coming day
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus continues Malachi's words. A coming day will burn up the wicked. Those who fear the Lord will receive healing. Elijah, an ancient prophet, will come to turn the hearts of parents and children.

chapterMaps.title: Teaching continues beyond the written account
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus explains the scriptures and events from beginning to end. Mormon includes only part of that teaching. Children speak remarkable things after Jesus teaches them. The disciples baptize, and the people share their goods.

chapterMaps.title: Jesus names his church and teaches his gospel
chapterMaps.summary: The disciples ask Jesus what to call the church. He tells them to use his name. He teaches his death, resurrection, repentance, and judgment. He asks them to follow his example and keep records.

chapterMaps.title: Three disciples ask to continue their ministry
chapterMaps.summary: Jesus asks the disciples what they desire. Nine ask to come to him after their lives. Three ask to remain and bring people to him. Mormon describes their changed condition and protected ministry.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon warns future readers
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon addresses those who will receive the record. Its arrival shows that the Lord remembers his covenant. He warns against rejecting Christ and his gifts. He also warns against mistreating Israel.

chapterMaps.title: A call to the Gentiles
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon records Christ's words to the Gentiles. They must turn from their sins and repent. Christ calls them to receive baptism and the Holy Ghost. They can then be numbered with his people.

chapterMaps.title: Unity gives way to division
chapterMaps.summary: The people live together in faith after Christ's visit. They share their goods and have no disputes. Later pride, separate churches, and old divisions return. Ammaron, a record keeper, hides the sacred records as wickedness spreads.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon's childhood and the coming war
chapterMaps.summary: Ammaron tells Mormon, a boy of about ten, where to find the records. Mormon travels with his father to Zarahemla. War begins near the Sidon. Mormon knows the Lord but cannot teach a people who reject repentance.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon leads a people in retreat
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon becomes commander while still young. His army loses cities and retreats through Joshua, Jashon, and Shem. Their sorrow does not lead to true repentance. A treaty gives the Nephites the land northward.

contextNote.title: A border after repeated retreats
contextNote.text: The army loses cities before reaching Jashon and Shem (verses 16–21). Mormon strengthens the people enough to recover land. A treaty then divides the country at the narrow passage. The agreed border ends this chapter’s fighting but leaves the peoples apart.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon refuses a war of revenge
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon strengthens defenses at Desolation and the narrow pass. The Nephites repel attacks but boast and vow revenge. Mormon refuses to lead them in that purpose. He turns to warning the future readers of his record.

chapterMaps.title: The Nephites lose Desolation and Boaz
chapterMaps.summary: The Nephites attack the Lamanites and are driven back. Desolation and Teancum change hands in repeated battles. Cruelty increases as the Nephites retreat to Boaz. Mormon retrieves the records from the hill Shim before the land falls.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon returns to lead the retreat
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon agrees to lead the Nephites again. They hold Jordan for a time, then flee. Mormon describes the record's future purpose for their descendants. He also calls the Gentiles to repentance.

chapterMaps.title: The last battle at Cumorah
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon gathers his people in the land of Cumorah. He hides most records in the hill Cumorah. He gives some plates to his son Moroni. A great battle destroys the Nephite armies. Mormon mourns the people who would not repent.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon's message to the survivors' descendants
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon asks future descendants of his people to know their identity. He calls them to repent and lay down weapons. He testifies of Christ's resurrection and judgment. He asks them to believe the record and the Bible.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni continues his father's record
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni, Mormon's son, describes his father's death and his own isolation. He writes about the record's future appearance. He warns those who oppose God's work. He also condemns future readers' pride and neglect of the poor.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni addresses those who doubt
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni asks unbelievers to prepare for God's presence. He testifies of creation, redemption, and resurrection. He defends miracles and the power of faith. He asks readers to allow for the record's human weaknesses.

chapterMaps.title: Jared's brother prays for his people
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni, Mormon's son, begins a short form of the Jaredite record. The Jaredites are an earlier people from the time of the great tower. Moroni first traces the family line of Ether, their last prophet. Jared asks his brother to pray during the confusion of languages. The Lord preserves their language. He promises to lead their families to a chosen land.

chapterMaps.title: The Jaredites prepare to cross the sea
chapterMaps.summary: The Lord leads the families through the wilderness to the sea. They later build vessels for the crossing. Jared's brother asks about air, steering, and light. The Lord explains the dangers and asks him to consider the light.

chapterMaps.title: Jared's brother sees the Lord
chapterMaps.summary: Jared's brother brings sixteen stones and asks the Lord to give them light. He sees the Lord's finger and then the Lord himself. The Lord shows him a great vision. He must preserve and seal the account with interpreters.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni writes about the sealed vision
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni explains why Jared's brother's vision remained hidden. He records the Lord's words about receiving that knowledge. Belief and repentance open the way to further revelation. The Lord invites readers to come to him.

chapterMaps.title: Instructions for the future translator
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni addresses the person who will translate the record. He forbids translation of the sealed portion. Three witnesses will see the plates through God's power. Their witness will stand with God's testimony.

chapterMaps.title: The voyage and the first king
chapterMaps.summary: The families cross the sea in their vessels. They give thanks when they reach the promised land. They farm and raise families. Orihah, a son of Jared, becomes king. Jared's brother had warned against kings.

chapterMaps.title: Rival rulers and prophetic warnings
chapterMaps.summary: Orihah's descendants fight for power. Corihor rebels against his father, King Kib, and takes him captive. Kib's son Shule restores him. Later rebellions divide the kingdom again. Shule protects prophets and calls the people to repentance.

chapterMaps.title: A secret agreement threatens Omer
chapterMaps.summary: Jared, a later king's son, rebels against his father, King Omer. Jared's daughter proposes a plot that involves Akish, a friend of Omer. The conspirators swear secret promises of loyalty and murder. Moroni warns future readers about such agreements.

chapterMaps.title: Omer escapes and later kings face famine
chapterMaps.summary: The Lord warns Omer, who leaves for a place called Ablom. Akish's rule collapses through family conflict and war. Later kings bring prosperity. Then Heth, a king's son, turns against the prophets. Famine ends after the people humble themselves.

contextNote.title: Omer leaves the struggle for power
contextNote.text: The Lord warns Omer to leave his land (verse 3). His journey passes Shim and Cumorah before reaching Ablom. He takes his family away from the plot against him. Akish’s household later destroys itself through rivalry (verses 7–12).

chapterMaps.title: Rulers, work, and renewed violence
chapterMaps.summary: Shez, a son of Heth, rebuilds the people after famine. Later rulers vary in justice and oppression. The record describes farming, trade, tools, and work under King Lib. Secret robbers return despite King Com's efforts against them.

chapterMaps.title: Prophets warn of the people's end
chapterMaps.summary: Prophets repeatedly warn the Jaredites to repent. Many rulers and people reject them. Wars, captivity, and political changes continue. The record's family line reaches Ether.

chapterMaps.title: Ether teaches faith; Moroni writes about weakness
chapterMaps.summary: Ether, a Jaredite prophet, calls the people to believe in God. Moroni recalls examples of faith and divine power. He worries that his writing is weak. The Lord teaches about humility, grace, and strength through weakness.

chapterMaps.title: Ether warns Coriantumr
chapterMaps.summary: Ether speaks about Jerusalem and a future New Jerusalem. He warns Coriantumr, the Jaredite king, that repentance can preserve his household and people. Coriantumr rejects the warning. Rival armies fight as Ether watches from hiding.

chapterMaps.title: The war spreads across the land
chapterMaps.summary: Coriantumr fights repeated battles against rival leaders. Shiz, the brother of a rival named Lib, takes command after Lib dies. Both armies leave cities and families destroyed. The struggle continues toward the eastern waters.

chapterMaps.title: The Jaredites gather for their final battle
chapterMaps.summary: Coriantumr remembers Ether's warning and seeks peace, but Shiz refuses. The armies move from the waters of Ripliancum toward Ogath and Ramah. They gather the remaining people for battle. Coriantumr kills Shiz after their armies are destroyed.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni writes while in hiding
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni, the son of Mormon, is the last Nephite record keeper. He had expected to finish his record. He hides from the Lamanites, who kill every Nephite who will not deny Christ. Moroni refuses to deny Christ. He writes more for the future benefit of the Lamanites, his brethren.

chapterMaps.title: Christ gives the disciples authority
