chapterMaps.summary: Moroni records words spoken privately to the twelve disciples. Jesus tells them to pray in his name. He gives them authority to confer the Holy Ghost. They use that authority by laying on hands.

chapterMaps.title: The church appoints priests and teachers
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni describes how elders appoint priests and teachers. They first pray to the Father in Christ's name. They lay hands on those appointed. The charge is to preach repentance and forgiveness through Christ.

chapterMaps.title: The prayer over the bread
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni records the prayer used over the sacramental bread. Elders and priests kneel with the church. The prayer asks the Father to bless the bread in Christ's name. It joins remembrance and obedience with the promise of his Spirit.

chapterMaps.title: The prayer over the wine
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni records the prayer used over the sacramental wine. The prayer asks the Father to bless it in Christ's name. Those who drink witness that they remember Christ's blood. The prayer asks that his Spirit remain with them.

chapterMaps.title: Baptism and care within the church
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni describes repentance required before baptism. The church records and nourishes new members. The people meet to pray, fast, and remember Christ. They offer forgiveness and conduct their meetings through the Spirit.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon teaches faith, hope, and charity
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni records a sermon from his father, Mormon, to peaceful followers of Christ. Mormon explains how to distinguish good from evil. He teaches faith in Christ and hope through his resurrection. He asks the people to pray for charity, Christ's pure love.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon writes about little children
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon answers a dispute about baptizing little children. He says that Christ's mercy makes them whole. Repentance and baptism are for those accountable for sin. He warns against false teaching and asks Moroni to continue his work.

chapterMaps.title: Mormon reports cruelty and asks Moroni to endure
chapterMaps.summary: Mormon describes terrible acts committed by both armies. His people reject his calls to repent. He asks Moroni to preserve the records if he survives. He urges him to find hope in Christ despite their suffering.

chapterMaps.title: Moroni's final invitation
chapterMaps.summary: Moroni asks readers to remember God's mercy and pray about the record. He describes spiritual gifts that come from Christ. He calls all people to come to Christ and receive his grace. He closes with hope of meeting them before God.

guides.title: Sorenson’s 17 maps
guides.description: Step through each numbered map in Mormon’s Map. Each step opens the chapter he uses.

steps.title: Map 1. Overall shape
steps.text: Sorenson begins with Alma 22:32. The land southward is nearly surrounded by water. A small neck joins it to the land northward. The result looks like an hourglass. Both far ends stay unknown.

steps.title: Map 2. Chief ethnic areas
steps.text: In Alma’s time, Lamanites held Nephi and both coasts. Nephites held the Sidon basin and Bountiful. The Jaredites were already gone. Sorenson says the Nephites sat like a cork in a bottle.

steps.title: Map 3. Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
steps.text: Amalickiah drove up the east coast toward the narrow neck. Sorenson shows his army staying near the shore. The text names Nephihah and Gid among the cities taken.

steps.title: Map 4. Teancum intercepts Morianton
steps.text: Morianton fled toward the land northward. Teancum knew he must use the narrow pass. Teancum took another road and got there first.

steps.title: Map 5. Lamanites go “round about”
steps.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and circled through the wilderness to Manti. The trip took long enough for Moroni to set a trap.

steps.title: Map 6. Some Jaredite locations
steps.text: Omer went from Moron past Shim and Cumorah to Ablom by the sea. Sorenson links these Jaredite places to the Nephite map. Higher land lay to the west.

steps.title: Map 7. Limhi’s explorers
steps.text: The explorers missed Zarahemla and kept going north. They found Ether’s plates near Ramah. Sorenson uses this trip to estimate the size of the land.

steps.title: Map 8. The Amlicite conflict
steps.text: All these moves took place in about 36 hours. So the area around Zarahemla covered only tens of miles.

steps.title: Map 9. Alma’s preaching circuit
steps.text: Alma taught in Gideon, Melek, Ammonihah, and Sidom. Sorenson thinks he circled the Sidon basin, where most Nephites lived.

steps.title: Map 10. Four cities across the land southward
steps.text: Moroni, Nephihah, Aaron, and Ammonihah touch one another in the text. Placed side by side, the land is about 200 miles wide.

steps.title: Map 11. The flight of Alma’s and Limhi’s peoples
steps.text: These two escapes give the best clues to the distance from Nephi to Zarahemla. The online PDF copy is missing this map’s page. The steps here follow Sorenson’s text.

steps.title: Map 12. Early spread of major groups
steps.text: The early groups stayed small and apart. Sorenson compares them to islands in a sea of wilderness.

steps.title: Map 13. Expansion in the time of the two Almas
steps.text: By about 50 BC, the Lamanite king ruled from sea to sea. Nephites filled the Sidon basin and moved into Bountiful.

steps.title: Map 14. Nephite expansion into the land northward
steps.text: Hagoth built a few ships. Sorenson thinks most settlers went north overland through the land Desolation.

steps.title: Map 15. Possible places of the destroyed cities
steps.text: A few destroyed cities have known places. Sorenson sorts the rest by the order of the list. Many points here are guesses.

steps.title: Map 16. Final flight from the land southward
steps.text: The Nephites left Zarahemla through Angola and David. They held Joshua by the west sea for years.

steps.title: Map 17. Final wars in the land northward
steps.text: The last Nephite wars stayed near the narrow neck. They were in the same area as the last Jaredite wars.

guides.title: Mormon’s own summary
guides.description: Read Alma 22:27–34 one part at a time. Mormon wrote this short aside about the land.

steps.title: The Lamanite king’s land
steps.text: The king ruled from sea to sea. A narrow strip of wilderness divided his land from Zarahemla. It ran by the head of Sidon.

steps.title: Lamanites along both coasts
steps.text: Lamanites also lived in the west wilderness and by the east seashore. So the Nephites were nearly surrounded.

steps.title: Bountiful and Desolation
steps.text: Bountiful bordered Desolation. Desolation held the bones of a destroyed people. The people of Zarahemla first landed there.

steps.title: A day and a half across
steps.text: A Nephite could cross this line in a day and a half. Water nearly surrounded Nephi and Zarahemla.

steps.title: Why hold the north
steps.text: The Nephites hemmed the Lamanites in on the south. They kept a country to flee to in the north.

terrain.name: Highlands of Nephi
terrain.summary: The land of Nephi was high country. People went up to it and down from it.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson reads every up and down as a change in elevation. Nephi stays above Zarahemla in dozens of passages.

terrain.name: Narrow strip of wilderness
terrain.summary: A strip of rugged wilderness ran from the east sea to the west sea. It divided the land of Nephi from Zarahemla.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson sees a band of mountains here. The head of the river Sidon lay inside it.

terrain.name: Western mountains
terrain.summary: Wilderness bounded the land of Zarahemla on the west. Melek lay by that wilderness.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson places a high range here. It shielded Melek, and armies crossed it only at two passes.

terrain.name: Western mountains
terrain.summary: The west wilderness continued north toward the land Bountiful.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson continues the western range north of the pass near Ammonihah.

terrain.name: Western mountains
terrain.summary: Wilderness also ran along the west in the land of Nephi.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson shows the same range south of the narrow strip of wilderness.

terrain.name: East wilderness upland
terrain.summary: Travelers went over a height to reach Gideon, Jershon, or the east lowlands.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson puts a wide, rugged upland east of the Sidon. Armies went around it, not through it.

terrain.name: Highlands of the land northward
terrain.summary: In the book of Ether, people go up to Moron. Other lands lay lower.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson puts the high country toward the west sea. Waters drained east toward Cumorah.

terrain.name: Highlands of the land northward
terrain.summary: The land of Moron was the Jaredite seat of rule.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson treats Moron as an upland area near the land Desolation.

terrain.name: Hill country by the east sea
terrain.summary: The hills Shim and Cumorah stood in the land northward near the east sea.
terrain.sorenson: Sorenson names hills but no mountains here. The hills sat in low, wet country.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Jerusalem was the capital of Judah. Lehi lived there until the Lord told him to leave.

refs.note: Lehi had lived at Jerusalem all his days.
Nephi and his brothers went up to the land of Jerusalem.

places.name: Borders near the Red Sea
places.summary: Lehi came down to the borders near the Red Sea. The text names no town there.

refs.note: Lehi came down by the borders near the shore of the Red Sea.

research.text: Researchers place this at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba. It is the arm of the Red Sea nearest Jerusalem.

places.name: Valley of Lemuel
places.summary: Lehi camped in a valley beside a river. He named the valley Lemuel and the river Laman.

refs.note: Lehi traveled three days and pitched his tent in a valley by a river.
He named the river Laman. It emptied into the Red Sea.
These things happened while Lehi lived in the valley of Lemuel.

research.text: George Potter proposed Wadi Tayyib al-Ism in northwest Arabia. A stream runs there through a deep canyon toward the sea.

places.name: Shazer
places.summary: The family camped at Shazer after four days of travel. They hunted there with bows.

refs.note: They traveled four days, nearly south-southeast, and named the place Shazer.

places.name: Nahom
places.summary: Ishmael died and was buried at a place called Nahom. His daughters mourned there.

refs.note: Ishmael was buried in the place which was called Nahom.

research.text: The Nihm tribal land lies northeast of Sanaa in Yemen. Altars near Marib carry the name NHM from about Lehi’s time.

places.name: Bountiful (Arabian coast)
places.summary: The family reached a coast with much fruit and wild honey. They called it Bountiful.

refs.note: They came to the land they called Bountiful, by the sea.
The Lord told Nephi to build a ship there.

research.text: Researchers propose green inlets on the Dhofar coast of Oman. Khor Kharfot and Khor Rori are the main candidates.

places.name: Zarahemla
places.summary: Zarahemla was the main Nephite city. It stood on the west bank of the river Sidon.

refs.note: Mosiah’s people came down from Nephi into Zarahemla.
The river Sidon ran by the land of Zarahemla.
Moroni calls the leaders in Zarahemla secure in the heart of the country.
The burned city was built again.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Zarahemla in a river basin, about 180 miles from Nephi. The land below it reached about 100 miles downstream.

places.name: Gideon
places.summary: Gideon was a city in a valley east of the river Sidon.

refs.note: Alma went over to the east of the Sidon, into the valley of Gideon.
The Nephite army camped in the valley of Gideon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Gideon about a day east of Zarahemla, in the east upland. The usual road to Manti went through it.

places.name: Hill Amnihu
places.summary: Amnihu was a hill east of the river Sidon, near Zarahemla.

refs.note: The Amlicites came to the hill Amnihu, east of the river Sidon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places the hill just across the river from the city.

places.name: Battle at the river crossing
places.summary: The Nephites fought the Lamanites and Amlicites while crossing the Sidon.

refs.note: The enemy came on them as they crossed the river Sidon.
Alma cleared the west bank of the river.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the crossing a few miles above the city. It was less than ten miles from Zarahemla.

places.name: Wilderness of Hermounts
places.summary: Hermounts was wild country west and north of the Nephite lands near Zarahemla.

refs.note: The enemy fled west and north into the wilderness called Hermounts.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates the battle scene was about ten miles from this wilderness.

places.name: Minon
places.summary: Minon was a land up the river from Zarahemla, toward the land of Nephi.

refs.note: Spies saw a Lamanite army in Minon, above Zarahemla, toward Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Minon no more than 35 miles from Zarahemla.

places.name: Manti
places.summary: Manti was the southern Nephite city on the upper river Sidon.

refs.note: The Lamanites crossed the river Sidon in the south wilderness, near Manti.
Moroni’s west-side army extended down into the borders of Manti.
The Lamanites marched around to come into the land of Manti.
Helaman’s army camped by the wilderness near the city of Manti.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Manti was about 75 miles upstream from Zarahemla.

places.name: Head of the river Sidon
places.summary: The river Sidon began in the wilderness south of Manti.

refs.note: The narrow strip of wilderness ran round about by the head of Sidon.
Lamanites went round about by the head of the river Sidon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the headwaters in the mountain band between Zarahemla and Nephi.

places.name: Melek
places.summary: Melek lay west of the river Sidon, by the western wilderness.

refs.note: Melek was on the west of the river Sidon, by the borders of the wilderness.
The people of Ammon moved to Melek.
Alma left as if to go to Melek and was not seen again.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Melek two or three days from Zarahemla. He says mountains on the west kept it safe.

places.name: Ammonihah
places.summary: Ammonihah was a city three days’ journey north of Melek.

refs.note: Alma traveled three days’ journey north of Melek to Ammonihah.
Lamanite armies came in on the wilderness side and destroyed it.
Lamanite armies were seen coming toward Ammonihah again.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Ammonihah near a pass through the western mountains. He thinks Lamanites crossed there from the coast.

places.name: Noah
places.summary: Noah was a Nephite city near Ammonihah.

refs.note: Lamanites destroyed Ammonihah and some around the borders of Noah.
The Lamanites marched toward the land of Noah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Noah near the western wilderness, between Melek and Ammonihah.

places.name: Sidom
places.summary: Sidom was a land where people cast out of Ammonihah found refuge.

refs.note: Alma and Amulek went to the land of Sidom.
From Sidom, Alma came over to the land of Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Sidom was on the river because of its name. The word “over” suggests an upland route home.

places.name: Aaron
places.summary: Aaron was a city that bordered both Ammonihah’s region and Nephihah.

refs.note: Alma started toward the city of Aaron.
Nephihah lay between the land of Moroni and the land of Aaron.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Aaron ruled a large, thinly settled area. That explains its links to both coasts.

places.name: Pass near Ammonihah
places.summary: Armies from the west coast came in on the wilderness side to reach Ammonihah.

refs.note: The Lamanites came in upon the wilderness side.
They went over to the land of Ammonihah.
Mormon’s army moved to Joshua, by the west seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson infers a mountain pass here. Mormon later held it for fourteen years from Joshua.

places.name: Joshua
places.summary: Joshua was a land in the borders west by the seashore.

refs.note: Joshua was in the borders west by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says this was the first named Nephite land on the west coast.

places.name: David
places.summary: David was a land the Nephites lost in their retreat from Zarahemla.

refs.note: The Lamanites drove the Nephites out of the land of David.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows David on the road from Zarahemla to the western pass.

places.name: Angola
places.summary: Angola was a city Mormon’s army fortified and then lost.

refs.note: Mormon’s army took and fortified the city of Angola.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Angola northwest of Zarahemla, near David.

places.name: Judea
places.summary: Judea was a Nephite city on the southwest front.

refs.note: Helaman marched his young men to the city of Judea.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Judea west of the Sidon, in the southwest part of the land.

places.name: Cumeni
places.summary: Cumeni was a city on the southwest front.

refs.note: Cumeni was one of the cities the Lamanites had taken.
Helaman’s army besieged the city of Cumeni.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Cumeni on the climb toward the western pass.

places.name: Zeezrom
places.summary: Zeezrom was a city on the southwest front.

refs.note: Zeezrom was one of the cities the Lamanites had taken.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Zeezrom between Judea and Antiparah.

places.name: Antiparah
places.summary: Antiparah was a strong Lamanite-held city in the southwest.

refs.note: Antiparah was one of the cities the Lamanites held.
Helaman marched near Antiparah toward a city by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Antiparah at or near the top of a southern pass. The road then fell to the coast.

places.name: Southern pass
places.summary: A road led past Antiparah to a city in the borders by the seashore.

refs.note: The city beyond was in the borders by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson infers a second pass through the western mountains here.

places.name: City by the seashore
places.summary: Helaman named a city beyond Antiparah, in the borders by the seashore.

refs.note: Helaman marched as if going to the city beyond, by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places this unnamed city below the southern pass, on the west coast.

places.name: Bountiful
places.summary: Bountiful was the land and city at the north end of the land southward.

refs.note: Bountiful bordered the land called Desolation.
The Lamanites chased Teancum until they came near the city Bountiful.
People gathered at the temple in the land Bountiful.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places the city near the beach, at about sea level. He estimates it was about 12 miles from Mulek.

places.name: Jershon
places.summary: Jershon was a land by the east sea, south of the land Bountiful.

refs.note: Jershon was on the east by the sea and joined the land Bountiful.
The Lamanites did not dare attack the Nephites in Jershon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson keeps Jershon inland of the coastal road. He says Amalickiah’s drive passed it by.

places.name: Mulek
places.summary: Mulek was a city on the east borders by the seashore.

refs.note: Mulek was among the cities on the east borders by the seashore.
Moroni took the city Mulek.
Nephi and Lehi preached at Mulek.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the people of Zarahemla first settled near here. He puts Mulek about 12 miles from Bountiful.

places.name: Gid
places.summary: Gid was a city in the east borders, near Mulek.

refs.note: Gid was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.
Nephi and Lehi went from Bountiful to Gid.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Gid straight inland from Mulek. Both were the same distance from Bountiful.

places.name: Omner
places.summary: Omner was a city on the east coast.

refs.note: Omner was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Omner was about 20 miles south of Mulek along the shore.

places.name: Morianton
places.summary: Morianton was a city in the east borders, next to the land of Lehi.

refs.note: The people of Morianton disputed land with the people of Lehi.
Morianton was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Morianton a little inland from the beach road.

places.name: Lehi
places.summary: Lehi was a city in the east borders near Morianton.

refs.note: The Nephites built the city of Lehi in the north, by the seashore.
Lehi was among the cities taken by Amalickiah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Lehi near the coast, north of Moroni.

places.name: Moroni
places.summary: The city of Moroni stood by the east sea, near the Lamanite border.

refs.note: The city of Moroni was by the east sea, near the Lamanite lands.
Amalickiah began by taking the city of Moroni.
The city of Moroni sank into the depths of the sea.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the edge of Nephite land here. It was only about 80 miles from the neck.

places.name: Nephihah
places.summary: Nephihah was a city between the land of Moroni and the land of Aaron.

refs.note: Nephihah lay between the land of Moroni and the land of Aaron.
The text names Nephihah first among the cities taken.
Moroni recaptured the city of Nephihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson shows Nephihah inland from the shore. His map 3 shows Amalickiah passing it by.

places.name: Antionum
places.summary: Antionum was the Zoramite land near the east seashore.

refs.note: Antionum lay east of Zarahemla, nearly bordering the seashore, south of Jershon.
The Lamanites left Antionum to go round about in the wilderness.

sorenson.text: Sorenson calls Antionum the enemy base nearest the narrow neck.

places.name: Siron
places.summary: Siron was a land among the borders of the Lamanites.

refs.note: Corianton went to the land of Siron, among the Lamanite borders.

sorenson.text: Sorenson gives no position for Siron. The map puts it near Antionum only because Alma 39 follows that mission.

places.name: Nephi (Lehi-Nephi)
places.summary: Nephi was the first Nephite city in the promised land. Later it was the Lamanite king’s city.

refs.note: Nephi’s people called the place Nephi.
Mosiah fled out of the land of Nephi.
The king of the Lamanites lived in the land of Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates about 22 days of foot travel to Zarahemla. That is about 180 miles in a straight line.

places.name: Shilom
places.summary: Shilom was a land next to Nephi. Zeniff’s people lived there too.

refs.note: Zeniff’s people repaired the walls of Lehi-Nephi and Shilom.
Noah’s tower overlooked Shilom and Shemlon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Shilom was within about ten miles of Nephi.

places.name: Shemlon
places.summary: Shemlon was a Lamanite land below Nephi.

refs.note: Noah’s tower overlooked Shemlon.
Noah looked toward Shemlon and saw a Lamanite army in the borders.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the near edge of Shemlon within about 20 miles of Nephi.

places.name: Place of Mormon
places.summary: Mormon was a place with a fountain of pure water, near the borders of Nephi.

refs.note: Mormon was in the borders of the land.
The place, the waters, and the forest of Mormon are named together.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Mormon was one to three days from the city of Nephi.

places.name: Jerusalem (Lamanite city)
places.summary: This Jerusalem was a city the Lamanites and Amulonites built in the land of Nephi.

refs.note: The city of Jerusalem joined the borders of Mormon.
Waters came up in the place of Jerusalem.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the waters of Mormon were a lake. Jerusalem and Mormon both bordered it.

places.name: Ani-Anti
places.summary: Ani-Anti was a Lamanite village that Aaron visited after Jerusalem.

refs.note: Aaron came over to a village called Ani-Anti.

sorenson.text: Sorenson does not place the village. He notes Aaron came over to it from Jerusalem.

places.name: Helam
places.summary: Helam was the land where Alma’s people settled after fleeing King Noah.

refs.note: They fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.
They called the land Helam.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Helam in a mountain valley. He estimates it was no more than 85 miles from Nephi.

places.name: Valley of Alma
places.summary: Alma’s people camped in this valley after one day of travel from Helam.

refs.note: After traveling all day, they called the valley Alma.

sorenson.text: Sorenson counts this day in the 13 days from Helam to Zarahemla.

places.name: Amulon
places.summary: Amulon was a land settled by King Noah’s former priests.

refs.note: The lost Lamanite army found the priests in the land of Amulon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Amulon was not far from Nephi. The rough land still got an army lost.

places.name: Land of Ishmael
places.summary: Ishmael was a Lamanite land where Ammon taught King Lamoni.

refs.note: Ammon went to the land of Ishmael.

sorenson.text: Sorenson lists Ishmael among lands the Lamanites settled. He does not place it.

places.name: Middoni
places.summary: Middoni was a Lamanite land where Aaron and others were jailed.

refs.note: Ammon’s brethren were in prison in the land of Middoni.

sorenson.text: Sorenson lists Middoni among lands the Lamanites settled. He does not place it.

places.name: Land of first inheritance
places.summary: Lehi’s family first landed here, by the west seashore.

refs.note: They arrived at the promised land.
The place of their fathers’ first inheritance was on the west, by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the landing in the far south of the land southward, near sea level.

places.name: Mocum
places.summary: Mocum was a city covered by waters at the time of Christ’s death.

refs.note: Waters came up in the place of the city Mocum.

sorenson.text: Sorenson does not know Mocum’s position. His map 15 guesses at it.

places.name: Narrow neck of land
places.summary: A small neck of land joined the land northward and the land southward.

refs.note: A Nephite could cross from sea to sea in a day and a half.
Hagoth launched his ship by the narrow neck.
The Jaredites built a city where the sea divides the land.

sorenson.text: Sorenson argues for 60 to 125 miles across. A narrow neck would not fit Limhi’s lost explorers.

places.name: Narrow pass
places.summary: The narrow pass led by the sea into the land northward.

refs.note: The pass led by the sea into the land northward.
Moroni told Teancum to secure the narrow pass.
Mormon fortified at the narrow pass.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts the pass near the east sea. He thinks large groups could enter the land northward only here.

places.name: Hagoth’s shipyard
places.summary: Hagoth built ships on the borders of Bountiful and launched them into the west sea.

refs.note: Hagoth launched his ship into the west sea, by the narrow neck.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks ships were used because no good land road ran up the west coast.

places.name: Gathering place against the robbers
places.summary: Lachoneus gathered the people into one place between Zarahemla and Bountiful.

refs.note: The people gathered in one body.
They gathered in the land between Zarahemla and Bountiful.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the area was small enough for the robbers to surround it.

places.name: Desolation
places.summary: Desolation was the land, and later a city, just north of the narrow neck.

refs.note: The land northward was called Desolation.
Mormon gathered his people at the land Desolation.
The Lamanites took the city Desolation.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the last Nephite wars stayed near this city. They also reached the hills north of it.

places.name: Teancum
places.summary: Teancum was a city in the borders by the seashore, near Desolation.

refs.note: The city Teancum lay in the borders by the seashore, near Desolation.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Teancum northeast of Desolation.

places.name: Boaz
places.summary: Boaz was a city the Nephites fled to after losing Desolation.

refs.note: The Nephites fled to the city of Boaz.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Boaz on the second retreat.

places.name: Jordan
places.summary: Jordan was a city the Nephites held during their last retreat.

refs.note: The Nephites held the city of Jordan.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Jordan north of Boaz.

places.name: Jashon
places.summary: Jashon was a land and city near the place where Ammaron hid the records.

refs.note: The Nephites fled until they came to the land of Jashon.
Jashon was near the land where Ammaron hid the records.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Jashon near the hill Shim. It was near Mormon’s home area.

places.name: Shem
places.summary: Shem was a land and city north of Jashon that Mormon fortified.

refs.note: The Nephites were driven north to the land called Shem.
They fortified the city of Shem.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows Shem on the first retreat, north of Jashon.

places.name: Hill Shim
places.summary: Shim was a hill in the land of Antum. Ammaron hid the records there.

refs.note: The records were in a hill called Shim, in the land of Antum.
Omer passed by the hill of Shim.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Shim just south of Cumorah. The Nephites reached Shim before Cumorah.

places.name: Hill Cumorah (Ramah)
places.summary: Cumorah was the hill of the last Nephite battle. The Jaredites called it Ramah.

refs.note: The land of Cumorah had many waters, rivers, and fountains.
The Jaredites gathered at the hill Ramah, where Mormon hid records.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Cumorah about 100 miles north of the narrow pass. He sees no great mountain there.

places.name: Ablom
places.summary: Ablom was a place by the seashore where Omer pitched his tent.

refs.note: Omer came over to a place called Ablom, by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Ablom by the east sea, past Cumorah.

places.name: Waters of Ripliancum
places.summary: Ripliancum was a large body of water that stopped an army going north.

refs.note: Coriantumr pitched his tents by the waters of Ripliancum.
From there, Shiz’s army fled south to a place called Ogath.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the waters came from highland runoff to the west. Ramah was one day south.

places.name: Ogath
places.summary: Ogath was where Shiz camped near the hill Ramah.

refs.note: Shiz pitched his tents in a place called Ogath.

sorenson.text: Sorenson does not place Ogath. The map puts it between Ripliancum and Ramah.

places.name: Hill Comnor
places.summary: Comnor was a hill near the valley of Shurr in the Jaredite wars.

refs.note: Coriantumr placed his armies by the hill Comnor.

sorenson.text: Sorenson lists Comnor with the hills near the east sea. He gives no exact place.

places.name: Farthest Nephite retreat
places.summary: Mormon’s people fled north past Jordan before the final battle.

refs.note: The Nephites fled, and some were swept down and destroyed.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 marks this as the farthest retreat north. It stayed near Cumorah.

places.name: Moron
places.summary: Moron was the Jaredite land where the king lived.

refs.note: Corihor came up to the land of Moron, where the king lived.
Moron was near the land the Nephites called Desolation.

sorenson.text: Sorenson puts Moron in the western highlands. He says the Nephites never lived there.

places.name: Jacobugath
places.summary: Jacobugath was the city of the dissenter Jacob. It burned when Christ died.

refs.note: Jacob led his people to the northernmost part of the land.
The Lord burned the city Jacobugath.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Jacobugath was farther north than any other known city.

places.name: Moronihah
places.summary: Moronihah was a city covered with earth when Christ died.

refs.note: Earth was carried on the city of Moronihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks this city was in the east borders near Jershon.

places.name: Onihah
places.summary: Onihah was a city covered by waters at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Waters came up in the place of the city Onihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Onihah in the land southward by guess.

places.name: Gilgal
places.summary: Gilgal was a city buried in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Gilgal was sunk and buried.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gilgal in the land southward by guess.

places.name: Kishkumen
places.summary: Kishkumen was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city Kishkumen and its people were burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Kishkumen near the neck by guess.

places.name: Laman
places.summary: Laman was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Laman was burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Laman in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gad
places.summary: Gad was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Gad was burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gad in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gadiandi
places.summary: Gadiandi was a city sunk in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Gadiandi was sunk with Gadiomnah, Jacob, and Gimgimno.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gadiandi in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gadiomnah
places.summary: Gadiomnah was a city sunk in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Gadiomnah was among the cities sunk in the earth.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gadiomnah in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Gimgimno
places.summary: Gimgimno was a city sunk in the earth at Christ’s death.

refs.note: Gimgimno was among the cities sunk in the earth.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Gimgimno in the land northward by guess.

places.name: Josh
places.summary: Josh was a city burned at Christ’s death.

refs.note: The city of Josh was burned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson places Josh in the land northward by guess.

areas.name: Borders by the east sea
match: \b(?:east sea|sea east|east borders by the seashore)\b

people.name: Lehi (father of Nephi)
people.role: Prophet who led his family from Jerusalem
people.summary: Lehi was a prophet in Jerusalem and the father of Nephi. He led his family into the wilderness.
people.detail: He saw God in vision and warned Jerusalem of its fall. Later Nephites date their years from his departure.

refs.note: Lehi lives at Jerusalem in the first year of Zedekiah.
The Lord tells Lehi in a dream to leave.
Lehi sees a tree whose fruit makes one happy.
Lehi grows old, dies, and is buried.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads Lehi as a short name meaning God is my strength.
Another proposal reads it as belonging to the Living One. The Hebrew letters also spell cheek.

people.name: Sariah
people.role: Wife of Lehi, mother of Nephi
people.summary: Sariah was the wife of Lehi. She was the mother of Laman, Lemuel, Sam, Nephi, Jacob, and Joseph.
people.detail: She feared her sons had died on their return to Jerusalem. When they came back, she bore witness of the Lord.

refs.note: Sariah leaves Jerusalem with Lehi and her sons.
She complains that her sons are lost.
She now knows the Lord protected her sons.

scholarship.text: Sariah may be a feminine form of the biblical name Seraiah.
One reading is prince of Jehovah. Similar names include Sarai and Sarah.
The name Sryh appears as a Jewish woman’s name in Aramaic papyri from Elephantine, Egypt.

people.name: Nephi (son of Lehi)
people.role: Prophet, record keeper, and first Nephite leader
people.summary: Nephi was a son of Lehi and Sariah. He wrote 1 and 2 Nephi on the small plates.
people.detail: He got the brass plates and built a ship. The Nephites took their name from him.

refs.note: Nephi says he was born of goodly parents.
He says he will go and do what the Lord commands.
The people want Nephi to be their king.
Nephi grows old and anoints a new king.

scholarship.text: The Onomasticon favors an Egyptian root, nfr, which means good or beautiful.
Hugh Nibley proposed a link to an Egyptian word for captain.

people.name: Laman (son of Lehi)
people.summary: Laman was the eldest son of Lehi and Sariah. The Lamanites took their name from him.
people.detail: He often rebelled against his father and Nephi. After Lehi died, he sought to kill Nephi.

refs.note: Laman and Lemuel murmur against their father.
Laman goes first to ask Laban for the plates.
Laman and Lemuel plan to kill Nephi.
Helaman calls Laman the eldest son of Lehi.

scholarship.text: Laman may come from a Semitic root LMN. A Lihyanite inscription from Arabia has the name.

people.name: Lemuel
people.summary: Lemuel was the second son of Lehi and Sariah. He usually followed his older brother Laman.
people.detail: Lehi named a valley after him and asked him to be firm and steadfast.

refs.note: Lehi wishes that Lemuel would be like the valley.
Laman and Lemuel beat Nephi and Sam with a rod.
Lehi speaks to Laman, Lemuel, and Sam before his death.

people.name: Sam
people.role: Son of Lehi, brother of Nephi
people.summary: Sam was the third son of Lehi and Sariah. He believed Nephi and followed him.
people.detail: Lehi blessed Sam that his seed would be numbered with Nephi’s seed.

refs.note: Nephi tells Sam what the Lord showed him, and Sam believes.
Lehi blesses Sam and his seed.
Sam goes with Nephi when the people separate.

scholarship.text: Sam may be a short form of Samuel. Others propose an Egyptian origin.

people.name: Jacob (son of Lehi)
people.role: Prophet, priest, and writer of the book of Jacob
people.summary: Jacob was the elder of two sons born to Lehi in the wilderness. Nephi gave him the small plates.
people.detail: Nephi made him a priest and teacher. His sermons appear in 2 Nephi and in his own book.

refs.note: Lehi has two sons in the wilderness, Jacob and Joseph.
Lehi calls Jacob his firstborn in the wilderness.
Nephi commands Jacob to write on the small plates.
Jacob gives the plates to his son Enos.

people.name: Joseph (son of Lehi)
people.summary: Joseph was the youngest son of Lehi and Sariah. He was born in the wilderness.
people.detail: Lehi blessed him with the prophecies of Joseph of Egypt. Nephi made him a priest and teacher.

refs.note: Joseph is the younger of two sons born in the wilderness.
Lehi speaks to Joseph, his last-born.
Nephi consecrates Jacob and Joseph as priests and teachers.

people.name: Zoram (servant of Laban)
people.role: Laban’s servant who joined Lehi’s family
people.summary: Zoram was the servant of Laban. He gave Nephi the brass plates and then joined Lehi’s family.
people.detail: He swore an oath to stay with them. He married the eldest daughter of Ishmael.

refs.note: Zoram agrees to go into the wilderness with them.
Zoram marries the eldest daughter of Ishmael.
Lehi calls Zoram a true friend to Nephi.
Ammoron later says he descends from Zoram.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads Zoram as the Rock is the divine kinsman. An Amorite name has the same parts.

people.name: Laban
people.role: Jerusalem official who kept the brass plates
people.summary: Laban was a powerful man in Jerusalem. He kept the brass plates and descended from Joseph.
people.detail: He took the family’s property and tried to kill Lehi’s sons. The Spirit told Nephi to slay him.

refs.note: Laban has the record of the Jews on plates of brass.
Laban takes their property and sends servants to kill them.
Nephi slays Laban with Laban’s own sword.
Laban also descends from Joseph.

scholarship.text: Laban may come from Hebrew lābān, which means white.
John W. Welch reads the slaying through ancient Israelite law on homicide.
He notes that Nephi did not lie in wait. The text says God delivered Laban to him.

people.name: Ishmael (companion of Lehi)
people.role: Head of the family that joined Lehi
people.summary: Ishmael lived in Jerusalem. He brought his family into the wilderness to join Lehi.
people.detail: His daughters married Lehi’s sons and Zoram. He died and was buried at Nahom.

refs.note: The Lord sends Lehi’s sons back to bring Ishmael’s family.
Lehi’s sons marry daughters of Ishmael.
Ishmael dies and is buried at Nahom.

people.name: Tribes of Lehi’s family
people.role: Family groups named after Lehi’s sons, Zoram, and Ishmael
people.summary: The early people kept tribe names from their founders. They were Nephites, Jacobites, Josephites, Zoramites, Lamanites, Lemuelites, and Ishmaelites.
people.detail: Jacob chose to call them only Nephites and Lamanites. The seven names return in 4 Nephi.

refs.note: Jacob lists the seven names.
Believers again take the names of the tribes.
War begins between the two sets of tribes.

people.name: Enos
people.summary: Enos was the son of Jacob. He kept the small plates after his father.
people.detail: He prayed all day and night and received forgiveness. He then prayed for the Nephites and the Lamanites.

refs.note: Jacob gives the plates to his son Enos.
Enos tells of his wrestle before God.
He prays for his brethren, the Lamanites.
He asks the Lord to preserve a record for the Lamanites.

people.name: Jarom
people.role: Son of Enos, Nephite record keeper
people.summary: Jarom was the son of Enos. He kept the small plates and wrote a short book.
people.detail: He says the plates are small. He describes prophets, kings, and wars with the Lamanites.

refs.note: Jarom writes at the command of his father Enos.
He writes little because the plates are small.
Jarom commands his son Omni to keep the record.

scholarship.text: Jarom may be a short form of a name from Hebrew ram, to be exalted.

people.name: Sherem
people.summary: Sherem was a skilled speaker among the Nephites. He taught that there should be no Christ.
people.detail: He asked Jacob for a sign and was struck down. Before he died, he confessed that he had lied.

refs.note: Sherem preaches that there should be no Christ.
He asks Jacob for a sign.
He confesses and then dies.

scholarship.text: The meaning of Sherem is not known. The Onomasticon judges most proposals unlikely.

people.name: Zenos
people.role: Prophet quoted from the brass plates
people.summary: Zenos was a prophet of Israel whose words were on the brass plates. The Bible does not name him.
people.detail: Jacob quotes his allegory of the olive tree. Alma quotes his prayer, and Nephi says he was slain.

refs.note: Zenos prophesies of three days of darkness.
Jacob quotes the words of Zenos.
Alma quotes Zenos on prayer.
Zenos was slain for his testimony.

scholarship.text: One proposal compares the Greek word zenos, stranger or guest.
Robert F. Smith proposed that Zenos lived before the exile, perhaps among Greek speakers.

people.name: Zenock
people.role: Prophet quoted from the brass plates
people.summary: Zenock was a prophet of Israel whose words were on the brass plates. The Bible does not name him.
people.detail: He prophesied that the Son of God would be lifted up. The people stoned him.

refs.note: Nephi cites Zenock on the Lord being lifted up.
Alma says Zenock also spoke of the Son.
The people stoned him to death.

people.name: Neum
people.role: Prophet quoted from the brass plates
people.summary: Neum was a prophet whose words were on the brass plates. Nephi cites him once.

refs.note: Neum prophesied that the God of Israel would be crucified.

scholarship.text: Neum may come from Hebrew neum, a word for a divine declaration.

people.name: Isaiah
people.role: Prophet of Judah, son of Amoz
people.summary: Isaiah was a prophet of Judah and the son of Amoz. Nephi copied many of his chapters.
people.detail: Nephi likened Isaiah’s words to his own people. Jesus later told the Nephites to search them.

refs.note: Nephi reads Isaiah to his brothers and likens it to them.
Nephi says his soul delights in Isaiah’s words.
The Isaiah chapters begin with his name.
Jesus says great are the words of Isaiah.

people.name: Moses
people.role: Prophet who led Israel out of Egypt
people.summary: Moses was the prophet who led Israel out of Egypt. Nephi uses his story to give courage.
people.detail: The brass plates held the five books of Moses. Later prophets cite his brass serpent.

refs.note: Nephi tells his brothers to be strong like Moses.
The brass plates contain the five books of Moses.
Nephi recalls how Moses divided the Red Sea.

people.name: Law of Moses
people.role: Israel’s law, kept by the Nephites until Christ
people.summary: The law of Moses was the law God gave Israel through Moses. The Nephites kept it.
people.detail: They taught that the law pointed to Christ. Christ said it was fulfilled in him.

refs.note: Nephi’s people keep the law of Moses.
They believe in Christ and still keep the law.
The law points their souls to Christ.
Jesus says the law is fulfilled.

people.name: Zedekiah
people.summary: Zedekiah was the last king of Judah. Lehi’s story begins in his first year.
people.detail: Babylon took him captive. His son Mulek escaped and came to the promised land.

refs.note: Lehi’s call comes in the first year of Zedekiah.
Zedekiah is carried away captive into Babylon.
All his sons were slain except Mulek.

people.name: Jeremiah
people.role: Prophet of Judah in Lehi’s day
people.summary: Jeremiah was a prophet in Jerusalem in Lehi’s time. The brass plates held some of his prophecies.

refs.note: The brass plates contain prophecies of Jeremiah.
The Jews have cast Jeremiah into prison.
Jeremiah testified of the fall of Jerusalem.

people.name: Joseph (of Egypt)
people.role: Son of Jacob, ancestor of Lehi
people.summary: Joseph was the son of Jacob who was sold into Egypt. Lehi and Laban descended from him.
people.detail: Lehi quotes Joseph’s prophecy of a choice seer in the latter days. Moroni later recalls his torn coat.

refs.note: Lehi learns from the brass plates that he descends from Joseph.
Lehi calls Joseph his ancestor.
Joseph prophesies of a choice seer.
Moroni recalls the remnant of Joseph’s coat.

people.name: Abraham
people.summary: Abraham was the father of Israel. God made a covenant with him about his seed.

refs.note: The Lord promised Abraham that his seed would bless all.
Isaiah tells Israel to look to Abraham.
Abraham obeyed in offering up Isaac.

people.name: Isaac
people.summary: Isaac was the son of Abraham and the father of Jacob.
people.detail: Jacob calls Abraham’s offering of Isaac a likeness of God and his Son.

refs.note: Nephi writes to bring men to the God of Isaac.
Abraham offers up his son Isaac.

people.name: Jacob (Israel)
people.role: Son of Isaac, father of the twelve tribes
match: (?<=(?:God of|Isaac,? and(?: of| with)?|with|son of|father|words of|language of) )Jacob\b
people.summary: Jacob was the son of Isaac. God renamed him Israel, and his sons led the twelve tribes.

refs.note: Joseph was the son of Jacob.
The Lord covenanted with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
Moroni retells Jacob’s words about Joseph’s coat.

people.name: Sarah
people.summary: Sarah was the wife of Abraham and the mother of Isaac. Isaiah names her once.

refs.note: Isaiah tells Israel to look to Sarah, who bore them.

people.name: Adam
people.summary: Adam was the first man. The brass plates told of Adam and Eve, our first parents.
people.detail: Lehi teaches that Adam fell that men might be. Later prophets explain the fall and the atonement.

refs.note: The brass plates tell of Adam and Eve.
Without the fall, Adam would have stayed in the garden.
Adam fell that men might be.
The natural man has been an enemy since the fall.

people.name: Eve
people.summary: Eve was the first woman and the wife of Adam.

refs.note: The brass plates name Adam and Eve as our first parents.
The devil tempts Eve.
Adam and Eve leave the garden after they eat the fruit.

people.name: Pharaoh
people.role: King of Egypt in the Exodus
people.summary: Pharaoh was the king of Egypt. His armies drowned in the Red Sea when they chased Israel.

refs.note: The armies of Pharaoh drown in the Red Sea.
Nephi reminds his brothers of the drowned Egyptians.

people.name: John (the apostle)
people.role: Apostle of Jesus who wrote of the end of the world
people.summary: John was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus. An angel told Nephi that John would write the end of the vision.

refs.note: The angel names the apostle John.
Jesus says John desired to remain on the earth.
The Lord’s revelations written by John will be unfolded.

people.name: David
people.summary: David was a king of Israel and the father of Solomon.
people.detail: Jacob condemns David’s many wives and concubines. Isaiah speaks of the throne of David.

refs.note: Isaiah foretells a ruler on the throne of David.
Jacob says David’s many wives were abominable.

people.name: Solomon
people.role: King of Israel, son of David
people.summary: Solomon was a king of Israel and the son of David. He built the temple at Jerusalem.

refs.note: Nephi builds a temple like Solomon’s temple.
Jacob condemns Solomon’s many wives.
Jesus says Solomon was not dressed like the lilies.

people.name: Brass plates
people.role: Scripture record that Lehi’s family took from Jerusalem
people.summary: The brass plates were a record kept by Laban. They held scripture and Lehi’s genealogy.
people.detail: They had the five books of Moses and prophecies of Jeremiah. Later Nephite kings kept them.

refs.note: Laban has the plates of brass.
The plates contain the five books of Moses.
King Benjamin teaches his sons from the plates of brass.
The plates will go forth to every nation.

people.name: Plates of Nephi
people.role: The Nephite records, large and small
people.summary: Nephi made two sets of plates. The large plates held history, and the small plates held the ministry.
people.detail: The small plates passed from Jacob to Amaleki. Mormon added them to his abridgment.

refs.note: Nephi names the full history the plates of Nephi.
The other plates hold the reign of kings and wars.
Nephi gives Jacob the small plates.
Mormon finds the small plates among the records.

people.name: Sword of Laban
people.summary: The sword of Laban had a gold hilt and a steel blade. Nephi took it from Laban.
people.detail: Nephi used it as a pattern for more swords. King Benjamin later fought with it.

refs.note: Nephi makes swords after the manner of it.
Nephi wielded the sword in defense of his people.
King Benjamin fights with the sword of Laban.
Benjamin gives the sword to his son Mosiah.

people.name: Liahona
people.role: Brass ball that guided Lehi’s family
people.summary: The Liahona was a brass ball with two spindles. It pointed the way for Lehi’s family.
people.detail: It worked by their faith and diligence. Alma names it and calls it a type of the word of Christ.

refs.note: Lehi finds a round ball of curious workmanship.
The pointers work by faith and diligence.
The compass stops working when Nephi is bound.
Alma says the fathers called it Liahona.

scholarship.text: Scholars agree the name likely begins to or of Jehovah. The ending is debated.
Hugh Nibley proposed God is our guide. Matthew Bowen proposed Look to the Lord.
The Onomasticon notes several older proposals and judges them unlikely.

people.name: Tree of life
people.role: Symbol of God’s love in Lehi’s dream
people.summary: In Lehi’s dream, a tree bore fruit that made people happy. Nephi learned it shows God’s love.
people.detail: Lehi also names the tree of life in Eden. Alma later invites people to eat its fruit.

refs.note: Lehi sees a tree whose fruit makes one happy.
The rod of iron leads to the tree of life.
The forbidden fruit stands in opposition to the tree of life.
Alma invites all to eat of the tree of life.

people.name: Rod of iron
people.role: Symbol of the word of God in Lehi’s dream
people.summary: In Lehi’s dream, a rod of iron ran beside a path to the tree. Nephi learned it was the word of God.

refs.note: Lehi sees a rod of iron along the river.
People hold the rod through the mist of darkness.
Those who hold to the word of God will not perish.

people.name: Great and spacious building
people.role: Symbol of the pride of the world
people.summary: In Lehi’s dream, people in a high building mocked those who ate the fruit.
people.detail: Nephi learned it stood for pride and vain imaginations. He saw that it fell.

refs.note: The building stands as if in the air.
Its people mock those who eat the fruit.
The building is the pride of the world, and it falls.

people.name: Great and abominable church
people.role: Symbol of opposition to God in Nephi’s vision
people.summary: In Nephi’s vision, the devil founded a great and abominable church. It fights the saints of God.
people.detail: It takes plain and precious things from the book of the Lamb. In the end it falls.

refs.note: Nephi sees the church and its founder, the devil.
Plain and precious things are taken from the book.
The angel names only two churches.
The church will tumble to the dust.

people.name: Allegory of the olive tree
people.role: Zenos’s parable of the house of Israel
people.summary: Zenos compared Israel to a tame olive tree in a vineyard. Its branches are scattered and grafted back.
people.detail: Lehi used the same image. Jacob quotes the whole allegory in Jacob 5.

refs.note: Lehi compares Israel to an olive tree.
Zenos likens Israel to a tame olive tree.
Jacob says Zenos’s words must come to pass.

people.name: Bible
people.summary: Nephi prophesies that many Gentiles will reject more scripture. They will say they already have a Bible.
people.detail: The Lord says the Bible came from the Jews. He says it does not hold all his words.

refs.note: Gentiles say there cannot be any more Bible.
The Bible comes forth from the Jews.
The Bible does not contain all of God’s words.

people.name: Language of the Egyptians
people.summary: Nephi wrote in the language of the Egyptians. Lehi learned it so he could read the brass plates.
people.detail: Moroni calls the later script reformed Egyptian. He says the Nephites changed it over time.

refs.note: Nephi’s record uses the learning of the Jews and the language of the Egyptians.
Lehi could read the plates because he knew the language.
Moroni names the script reformed Egyptian.

people.name: Amoz
people.summary: Amoz was the father of the prophet Isaiah.

refs.note: Isaiah is the son of Amoz.
The burden of Babylon is from Isaiah, son of Amoz.

people.name: Uzziah
people.summary: Uzziah was a king of Judah and the grandfather of Ahaz. Isaiah saw the Lord in the year Uzziah died.

refs.note: Isaiah sees the Lord in the year Uzziah died.
Uzziah is the father of Jotham.

people.name: Jotham
people.role: King of Judah, father of Ahaz
people.summary: Jotham was the son of Uzziah and the father of Ahaz.

refs.note: Ahaz is the son of Jotham.

people.name: Ahaz
people.role: King of Judah in Isaiah’s day
people.summary: Ahaz was a king of Judah. Syria and Israel attacked Jerusalem in his day.
people.detail: Isaiah told him not to fear and offered him a sign. Ahaz refused to ask.

refs.note: Rezin and Pekah attack Jerusalem in the days of Ahaz.
Ahaz will not ask for a sign.
A burden comes in the year Ahaz died.

people.name: Rezin
people.summary: Rezin was the king of Syria. He joined Pekah of Israel to attack Judah.

refs.note: Rezin and Pekah go up against Jerusalem.
Rezin is the head of Damascus.

people.name: Pekah, son of Remaliah
people.summary: Pekah, son of Remaliah, was king of the northern kingdom of Israel. He joined Rezin against Judah.
people.detail: Isaiah often calls him only Remaliah’s son.

refs.note: Pekah, son of Remaliah, attacks Jerusalem.
Remaliah’s son is the head of Samaria.

people.name: Shearjashub
people.summary: Shearjashub was a son of Isaiah. He went with his father to meet King Ahaz.

refs.note: Isaiah takes Shearjashub to meet Ahaz.

people.name: Son of Tabeal
people.role: Man Syria and Israel planned to make king
people.summary: Syria and Israel planned to make the son of Tabeal king in Judah. The text does not name him.

refs.note: The enemies plan to set the son of Tabeal as king.

people.name: Maher-shalal-hash-baz
people.summary: Maher-shalal-hash-baz was a son of Isaiah. His name served as a sign to Judah.

refs.note: Isaiah writes the name on a great roll.
The Lord tells Isaiah to give his son this name.

people.name: Uriah (the priest)
people.summary: Uriah was a priest. Isaiah took him as a faithful witness.

refs.note: Isaiah takes Uriah the priest as a witness.

people.name: Zechariah (son of Jeberechiah)
people.summary: Zechariah was the son of Jeberechiah. Isaiah took him as a faithful witness.

refs.note: Isaiah takes Zechariah as a witness.

people.name: Jesse
people.summary: Jesse was the father of King David. Isaiah foretells a rod and a root from Jesse.

refs.note: A rod comes forth from the stem of Jesse.
A root of Jesse stands for an ensign.

people.name: Ephraim
people.role: Tribe and northern kingdom of Israel
people.summary: Ephraim was a son of Joseph and a tribe of Israel. Isaiah uses the name for the northern kingdom.

refs.note: Syria is allied with Ephraim.
Ephraim will be broken.
The envy of Ephraim will depart.

people.name: Manasseh
people.role: Son of Joseph and tribe of Israel
people.summary: Manasseh was a son of Joseph of Egypt and a tribe of Israel. Lehi descended from him.

refs.note: Isaiah says Manasseh and Ephraim will turn on each other.
Amulek says Lehi descended from Manasseh.

people.name: Philistines
people.summary: The Philistines lived on the coast west of Judah. Isaiah names them as enemies of Israel.

refs.note: The Syrians and the Philistines devour Israel.
Israel will fly upon the Philistines.

people.name: Syrians
people.role: People of Syria, north of Israel
people.summary: The Syrians lived north of Israel, with Damascus as their head city. Rezin was their king.

refs.note: The Syrians come before and the Philistines behind.

people.name: The Assyrian
people.summary: Assyria was a great empire east of Israel. Isaiah calls the Assyrian the rod of the Lord’s anger.
people.detail: Isaiah also says the Lord will break the Assyrian in his land.

refs.note: The Assyrian is the rod of the Lord’s anger.
The Lord will break the Assyrian.

people.name: Chaldeans
people.summary: The Chaldeans ruled Babylon. Isaiah tells Israel to flee from them.

refs.note: Go forth of Babylon and flee from the Chaldeans.
Babylon, the glory of the Chaldees, will fall.

people.name: Medes
people.summary: The Medes lived east of Babylon. Isaiah says the Lord will stir them up against Babylon.

refs.note: The Lord will stir up the Medes.

people.name: Rahab (the sea monster)
people.summary: Isaiah praises the arm of the Lord that cut Rahab. The verse pairs Rahab with the dragon.

refs.note: The arm of the Lord cut Rahab.

people.name: Omni
people.summary: Omni was the son of Jarom. He kept the small plates after his father and wrote three verses.
people.detail: He calls himself a wicked man who fought often to defend his people. His short entry starts the book that carries his name.

refs.note: Jarom gives the plates to his son Omni.
Omni says he fought with the sword to preserve his people.

people.name: Amaron
people.role: Nephite record keeper, son of Omni
people.summary: Amaron was the son of Omni. He kept the plates after his father.
people.detail: He records the destruction of the more wicked Nephites. He then gives the plates to his brother Chemish.

refs.note: Amaron writes after his father Omni.
He dates the destruction to 320 years after Lehi left Jerusalem.

people.name: Chemish
people.role: Nephite record keeper, brother of Amaron
people.summary: Chemish was the brother of Amaron. He wrote one verse on the plates.
people.detail: He notes that the record follows the commandments of the fathers.

refs.note: Chemish writes in the same book as his brother.

people.name: Abinadom
people.role: Nephite record keeper, son of Chemish
people.summary: Abinadom was the son of Chemish. He fought the Lamanites and kept the plates.
people.detail: He says he knows of no revelation or prophecy beyond what is written.

refs.note: Abinadom writes after his father Chemish.
He knows of no new revelation.

people.name: Amaleki
people.role: Last keeper of the small plates
people.summary: Amaleki was the son of Abinadom. He wrote most of the book of Omni.
people.detail: He tells how Mosiah led his people to Zarahemla. He had no children, so he gave the plates to King Benjamin.

refs.note: Amaleki begins with the story of Mosiah.
He gives the plates to King Benjamin.
He invites all to come to Christ.

people.name: Mosiah (the first)
people.summary: Mosiah the first led the faithful Nephites out of the land of Nephi. He became king in Zarahemla.
people.detail: He read an engraved stone with the interpreters. His grandson, also named Mosiah, appears in the book of Mosiah.

refs.note: The Lord warns Mosiah to flee from the land of Nephi.
The two peoples unite, and Mosiah becomes their king.
Mosiah interprets the engravings on a large stone.

people.name: People of Zarahemla (Mulekites)
people.role: People who came from Jerusalem with Mulek
people.summary: The people of Zarahemla left Jerusalem when King Zedekiah fell. They crossed the sea and settled in the land.
people.detail: Their language had changed, and they had no records. They joined Mosiah’s people and outnumbered the Nephites. Readers often call them Mulekites, after Mulek.

refs.note: They came out of Jerusalem when Zedekiah was taken to Babylon.
Their language had become corrupted, and they denied God.
They descended from Mulek and outnumbered the Nephites.

scholarship.text: The name Mulek may come from the Hebrew root mlk, which means king or reign. One proposal reads it as a short form for little king.

people.name: Mulek
people.role: Son of Zedekiah, king of Judah
people.summary: Mulek was a son of Zedekiah, the last king of Judah. He escaped when Babylon took Jerusalem.
people.detail: The Lord brought him to the promised land. The people of Zarahemla descended from his group.

refs.note: Zarahemla was a descendant of Mulek.
The land north was named after Mulek, a son of Zedekiah.
Nephi says all of Zedekiah’s sons were slain except Mulek.

scholarship.text: Mulek likely comes from the Hebrew root mlk, as in melek, the word for king. The form may mean little king.
Hugh Nibley first proposed this diminutive. It could suit a young prince who escaped the fall of Jerusalem.
Jeremiah 38:6 names Malchiah the son of Hammelech. The Hebrew can also read Malkiyahu, son of the king.
Some Latter-day Saint scholars link Mulek to that Malkiyahu. Others note that Malkiyahu seems an adult there.
A stamp seal from Jerusalem, about 600 BCE, names Malkiyahu, son of the king.
Jeffrey Chadwick proposed that this was Zedekiah’s son. The seal does not name the father.

people.name: Zarahemla (the leader)
people.role: Leader of the people of Zarahemla
people.summary: Zarahemla led the people who lived in the land when Mosiah arrived. The land and city carry his name.
people.detail: He gave the genealogy of his fathers from memory. He descended from Mulek.

refs.note: Zarahemla gives his fathers’ genealogy from memory.
Zarahemla was a descendant of Mulek.

people.name: Coriantumr (the Jaredite king)
people.summary: Coriantumr was the last Jaredite king. The people of Zarahemla found him after his nation’s final war.
people.detail: He lived with them for nine moons. A large stone told his story, and Mosiah read it.

refs.note: The people of Zarahemla discover Coriantumr.
Coriantumr kills Shiz and is the last of his people.
Ether prophesies that Coriantumr will see another people.

people.name: King Benjamin
people.role: Nephite king and prophet, son of Mosiah
people.summary: Benjamin was the son of Mosiah the first. He became king in Zarahemla after his father died.
people.detail: He fought the Lamanites and made peace in the land. Late in life, he spoke to his people from a tower. They made a covenant to take the name of Christ.

refs.note: Benjamin reigns after his father Mosiah.
Mormon calls Benjamin a holy man who reigned in righteousness.
Benjamin teaches that service to others is service to God.
The people become the children of Christ.

scholarship.text: The name Benjamin usually means son of the right hand.
A rival reading is son of the south. The Mari archives name a southern Yamina tribe.
If right hand is correct, Mosiah 5 may contain a wordplay on the name.
Scholars compare the gathering in tents with the Feast of Tabernacles.
The article admits that the text does not say why the people used tents.

people.name: Benjamin’s tower
people.summary: King Benjamin built a tower near the temple. He spoke to his people from it.
people.detail: The crowd was too large for the temple walls. The people who could not hear received his words in writing.

refs.note: Benjamin builds a tower because the crowd is so great.
Not all hear, so his words are written and sent out.

people.name: Helorum
people.summary: Helorum was a son of King Benjamin. He was a brother of Mosiah and Helaman.
people.detail: Benjamin taught his three sons the language and records of their fathers.

refs.note: Benjamin names his three sons.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads Helorum as Hebrew for God exalts. Other proposals also exist.

people.name: Helaman (son of Benjamin)
people.summary: This Helaman was a son of King Benjamin. He is not the later Helaman, son of Alma.
people.detail: The text names him once, with his brothers Mosiah and Helorum.

refs.note: Benjamin names his three sons.

people.name: Mosiah (the second)
people.role: Last Nephite king, son of Benjamin
people.summary: Mosiah was the son of King Benjamin. He became king in Zarahemla and later ended the rule of kings.
people.detail: He translated the Jaredite record with the interpreters. None of his sons would be king. He set up the reign of the judges instead.

refs.note: Mosiah begins to reign at thirty years of age.
Mosiah translates the records with two stones.
Mosiah proposes judges in place of a king.
Mosiah dies at sixty-three years of age.

scholarship.text: Mosiah may come from Hebrew for the Lord delivers or saves.
The entry compares the Hebrew form of Isaiah. It also lists deliverer as a possible root.

people.name: Ammon (the explorer)
people.role: Leader of the search party to the land of Nephi
people.summary: Ammon was a strong man and a descendant of Zarahemla. King Mosiah sent him to find Zeniff’s people.
people.detail: He found King Limhi in the land of Nephi. He then helped Limhi’s people escape to Zarahemla. He is not Ammon the son of Mosiah.

refs.note: Ammon goes up with the sixteen strong men.
Ammon tells Limhi who he is.
Ammon tells Limhi of a man who can translate.
Ammon leads Limhi’s people toward Zarahemla.

people.name: Amaleki (Ammon’s companion)
people.summary: This Amaleki went with Ammon to the land of Nephi. He is not Amaleki the record keeper.

refs.note: Ammon takes Amaleki, Helem, and Hem with him.

people.name: Helem
people.summary: Helem was one of Ammon’s brethren. He went with Ammon to the land of Nephi.
people.detail: The king’s guard took the four men and put them in prison.

refs.note: Ammon takes Amaleki, Helem, and Hem with him.
The king’s guard binds the men and puts them in prison.

people.name: Hem
people.summary: Hem was one of Ammon’s brethren. He went with Ammon to the land of Nephi.

refs.note: Ammon takes Amaleki, Helem, and Hem with him.

people.name: Zeniff
people.role: Founder of a Nephite colony in the land of Nephi
people.summary: Zeniff led a group from Zarahemla back to the land of Nephi. He became their king.
people.detail: King Laman gave him land as a trick to bring his people into bondage. He fought the Lamanites and gave the kingdom to his son Noah.

refs.note: Zeniff begins his own record.
The king covenants to give Zeniff the land.
Zeniff confers the kingdom on his son Noah.

scholarship.text: Hugh Nibley proposed Arabic, Egyptian, and cuneiform parallels. The Onomasticon entry is unfinished.

people.name: King Laman (Lamanite kings)
people.role: Lamanite king, and his son of the same name
people.summary: Laman was a Lamanite king in the time of Zeniff. His son, also called King Laman, reigned after him.
people.detail: The first King Laman gave land to Zeniff to bring his people into bondage. The later king made Amulon a ruler over Alma’s people.

refs.note: King Laman yields land to Zeniff by craftiness.
King Laman dies, and his son reigns.
The king is called Laman after his father.

people.name: Noah (the king)
people.summary: Noah was the son of Zeniff. He ruled the colony in the land of Nephi after his father.
people.detail: He taxed his people heavily and replaced his father’s priests. He had Abinadi burned to death. His own people later burned him.

refs.note: Noah reigns after Zeniff, but not in his father’s ways.
He taxes one fifth of all his people owned.
The angry king delivers Abinadi up to be slain.
Noah’s men put him to death by fire.

people.name: Priests of Noah
people.summary: King Noah put down his father’s priests and appointed new ones. The new priests lived on the people’s taxes.
people.detail: They judged Abinadi. Later they fled, took Lamanite daughters as wives, and followed Amulon. Their children joined the Lamanites.

refs.note: Noah appoints new priests who are lifted up in pride.
The priests carry away twenty-four daughters of the Lamanites.
Amulon leads the priests.
The Lamanites hunt the seed of the priests, as Abinadi said.

people.name: Abinadi
people.summary: Abinadi was a prophet among King Noah’s people. He called them to repent.
people.detail: He taught the law of Moses and quoted Isaiah about the Messiah. Noah had him burned. Alma believed his words and began a church.

refs.note: Abinadi first warns the people.
His face shines while he speaks.
Alma believes the words of Abinadi.
Abinadi was the first to suffer death by fire.

scholarship.text: The meaning of Abinadi is uncertain. The first part, abi, means my father.
Proposals include my divine father is present and father of my wandering.
Scholars see parallels between Abinadi before Noah and Moses before Pharaoh.
Both men face a hard king and his priests. Both recite the commandments.
Abinadi’s shining face may echo the face of Moses after Sinai.

people.name: Gideon
people.summary: Gideon was a strong man in King Noah’s land. He later became King Limhi’s captain.
people.detail: He planned the escape of Limhi’s people from the Lamanites. In old age, Nehor killed him with a sword. A valley was named after him.

refs.note: Gideon swears to slay King Noah.
Gideon proposes an escape through the back pass.
Nehor kills the old Gideon with the sword.
The valley of Gideon carries his name.

people.name: Limhi
people.role: King of Zeniff’s colony, son of Noah
people.summary: Limhi was the son of King Noah. He ruled the people of Zeniff’s colony after his father.
people.detail: His people lived in bondage to the Lamanites. Ammon found him, and Gideon planned their escape. He brought the twenty-four gold plates to Mosiah.

refs.note: Limhi names himself as son of Noah and grandson of Zeniff.
The people confer the kingdom on Limhi.
Limhi tells Ammon of the twenty-four gold plates.
Limhi’s people escape into the wilderness.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads Limhi as the people live. The root is uncertain.

people.name: People of Limhi
people.summary: The people of Limhi were the descendants of Zeniff’s colony. They lived in bondage to the Lamanites.
people.detail: Three times they fought to be free and lost. They escaped with Ammon and Gideon and joined Mosiah in Zarahemla.

refs.note: They cannot free themselves, for the Lamanites surround them.
The Lord softens the hearts of the Lamanites.
They arrive in Zarahemla and join Mosiah’s people.
Their search party found the Jaredite plates.

people.name: Daughters of the Lamanites
people.role: Lamanite women taken by Noah’s priests
people.summary: The daughters of the Lamanites met in Shemlon to sing and dance. Noah’s priests carried twenty-four of them away.
people.detail: The Lamanites blamed Limhi’s people and went to war. Later the women pleaded for their husbands’ lives.

refs.note: The priests carry away twenty-four of the women.
The Lamanite king blames Limhi’s people.
The wives plead with the Lamanites to spare their husbands.

people.name: Alma (the elder)
people.role: Priest of Noah who became a prophet and church founder
people.summary: Alma was a young priest of King Noah. He believed Abinadi and fled for his life.
people.detail: He baptized believers at the waters of Mormon and founded a church. He led his people out of bondage to Zarahemla. Mosiah made him head of the church.

refs.note: Alma believes Abinadi and pleads for him.
Alma invites the people to be baptized.
The Lord comforts Alma’s people in their bondage.
The Lord blesses Alma for his faith.
The elder Alma dies at eighty-two years of age.

scholarship.text: Alma may come from a Hebrew word for youth or young man.
A Bar Kokhba-era deed names a man called Alma, son of Judah.
Terrence Szink found a similar name in Ebla tablets from the third millennium BCE.
Some readings are debated. The article still calls Alma a plausible Semitic name for men.

people.name: Alma (the younger)
people.role: First chief judge and high priest, son of Alma
match: (?<!valley (?:of )?|father,? |sons of |who was the son of |servant, |complain to )\bAlma\b(?! laid|, who was the founder)
people.summary: Alma was the son of Alma the elder. In his youth he fought against the church.
people.detail: An angel stopped him, and he changed. He became the first chief judge and high priest. He then gave up the judgment seat to preach.

refs.note: Young Alma is a wicked and idolatrous man.
An angel appears to Alma and the sons of Mosiah.
Alma becomes the first chief judge.
Alma gives the judgment seat to another man.

scholarship.text: Alma may come from a Hebrew word for youth or young man.
Ancient records from Ebla and the Bar Kokhba period show similar names for men.

people.name: Helam (Alma’s first convert)
people.role: One of the first people Alma baptized
people.summary: Helam was one of the first believers to follow Alma. Alma baptized him in the waters of Mormon.
people.detail: Both men went under the water and came out rejoicing. Alma’s people later named a land Helam.

refs.note: Alma baptizes Helam.
Both Alma and Helam are buried in the water.
Alma’s people call their land Helam.

people.name: Amulon
people.summary: Amulon led the priests of King Noah after they fled. They joined the Lamanites.
people.detail: The Lamanite king made him ruler over Alma’s people. He forbade them to pray aloud. His descendants later became the Amulonites.

refs.note: Amulon leads the former priests.
Amulon knew Alma as one of the king’s priests.
Amulon orders death for anyone who calls on God.
Most of Amulon’s seed are slain.

scholarship.text: The root of Amulon may be the Hebrew ʿml, meaning toil. The full meaning is unclear.

people.name: Sons of Mosiah
people.summary: The sons of Mosiah were Ammon, Aaron, Omner, and Himni. With young Alma, they fought the church.
people.detail: An angel stopped them, and they changed. They refused the kingdom and preached to the Lamanites for fourteen years.

refs.note: The text names the four sons.
They want salvation declared to every creature.
Alma meets them after their mission.
They taught the Lamanites for fourteen years.

people.name: Ammon (son of Mosiah)
people.summary: Ammon was a son of King Mosiah. He preached to the Lamanites in the land of Ishmael.
people.detail: He served King Lamoni and defended the king’s flocks. Many Lamanites believed. The converts were later called the people of Ammon.

refs.note: Ammon is named as a son of Mosiah.
Ammon becomes a servant to King Lamoni.
Ammon will not boast of himself, but of his God.
The converts are called the people of Ammon.

scholarship.text: Ammon may be a short name built on a Semitic kinship word. Other roots are also proposed.

people.name: Aaron (son of Mosiah)
people.summary: Aaron was a son of King Mosiah. The people wanted him as king, but he refused.
people.detail: He was put in prison in Middoni. He later taught the father of King Lamoni, who believed.

refs.note: Aaron will not take the kingdom.
Aaron and some of his brethren are cast into prison.
Aaron goes in to the king of the Lamanites.

people.name: Omner
people.role: Son of Mosiah and missionary to the Lamanites
people.summary: Omner was a son of King Mosiah. He preached among the Lamanites with his brothers.
people.detail: He later went with Alma to teach the Zoramites.

refs.note: Omner is named as a son of Mosiah.
Alma takes Omner to the Zoramites.

people.name: Himni
people.role: Son of Mosiah and missionary to the Lamanites
people.summary: Himni was a son of King Mosiah. He preached among the Lamanites with his brothers.
people.detail: Alma later left him to serve the church in Zarahemla.

refs.note: Himni is named as a son of Mosiah.
Himni stays in the church in Zarahemla.

scholarship.text: A seal from Megiddo shows a similar name, ḥmn. The meaning is still uncertain.

people.name: Interpreters (seer stones)
people.summary: The interpreters were two stones set in the rims of a bow. A seer used them to translate.
people.detail: Ammon told Limhi that King Mosiah could translate with them. Mosiah used them to read the Jaredite record. Alma later kept them.

refs.note: Ammon calls the things interpreters.
A seer is a revelator and a prophet also.
Mosiah translates with two stones fastened in a bow.
Alma says the interpreters were prepared to fulfill God’s word.

people.name: Twenty-four gold plates
people.summary: Limhi’s search party found twenty-four gold plates in a land full of bones. The plates held the Jaredite record.
people.detail: Mosiah translated them with the interpreters. Moroni later abridged them as the book of Ether.

refs.note: The search party brings back twenty-four plates of pure gold.
Mosiah translates the plates of gold.
Alma tells Helaman to keep the twenty-four plates.
Moroni takes his account from these plates.

people.name: Natural man
people.role: Benjamin’s term for fallen human nature
people.summary: King Benjamin said the natural man is an enemy to God. He must yield to the Holy Spirit.
people.detail: Benjamin teaches that a person becomes a saint through the atonement of Christ. The person becomes like a child.

refs.note: The natural man is an enemy to God.
Ammon asks what natural man knows these things.

people.name: Mary
people.summary: Mary is the mother of Jesus Christ. An angel told King Benjamin her name.
people.detail: Alma later calls her a virgin and a precious and chosen vessel.

refs.note: His mother shall be called Mary.
He shall be born of Mary at Jerusalem.

people.name: Reign of the judges
people.summary: The reign of the judges replaced the Nephite kings. The people chose judges by their voice.
people.detail: King Mosiah proposed it because a wicked king does great harm. The Nephites then dated their years by it.

refs.note: Mosiah tells the people to choose judges.
The voice of the people seldom desires wrong.
The reign of the judges begins.

people.name: Chief judge
people.role: Highest Nephite judge after the kings
people.summary: The chief judge held the highest office in the Nephite government after Mosiah. Alma was the first chief judge.
people.detail: The chief judge sat on the judgment seat. Lower judges could judge an unrighteous higher judge.

refs.note: Alma becomes the first chief judge.
Lower judges can judge unrighteous higher judges.

people.name: Nehor
people.summary: Nehor was a large and strong man who preached in Zarahemla. He taught that priests should be paid by the people.
people.detail: He also taught that all people would be saved. He killed the aged Gideon with a sword and was executed for the murder.

refs.note: Nehor teaches paid priestcraft and universal salvation.
He kills Gideon with the sword.
He confesses and dies on the hill Manti.
