scholarship.text: The name may relate to biblical Nahor. It may also depend on the Jaredite place name Nehor.

people.name: Order of Nehor
people.summary: The order of Nehor was the group that kept Nehor’s teachings after his death.
people.detail: Its members led the courts of Ammonihah. Many Amalekites and Amulonites also followed the order.

refs.note: The judge in Ammonihah follows the order of Nehor.
The Amalekites build synagogues after the order of the Nehors.
None of the order of Nehor joins the converts.

people.name: Amlici
people.role: Nephite who sought to be king
people.summary: Amlici was a cunning man who wanted to be king over the Nephites. He followed the order of Nehor.
people.detail: The voice of the people rejected him. His followers made him king anyway, and he led them to war. Alma killed him in battle.

refs.note: Amlici draws away many people.
The vote goes against him, but his followers crown him.
Alma kills Amlici with the sword.

scholarship.text: The name likely uses the Semitic root mlk, which means to reign. One proposal reads it as I reign.

people.name: Amlicites
people.summary: The Amlicites were the followers of Amlici. They joined the Lamanites to fight the Nephites.
people.detail: They marked their foreheads with red. The text says they brought the curse on themselves.

refs.note: The people of Amlici take the name Amlicites.
The Amlicites join a large Lamanite army.
The Amlicites mark themselves with red.

scholarship.text: In the printer’s manuscript, the name first appears as Amlikites. This suggests a hard c sound.
Royal Skousen proposes that the Amlicites and the Amalekites were one people.

people.name: Amnor
people.summary: Amnor was one of the spies that Alma sent to watch the Amlicite camp.

refs.note: Zeram, Amnor, Manti, and Limher watch the camp.

people.name: Limher
people.summary: Limher was one of the spies that Alma sent to watch the Amlicite camp.
people.detail: He and the other spies saw the Amlicites join a Lamanite army.

refs.note: Limher goes out with his men to watch.
The spies report the joined armies.

people.name: Zeram
people.summary: Zeram was one of the spies that Alma sent to watch the Amlicite camp.

refs.note: Zeram is the first spy named.

people.name: Nephihah (chief judge)
people.role: Second chief judge of the Nephites
people.summary: Nephihah was a wise elder of the church. Alma gave him the judgment-seat.
people.detail: Alma then gave all his time to preaching. Nephihah judged with perfect uprightness until his death.

refs.note: Alma chooses Nephihah as chief judge.
Alma gives up the judgment-seat to preach.
Nephihah dies, and he is called the second chief judge.

people.name: Amulek
people.summary: Amulek was a wealthy man of Ammonihah. An angel sent him to receive Alma into his home.
people.detail: He became Alma’s companion and a second witness. He lost his family and wealth for the gospel.

refs.note: Amulek feeds Alma at an angel’s word.
Amulek says he knew but would not know.
Amulek gives up his gold, his friends, and his family.
He teaches the infinite and eternal sacrifice.

scholarship.text: The name is probably a form of Mulek. The first a may come from the Hebrew article.

people.name: Giddonah (father of Amulek)
people.summary: Giddonah was the father of Amulek. He was the son of Ishmael.

refs.note: Amulek names his father Giddonah.

people.name: Ishmael (grandfather of Amulek)
people.summary: This Ishmael was the father of Giddonah and the grandfather of Amulek.
people.detail: He descended from Aminadi. He is not the Ishmael who came with Lehi.

refs.note: Amulek traces his line through Ishmael to Aminadi.

people.name: Aminadi
people.summary: Aminadi was an ancestor of Amulek. He descended from Nephi, the son of Lehi.
people.detail: He read the writing on the temple wall. The finger of God had written it.

refs.note: Aminadi interprets the writing on the wall.
Aminadi descends from Nephi.

people.name: Nephite money and measures
people.role: Units of gold, silver, and grain
people.summary: Alma 11 lists the Nephite units of gold and silver. Each unit equals a measure of grain.
people.detail: King Mosiah set these values. A judge earned one senine of gold for each day of work.

refs.note: A judge’s wage is a senine of gold for each day.
The text names the units and their values.
Zeezrom offers six onties of silver.

scholarship.text: Silver and barley form the core of the system, as in old Babylonia.
The laws of Eshnunna open with a similar list of silver and grain values.
John W. Welch sees the system as a way to pay the judges fairly.

people.name: Zeezrom
people.summary: Zeezrom was a skilled lawyer in Ammonihah. He tried to trap Amulek with questions.
people.detail: He offered Amulek six onties of silver to deny God. He then felt guilt, repented, and became a missionary.

refs.note: Zeezrom is the most expert lawyer.
He offers six onties of silver.
He sees his guilt and pleads for Alma and Amulek.
Alma heals and baptizes him.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads the name as he of the ezrom, a silver unit. It may hint at his love of money.

people.name: Antionah
people.summary: Antionah was a chief ruler in Ammonihah. He questioned Alma about the resurrection.
people.detail: He asked how a soul could never die. Adam and Eve could not eat from the tree of life.

refs.note: Antionah asks about the tree of life.

people.name: Melchizedek
people.role: King of Salem and high priest
people.summary: Melchizedek was king of Salem and a high priest. Abraham paid tithes to him.
people.detail: Alma uses him as an example of a high priest after the holy order. His people repented and had peace.

refs.note: Abraham pays tithes to Melchizedek.
He preaches repentance to a wicked people.
None were greater than he.

people.name: Noah (of the flood)
people.summary: Noah is the biblical patriarch who lived through the great flood.
people.detail: Amulek says the Lord will not destroy Ammonihah by flood, as in Noah’s days.

refs.note: Amulek recalls the people in the days of Noah.
The Lord swears the waters of Noah will not return.

people.name: Zoram (chief captain)
people.summary: Zoram was the chief captain of the Nephite armies. He had two sons, Lehi and Aha.
people.detail: He asked Alma where to find captives from Ammonihah. He followed the prophecy and freed them.

refs.note: Zoram and his sons ask Alma for guidance.
Zoram rescues the captives beyond Manti.

people.name: Aha
people.summary: Aha was a son of Zoram, the chief captain. His brother was named Lehi.

refs.note: Zoram goes to Alma with his sons Lehi and Aha.

people.name: Lamoni
people.role: Lamanite king over the land of Ishmael
people.summary: Lamoni was the Lamanite king over the land of Ishmael. He descended from Ishmael.
people.detail: Ammon served him and defended his flocks. Lamoni believed, fell as if dead, and woke praising the Redeemer.

refs.note: Ammon is brought before King Lamoni.
Lamoni prays for mercy and falls to the earth.
Lamoni rises and testifies of the Redeemer.
He refuses his father’s order to slay Ammon.

scholarship.text: John A. Tvedtnes and Robert F. Smith link the name to Laman. The ending may mean of Laman.

people.name: Queen of Lamoni
people.summary: The queen was the wife of King Lamoni. She believed Ammon when her husband lay as if dead.
people.detail: She too was overcome by the Spirit. Abish raised her by the hand.

refs.note: The queen asks Ammon to come to the king.
Ammon praises her great faith.
She rises and speaks many words.

people.name: Abish
people.summary: Abish was a Lamanite servant to the queen of Lamoni. She had been converted long before.
people.detail: Her father had seen a remarkable vision. She ran from house to house to gather the people.

refs.note: Abish knows the power of God and tells the people.
She hopes the people will believe.
She takes the queen by the hand.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads Abish as father is a man. Another reads it as a short form of Abishag.

people.name: Rabbanah
people.summary: Rabbanah is a title that Lamoni’s servants give to Ammon. The text interprets it as powerful or great king.

refs.note: A servant calls Ammon Rabbanah.

scholarship.text: The title likely comes from the Semitic root rbb, which means great.

people.name: Father of Lamoni
people.role: Lamanite king over all the land
match: \b(?:[Tt]he|old) king\b(?! of the land of Middoni| of the land[,;]| that he will cast)
people.summary: Lamoni’s father was the king over all the Lamanite lands. The text does not give his name.
people.detail: He tried to kill Ammon, but Ammon spared him. Aaron then taught him, and he gave away his sins to know God.

refs.note: The king meets Lamoni and Ammon on the road.
He offers half his kingdom for his life.
He offers to give away all his sins to know God.
He proclaims freedom for the preachers.

people.name: Muloki
people.summary: Muloki served with Aaron on the mission to the Lamanites. He was put in prison in Middoni.
people.detail: Ammon and Lamoni won his release. He preached in the village of Ani-Anti.

refs.note: Muloki is in prison with Aaron.
Aaron finds Muloki preaching in Ani-Anti.

people.name: Ammah
people.summary: Ammah served with Aaron on the mission to the Lamanites. He was put in prison in Middoni.

refs.note: Ammah is in prison with Aaron and Muloki.
Ammah preaches with his brethren in Ani-Anti.

people.name: Antiomno
people.summary: Antiomno was the king of the land of Middoni. He was a friend to Lamoni.

refs.note: Lamoni names Antiomno as his friend.
Aaron and his brothers come out of prison.

people.name: Amalekites
people.role: Nephite dissenters who lived among the Lamanites
people.summary: The Amalekites were Nephite dissenters who lived with the Lamanites. They built a city called Jerusalem.
people.detail: Many followed the order of Nehor. They stirred the Lamanites to attack the converts and later served as captains.

refs.note: Aaron preaches to the Amalekites in Jerusalem.
Few or none of them believe.
Amalekites serve as Lamanite chief captains.

scholarship.text: The text does not explain where the Amalekites came from.
The oldest surviving spelling is Amelicites. It differs from Amlicites by one letter.
Royal Skousen proposes that they were the Amlicites. Other scholars disagree.

people.name: Amulonites
people.role: Descendants of Amulon and the priests of Noah
people.summary: The Amulonites were the descendants of Amulon and the other priests of King Noah. They lived among the Lamanites.
people.detail: They joined the Amalekites against the converts. Few or none of them believed.

refs.note: The Amulonites help build Jerusalem.
None of them join the people of the Lord.
Most of the seed of Amulon die in battle.

people.name: Anti-Nephi-Lehi (king)
people.summary: Anti-Nephi-Lehi was a brother of Lamoni. His father gave him the kingdom before he died.
people.detail: He led his people to bury their swords. He thanked God for taking away their guilt.

refs.note: The old king names his son Anti-Nephi-Lehi.
He holds a council with Lamoni and Ammon.
He asks the people to bury their swords.

people.name: Anti-Nephi-Lehies (people of Ammon)
people.role: Lamanite converts who buried their weapons
people.summary: The Anti-Nephi-Lehies were Lamanites converted by the sons of Mosiah. They later took the name people of Ammon.
people.detail: They buried their weapons and would not fight, even to save their lives. The Nephites gave them the land of Jershon.

refs.note: The converts take the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies.
They bury their swords deep in the earth.
They are called the people of Ammon.
They nearly break their oath, but Helaman stops them.

people.name: Korihor
people.summary: Korihor was a man who preached against Christ. The text calls him an Anti-Christ.
people.detail: He taught that there would be no Christ and no sin. He asked for a sign, was struck dumb, and later died.

refs.note: Korihor comes to Zarahemla as an Anti-Christ.
He asks for a sign and is struck dumb.
He confesses that the devil deceived him.
The Zoramites trample him to death.

scholarship.text: John A. Tvedtnes links the name to the Jaredite name Corihor.
Hugh Nibley compared it with Herihor, an Egyptian priest who took a throne.

people.name: Giddonah (high priest)
people.role: High priest in the land of Gideon
people.summary: Giddonah was the high priest in the land of Gideon. He questioned Korihor.
people.detail: He sent Korihor bound to Alma and the chief judge.

refs.note: Korihor stands before Giddonah.
Giddonah sends Korihor to Zarahemla.

people.name: Zoram (Zoramite leader)
people.summary: Zoram was the leader of a people who separated from the Nephites. They took his name.
people.detail: He led them into Antionum and into false worship.

refs.note: The Zoramites follow a man named Zoram.
Zoram leads his people to bow to dumb idols.

people.name: Zoramites (of Alma’s day)
people.summary: The Zoramites were dissenters who followed Zoram. They lived in Antionum, east of Zarahemla.
people.detail: They prayed on the Rameumptom once a week. They cast out their poor, and later joined the Lamanites.

refs.note: They pervert the ways of the Lord.
They pray on the Rameumptom.
They cast the poor out of their synagogues.
They join the Lamanites.

people.name: Rameumptom
people.summary: The Rameumptom was a high stand in the Zoramite synagogues. The text says the name means the holy stand.
people.detail: Each person climbed it to say the same proud prayer. They did not speak of God again all week.

refs.note: The stand rises high above the head.
The Zoramites call the place Rameumptom.
They do not speak of God until the next week.

scholarship.text: Robert F. Smith proposes a Hebrew meaning like their high standing places.
The first part may come from rām, high. The second may come from ‘ōmed, standing place.

people.name: Helaman (son of Alma)
people.summary: Helaman was the eldest son of Alma the younger. He received the sacred records from his father.
people.detail: He led the church after Alma. In the war, he led two thousand young Ammonite soldiers.

refs.note: Alma gives Helaman the records.
Helaman sets the church in order.
He marches at the head of the young soldiers.
Helaman dies.

scholarship.text: Jo Ann Hackett proposes Hebrew ḥlm, to dream. The name may mean seer or visionary.

people.name: Gazelem
people.role: Name for a servant with a seer stone
people.summary: Gazelem is a name in a prophecy that Alma quotes. The Lord will give his servant Gazelem a stone.
people.detail: The stone will shine in darkness. It will bring secret works to light.

refs.note: The Lord prepares a stone for his servant Gazelem.
The interpreters will reveal secret works.

scholarship.text: One proposal ends the name with a dual form. It could fit the two stones of the interpreters.
A similar name, Gazelam, refers to Joseph Smith in Doctrine and Covenants 78:9.

people.name: Shiblon
people.summary: Shiblon was a son of Alma the younger. He served with his father among the Zoramites.
people.detail: He suffered bonds and stoning for the gospel. Later he kept the sacred records after Helaman.

refs.note: Alma praises Shiblon’s faithfulness.
Alma tells him to bridle his passions.
Shiblon takes the sacred records.

scholarship.text: Jo Ann Hackett links it to words for ear of grain or path. A less likely proposal reads lion cub.

people.name: Corianton
people.summary: Corianton was a son of Alma the younger. He served with his father among the Zoramites.
people.detail: He left his mission for the harlot Isabel. Alma taught him about justice, mercy, and the resurrection.

refs.note: Alma rebukes Corianton for leaving the ministry.
Alma teaches him the plan of mercy.
Corianton preaches with his brothers.
He goes to the land northward by ship.

scholarship.text: John A. Tvedtnes links the name to Akkadian gārium, which means opponent.

people.name: Isabel
people.role: Harlot in the land of Siron
people.summary: Isabel was a harlot in the land of Siron. She led away the hearts of many.

refs.note: Corianton goes after the harlot Isabel.

scholarship.text: The name may be a form of Jezebel.

people.name: Moroni (chief captain)
people.role: Chief captain of the Nephite armies
people.summary: Moroni was chief captain of the Nephite armies. He took command at age twenty-five.
people.detail: He armed his people with armor and forts. He raised the title of liberty. Mormon later named his son after him.

refs.note: Moroni becomes chief captain at twenty-five.
He makes the title of liberty.
The text praises men like unto Moroni.
He gives command to his son Moronihah.

scholarship.text: One proposal links Moroni to the Jaredite place Moron. Another reads West Semitic mr’, lord.

people.name: Zerahemnah
people.summary: Zerahemnah led the Lamanite armies against the Nephites. He chose Amalekites and Zoramites as his captains.
people.detail: Moroni surrounded his army at the river Sidon. He swore an oath of peace after he lost his scalp.

refs.note: Zerahemnah appoints Amalekite and Zoramite captains.
A soldier cuts off his scalp.
He swears a covenant of peace.

scholarship.text: Jo Ann Hackett suggests a confusion with Zarahemla. Others propose seed meanings from Hebrew zera‘.

people.name: Lehi (Nephite commander)
people.summary: Lehi was a Nephite captain who served with Moroni in most of his battles.
people.detail: He led a hidden army at the river Sidon. The Lamanites feared him greatly.

refs.note: Lehi’s army attacks from the rear.
Lehi commands the city, and the Lamanites fear him.
He is like Moroni and rejoices in his safety.

people.name: Amalickiah
people.role: Nephite dissenter who became Lamanite king
people.summary: Amalickiah was a large and strong Nephite who wanted to be king. He led many dissenters.
people.detail: He fled to the Lamanites and seized their throne by treachery. Teancum killed him in his tent.

refs.note: Amalickiah seeks to be king.
He marries the queen and takes the kingdom.
Teancum kills him with a javelin.

scholarship.text: John W. Welch suggests the ironic meaning Yahweh is king, for a man who made himself king.

people.name: Amalickiahites
people.summary: The Amalickiahites were the followers of Amalickiah. Moroni put to death those who would not support freedom.

refs.note: Moroni marches against the Amalickiahites.
Most of them covenant to keep freedom.

people.name: Title of liberty
people.summary: The title of liberty was a banner that Moroni made from his torn coat.
people.detail: It asked the people to defend their God, religion, freedom, peace, wives, and children. Supporters made a covenant and tore their own garments.

refs.note: Moroni writes on a piece of his coat.
The people covenant and tear their garments.
Moroni raises the title on every tower.

scholarship.text: Moroni quotes a story of Jacob and Joseph’s coat. The story is not in the Bible.
The War Scroll from the Dead Sea Scrolls also describes battle banners with writing.
Kerry Hull compares the title with Mesoamerican war banners.

people.name: Christians
people.summary: Christians was the name that unbelievers gave to the followers of Christ.
people.detail: The believers took the name gladly. Moroni prayed for the land of the Christians.

refs.note: Moroni prays for the cause of the Christians.
Believers are called Christians.
Moroni defends the cause of the Christians.

people.name: Lehonti
people.summary: Lehonti led Lamanites who refused the king’s order to go to war.
people.detail: He gave his army to Amalickiah. Amalickiah then had him poisoned by degrees.

refs.note: Lehonti leads the army on mount Antipas.
He agrees to meet Amalickiah.
A servant poisons Lehonti.

people.name: Queen of the Lamanites
people.role: Wife of the murdered Lamanite king
people.summary: The queen was the wife of the Lamanite king. Amalickiah’s servants killed her husband.
people.detail: Amalickiah blamed the king’s servants. He then won the queen’s favor and married her.

refs.note: The queen hears of the king’s death.
Amalickiah takes her as his wife.

people.name: Teancum
people.summary: Teancum was a Nephite captain under Moroni. He was a great warrior.
people.detail: He killed Amalickiah and later Ammoron in their tents. He died after he killed Ammoron.

refs.note: Teancum stops the people of Morianton.
He kills Amalickiah at night.
He kills Ammoron and is slain.
Moroni and Lehi mourn him.

scholarship.text: The -nc- sound may point to a Jaredite name, as in Moriancumer.

people.name: Morianton (leader)
people.role: Leader of the people of Morianton
people.summary: Morianton led the people of the land of Morianton. He was a man of much passion.
people.detail: He beat one of his maid servants. He tried to lead his people into the land northward, but Teancum killed him.

refs.note: Morianton plans to flee northward.
He beats his maid servant.
Teancum kills Morianton.

people.name: Pahoran (the first)
people.summary: Pahoran was the son of Nephihah. He followed his father as chief judge.
people.detail: King-men drove him from Zarahemla. He answered Moroni’s angry letter with meekness, and they joined forces.

refs.note: Pahoran becomes chief judge.
He says he is not angry with Moroni.
Pahoran returns to the judgment-seat.

scholarship.text: The Amarna letters name an Egyptian official Pahura in Palestine. One proposal links the names.

people.name: King-men
people.summary: The king-men wanted to change the law and set up a king. They were of high birth.
people.detail: They refused to fight the Lamanites. Moroni forced them to defend their country.

refs.note: The king-men want to overthrow the free government.
Moroni compels them to fight.
King-men who will not defend the land die.

people.name: Freemen
people.summary: The freemen wanted to keep Pahoran as chief judge and the free government.

refs.note: The freemen keep their rights and religion.
The voice of the people favors the freemen.

people.name: Ammoron
people.summary: Ammoron was the brother of Amalickiah. He became Lamanite king after Amalickiah died.
people.detail: He traded angry letters with Moroni. He claimed descent from Zoram. Teancum killed him at night.

refs.note: Ammoron becomes king.
His letter to Moroni.
Teancum kills Ammoron.

people.name: Jacob (Zoramite captain)
people.summary: Jacob was a Zoramite who led the Lamanite army in the city of Mulek.
people.detail: Moroni drew him out of the city with a trap. Jacob died in the battle.

refs.note: Jacob leads the army at Mulek.
He fights with an unconquerable spirit.
Jacob is killed.

people.name: Laman (servant of the king)
people.summary: Laman was a servant of the Lamanite king that Amalickiah murdered. He later joined the Nephites.
people.detail: Moroni sent him with wine to the Lamanite guards at Gid. The guards got drunk, and the Nephite prisoners were freed.

refs.note: Moroni finds Laman among his men.
Laman offers wine to the guards.
Laman reports that the guards sleep.

people.name: Stripling warriors
match: \b(?:my|his|these) (?:little band of )?two thousand(?: and sixty)?(?: sons| young men)?\b
people.summary: The stripling warriors were two thousand young sons of the Anti-Nephi-Lehies. Helaman led them in war.
people.detail: Their fathers had sworn never to fight. The sons had not, so they took up arms. None of them died.

refs.note: The young men covenant and choose Helaman.
Their mothers taught them faith.
None of them is slain.

scholarship.text: The text does not give their ages. Some scholars think they were about twenty.
Helaman calls them very young. One proposal places some near twelve to fifteen.

people.name: Antipus
people.summary: Antipus commanded the Nephite army in the city of Judea. Helaman’s young soldiers joined him.
people.detail: He died in battle near the city of Antiparah.

refs.note: Helaman joins Antipus at Judea.
Antipus falls by the sword.

people.name: Gid (Nephite captain)
people.summary: Gid was a Nephite captain under Helaman. He guarded Lamanite prisoners on the way to Zarahemla.
people.detail: He and Teomner later hid in the wilderness and took the city of Manti.

refs.note: Gid reports on the prisoners.
Gid hides with a small army.
Gid and Teomner cut off the Lamanite spies.

people.name: Teomner
people.summary: Teomner was a Nephite captain under Helaman. He helped take the city of Manti.

refs.note: Teomner hides with a small army.
Gid and Teomner take the strongholds.

people.name: Pachus
people.summary: Pachus led the king-men who took Zarahemla from Pahoran. They made him king.
people.detail: He made an alliance with the Lamanite king. He died when Moroni and Pahoran took back the city.

refs.note: Pahoran tells Moroni of the revolt.
Pachus is king of the dissenters.
Pachus is slain.

people.name: Pahoran (the second)
people.role: Nephite chief judge, son of Pahoran
people.summary: Pahoran was a son of the chief judge Pahoran. The people chose him as the next chief judge.
people.detail: His brothers Paanchi and Pacumeni also wanted the seat. Kishkumen murdered him on the judgment seat.

refs.note: Three sons of Pahoran contend for the judgment seat.
The voice of the people appoints Pahoran.
Kishkumen murders Pahoran on the judgment seat.

people.name: Paanchi
people.summary: Paanchi was a son of the chief judge Pahoran. He lost the contest for the judgment seat.
people.detail: He planned a rebellion against his brother. The people condemned him to death for it.

refs.note: Paanchi contends for the judgment seat.
Paanchi is about to lead a rebellion.
The people condemn him to death.

scholarship.text: One proposal reads Paanchi as an Egyptian name. It may mean the living one.
Hugh Nibley linked it to the name of an Egyptian pharaoh. Later readings of that pharaoh’s name weaken the link.

people.name: Pacumeni
people.summary: Pacumeni was a son of the chief judge Pahoran. He became chief judge after his brother died.
people.detail: He accepted the choice of the people at first. Coriantumr killed him when the Lamanites took Zarahemla.

refs.note: Pacumeni unites with the people when he loses the seat.
The people appoint Pacumeni as chief judge.
Coriantumr kills Pacumeni by the city wall.

scholarship.text: Proposals for Pacumeni include Egyptian roots. Hugh Nibley compared an Egyptian name that may mean blind man.

people.name: Kishkumen
people.summary: Kishkumen murdered the chief judge Pahoran. A secret band then protected him.
people.detail: A servant of Helaman stabbed him on the way to murder Helaman. Gadianton then took his band into the wilderness.

refs.note: Kishkumen murders Pahoran.
Kishkumen waits to destroy Helaman also.
The servant of Helaman stabs Kishkumen.

scholarship.text: Hugh Nibley compared the kumen part of the name with Kumani, an ancient city name.

people.name: Tubaloth
people.summary: Tubaloth was the king of the Lamanites. He was the son of Ammoron.
people.detail: He sent Coriantumr to attack the Nephites during their contention.

refs.note: Tubaloth, son of Ammoron, appoints Coriantumr.

people.name: Coriantumr (the Nephite dissenter)
people.summary: Coriantumr was a descendant of Zarahemla and a Nephite dissenter. He led a Lamanite army.
people.detail: He took the city of Zarahemla and killed Pacumeni. Moronihah then defeated his army.

refs.note: Coriantumr leads the Lamanites as a dissenter.
He enters the city of Zarahemla.
Moronihah heads off the retreating army.

people.name: Moronihah (son of Moroni)
people.summary: Moronihah was the son of the captain Moroni. He took command of the Nephite armies.
people.detail: He retook Zarahemla from Coriantumr. Later he regained half of the lands the Nephites had lost.

refs.note: Moroni gives his armies to his son Moronihah.
Moronihah retakes the city of Zarahemla.
Moronihah leads the repentant people back to battle.

people.name: Helaman (son of Helaman)
people.role: Nephite chief judge and record keeper
people.summary: Helaman was the son of Helaman and grandson of Alma. He became chief judge.
people.detail: His servant saved him from Kishkumen. He named his sons Nephi and Lehi after their first parents.

refs.note: Helaman, son of Helaman, becomes chief judge.
Helaman judges with justice and equity.
He gives his sons the names of their first parents.

people.name: Gadianton
people.role: Founder of a band of robbers
people.summary: Gadianton was skilled with words and in craft. He became the leader of Kishkumen’s band.
people.detail: He wanted the judgment seat. Mormon says his band later almost destroyed the Nephites.

refs.note: Gadianton becomes the leader of the band.
Gadianton flees with his band into the wilderness.
Mormon says Gadianton nearly overthrew the Nephites.

scholarship.text: John W. Welch proposed a link to the Hebrew root gdd, used for bands of raiders.
That root does not explain the end of the name. Other proposals are called unlikely.

people.name: Gadianton robbers
people.role: Secret band of robbers and murderers
people.summary: The Gadianton robbers were a secret band named after Gadianton. They used oaths to hide murder and theft.
people.detail: They took the judgment seats in Helaman’s time. Nephites and Lamanites joined to defeat them in 3 Nephi.

refs.note: Kishkumen and Gadianton formed the band.
The Lamanites hunt down the robbers of Gadianton.
The robbers become numerous and attack the people.
The robbers spread over the land again.

people.name: Nephi (son of Helaman)
match: (?<!(?:father|plates of|book of|land of|city of|people of|children of|descendant of) )\bNephi\b(?!-| also testified)
people.summary: Nephi was the eldest son of Helaman. He served as chief judge, then gave up the seat to preach.
people.detail: The Lord gave him the sealing power. He asked for a famine to turn the people from war.

refs.note: Nephi begins to reign after Helaman dies.
Nephi gives up the judgment seat to preach.
The Lord gives Nephi power to seal on earth.
Nephi asks the Lord for a famine.

people.name: Lehi (son of Helaman)
people.summary: Lehi was the younger son of Helaman. He preached with his brother Nephi.
people.detail: Lamanites put the brothers in prison. A fire encircled them there, and many Lamanites converted.

refs.note: Helaman names his younger son Lehi.
Nephi and Lehi are encircled by fire.
Lehi is not behind his brother in righteousness.

people.name: Aminadab
people.role: Nephite dissenter in a Lamanite prison
people.summary: Aminadab was a Nephite by birth who had left the church. He was at the prison with the Lamanites.
people.detail: He saw Nephi and Lehi talk with angels. He told the people to repent and pray.

refs.note: Aminadab says the brothers converse with angels.
Aminadab tells them to repent and cry to the Lord.

people.name: Cezoram
people.summary: Cezoram became chief judge when Nephi gave up the seat.
people.detail: An unknown hand murdered him on the judgment seat. His son was murdered after him.

refs.note: Nephi gives the judgment seat to Cezoram.
Cezoram is murdered on the judgment seat.
The robbers murdered Cezoram and his son.

people.name: Cain
people.summary: Cain was a son of Adam in the Bible. He murdered his brother Abel.
people.detail: Mormon and Moroni trace secret plots for power back to Cain.

refs.note: The devil plotted with Cain to hide the murder of Abel.
Secret oaths came down from Cain.

people.name: Abel
people.role: Son of Adam, brother of Cain
people.summary: Abel was a son of Adam in the Bible. His brother Cain murdered him.

refs.note: Mormon names the murder of Abel.

people.name: Ezias
people.summary: Ezias was a prophet whose words Nephi cites. The Bible does not name him.
people.detail: Nephi lists him with Zenos, Zenock, and Isaiah as witnesses of Christ.

refs.note: Nephi names Ezias among the prophets.

people.name: Seezoram
people.summary: Seezoram was the chief judge in Nephi’s time. His brother Seantum murdered him.
people.detail: Nephi revealed the murder as a sign that he was a prophet.

refs.note: The judges accuse Nephi of the murder of Seezoram.
Nephi names Seantum as the murderer of his brother.

people.name: Seantum
people.summary: Seantum was the brother of the chief judge Seezoram. He murdered him.
people.detail: Nephi told the people to find blood on his cloak. Seantum then confessed.

refs.note: Nephi sends them to the house of Seantum.
The people find it as Nephi said.

people.name: Samuel the Lamanite
people.summary: Samuel was a Lamanite prophet who preached in Zarahemla. He stood on the city wall to prophesy.
people.detail: He foretold signs of the birth and death of Christ. Arrows and stones could not hit him.

refs.note: Samuel prophesies from the wall.
He foretells a night with no darkness.
Arrows and stones cannot hit him.
Jesus asks why one of Samuel’s prophecies is missing.

scholarship.text: S. Kent Brown reads two laments in Samuel’s sermon. He compares them to biblical laments.

people.name: Lachoneus
people.summary: Lachoneus was the chief judge and governor when Christ was born.
people.detail: He refused Giddianhi’s demand to surrender. He gathered the people into one place to resist the robbers.

refs.note: Lachoneus is the chief judge in the year of the sign.
Mormon calls Lachoneus a just man.
His call gathers the people together.

scholarship.text: One proposal links Lachoneus to a Greek word for Spartan. The source word is hypothetical.

people.name: Lachoneus (the son)
people.summary: Lachoneus was the son of the governor Lachoneus. He took his father’s seat.

refs.note: Lachoneus fills the seat of his father.

people.name: Nephi (son of Nephi, disciple)
match: (?<!(?:plates of|land of|city of|people of) )\bNephi\b(?!-|, the son of Helaman|, who was the father)
people.summary: Nephi was the son of Nephi and grandson of Helaman. He kept the records after his father.
people.detail: He prayed all day before the sign of Christ’s birth. He was the first disciple Jesus called in Bountiful.

refs.note: Nephi keeps the records after his father leaves.
Nephi prays all day for his people.
Jesus calls Nephi forth.
Nephi heads the list of the twelve disciples.

people.name: Giddianhi
people.summary: Giddianhi was the governor of the Gadianton robbers. He wrote a threatening letter to Lachoneus.
people.detail: He demanded that the Nephites join his band. He died in battle as his army retreated.

refs.note: Giddianhi names himself governor of the secret society.
His armies come girded with lambskins.
The Nephites overtake and slay Giddianhi.

people.name: Gidgiddoni
people.summary: Gidgiddoni was the chief captain of the Nephites under Lachoneus. Mormon calls him a great prophet.
people.detail: He refused to attack the robbers in their mountains. He waited for them to come to the people.

refs.note: Gidgiddoni is chosen as chief captain.
He will not go up against the robbers.
He sees through the robbers’ plan to withdraw.

scholarship.text: John Gee compared Gidgiddoni with similar personal names from ancient Assyria.

people.name: Zemnarihah
people.summary: Zemnarihah led the robbers after Giddianhi died. He laid siege to the gathered Nephites.
people.detail: The siege failed when the robbers ran out of food. The Nephites captured him and hanged him on a tree.

refs.note: The robbers appoint Zemnarihah as their leader.
Zemnarihah orders a march away.
He is hanged, and the tree is cut down.

scholarship.text: One KnoWhy compares the felled tree with later Jewish rules for hangings.
Those rules had the tree buried with the body. The article reads the act as a curse on rebels.

people.name: Jacob (king of the secret band)
people.role: King of a band of dissenters
people.summary: Jacob was the king of a secret combination after the government fell.
people.detail: He led his band to the north to build a kingdom. The Lord later burned the city of Jacobugath.

refs.note: The secret combination places Jacob at its head.
Jacob leads his people to the north.
The people of king Jacob die in the burned city.

people.name: The twelve disciples
match: \btwelve(?=\)| whom (?!Jesus chose to be his disciples in the land of Jerusalem)| did teach)
people.summary: Jesus chose twelve disciples among the Nephites. He gave them power to baptize.
people.detail: They taught the people. Mormon says they will also judge the people.

refs.note: The called disciples number twelve.
The names of the twelve disciples.
The twelve teach the multitude.
Jesus gives the twelve power to give the Holy Ghost.

people.name: Timothy
people.summary: Timothy was the brother of the disciple Nephi. Nephi raised him from the dead.

refs.note: Timothy is named among the disciples.
Nephi raises his brother from the dead.

people.name: Jonas (son of Nephi)
people.summary: Jonas was the son of the disciple Nephi. He was one of the twelve disciples.

refs.note: Jonas, son of Nephi, is named among the disciples.

people.name: Jonas (the second disciple)
people.summary: This Jonas was a second disciple with that name. The text gives no more about him.

refs.note: A second Jonas is named among the disciples.

people.name: Mathoni
people.summary: Mathoni was one of the twelve disciples. His brother Mathonihah was also a disciple.

refs.note: Mathoni is named among the disciples.

people.name: Mathonihah
people.summary: Mathonihah was one of the twelve disciples. He was the brother of Mathoni.

refs.note: Mathonihah is named with his brother.

people.name: Kumen
people.summary: Kumen was one of the twelve disciples.

refs.note: Kumen is named among the disciples.

people.name: Kumenonhi
people.summary: Kumenonhi was one of the twelve disciples.

refs.note: Kumenonhi is named among the disciples.

people.name: Jeremiah (the disciple)
people.summary: This Jeremiah was one of the twelve disciples. He is not the Bible prophet.

refs.note: Jeremiah is named among the disciples.

people.name: Shemnon
people.summary: Shemnon was one of the twelve disciples.

refs.note: Shemnon is named among the disciples.

people.name: Zedekiah (the disciple)
people.summary: This Zedekiah was one of the twelve disciples. He is not the king of Judah.

refs.note: Zedekiah is named among the disciples.

people.name: Isaiah (the disciple)
people.summary: This Isaiah was one of the twelve disciples. He is not the Bible prophet.

refs.note: Isaiah is the last disciple named.

people.name: Samuel (the Bible prophet)
people.summary: Samuel was a prophet in the Bible. Jesus names him first among the prophets.

refs.note: All the prophets from Samuel testified of Christ.

people.name: Malachi
people.summary: Malachi was the last prophet in the Old Testament. Jesus gave his words to the Nephites.
people.detail: The Nephites did not have these words before.

refs.note: Jesus commands them to write the words of Malachi.
Jesus says they did not have these scriptures.

people.name: Elijah
people.summary: Elijah was a prophet in the Bible. Malachi foretold that the Lord would send him again.

refs.note: The Lord will send Elijah before the great day.
He will turn the hearts of fathers and children.

people.name: The Three Nephites
people.role: Disciples who did not taste death
people.summary: Three of the twelve disciples asked to stay on earth until Jesus comes again. Jesus granted it.
people.detail: Mormon was forbidden to write their names. Moroni says that he and his father saw them.

refs.note: Jesus says they will never taste of death.
Mormon may not write their names.
Moroni says his father and he have seen them.

people.name: Mormon
people.role: Nephite prophet, general, and editor of the record
people.summary: Mormon was a Nephite prophet and the last great general of his people. He abridged the records into one book.
people.detail: He was named after the land of Mormon. He led the armies at sixteen and hid the records in Cumorah.

refs.note: Mormon prepares to give the record to Moroni.
Mormon is named after the land of Mormon.
He leads the Nephite armies at sixteen.
He hides the records in the hill Cumorah.

scholarship.text: Proposals for the name include Egyptian roots meaning beloved. None is settled.
An 1843 letter said Mormon means more good. The entry calls this a metaphor, not a translation.

people.name: Nephi (author of 4 Nephi)
people.summary: This Nephi was the son of the disciple Nephi. He kept the record in the time of peace.
people.detail: The book of 4 Nephi carries his name. His son Amos kept the record after him.

refs.note: Nephi dies, and his son Amos keeps the record.

people.name: Amos (son of Nephi)
people.summary: Amos was the son of Nephi, the author of 4 Nephi. He kept the record for eighty-four years.

refs.note: Amos keeps the record after his father.
Amos dies, and his son Amos keeps it.

people.name: Amos (son of Amos)
people.summary: Amos was the son of Amos. He kept the record as pride and division returned.
people.detail: His brother Ammaron kept the record after him.

refs.note: Amos keeps the record after his father.
Amos dies, and Ammaron keeps the record.

people.name: Ammaron
people.summary: Ammaron was the brother of Amos. He hid the sacred records in the land Antum.
people.detail: He told the boy Mormon where to find the records. He chose Mormon as the next keeper.

refs.note: Ammaron hides up the sacred records.
Ammaron speaks to Mormon at about ten years old.
He names the hill Shim in the land Antum.

people.name: Mormon (father of Mormon)
people.summary: The prophet Mormon says his father was also named Mormon.
people.detail: He took his son to the land of Zarahemla.

refs.note: Mormon gives his father’s name.
His father carries him to Zarahemla.

people.name: Aaron (Lamanite king)
people.summary: Aaron was a king of the Lamanites in Mormon’s time. Mormon defeated his army.
people.detail: Mormon’s letter in Moroni 9 names an army of Aaron. It may be the same man.

refs.note: Aaron attacks with forty-four thousand men.
Prisoners suffer in the army of Aaron.

people.name: Moroni (son of Mormon)
people.role: Last Nephite prophet and record keeper
people.summary: Moroni was the son of Mormon. He finished his father’s record after the last battle.
people.detail: He abridged the Jaredite record and wrote the book of Moroni. He then sealed up the records.

refs.note: Moroni leads ten thousand men at Cumorah.
Moroni finishes the record of his father.
He finishes the Jaredite account and keeps writing.
He invites readers to ask God if the record is true.

scholarship.text: One proposal links Moroni to the Jaredite place Moron. Others suggest Semitic or Egyptian roots.

people.name: Gidgiddonah
people.summary: Gidgiddonah led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Gidgiddonah falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Lamah
people.summary: Lamah led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Lamah falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Gilgal (Nephite commander)
people.summary: Gilgal led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Gilgal falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Limhah
people.summary: Limhah led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Limhah falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Jeneum
people.summary: Jeneum led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Jeneum falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Cumenihah
people.summary: Cumenihah led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Cumenihah falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Moronihah (commander at Cumorah)
people.summary: This Moronihah led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He is not the earlier captain.

refs.note: Moronihah falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Antionum (Nephite commander)
people.summary: Antionum led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Antionum falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Shiblom (Nephite commander)
people.summary: This Shiblom led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Shiblom falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Shem (Nephite commander)
people.summary: Shem led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Shem falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Josh (Nephite commander)
people.summary: Josh led ten thousand Nephites in the last battle. He fell with them.

refs.note: Josh falls with his ten thousand.

people.name: Jared
people.summary: Jared led his family from the great tower to the promised land. The Jaredites descend from him and his brother.
people.detail: He asked his brother to pray that their language would not be confused. He agreed to let the people have a king.

refs.note: Jared asks his brother to cry unto the Lord.
The Lord does not confound their language.
Jared lets the people choose a king.

scholarship.text: Jared may share the Hebrew root yrd, to go down. All Jaredite name roots stay speculative.

people.name: Brother of Jared
people.summary: The brother of Jared was a large and mighty man and a prophet. He led the journey with Jared.
people.detail: He built barges and asked the Lord to touch sixteen stones. He saw the finger of the Lord and then the Lord himself.

refs.note: He is a large and mighty man, highly favored.
The Lord touches the stones, and he sees the finger.
The Lord shows himself to him.
By faith he moved the mountain Zerin.

scholarship.text: Later reports name him Mahonri Moriancumer. The name does not appear in the text.
Moriancumer is the name of their camp by the sea in Ether 2:13.

people.name: Jaredites
people.role: People descended from Jared and his brother
people.summary: The Jaredites came to the promised land from the great tower. The book of Ether tells their history.
people.detail: They became a great nation. Secret combinations and war destroyed them, as Ether had warned.

refs.note: Jared and his brother leave the great tower.
They land on the shore of the promised land.
Mormon fears the Nephites will end like the Jaredites.

people.name: Deseret
people.summary: Deseret is a Jaredite word. The text says it means a honey bee.
people.detail: The Jaredites carried swarms of bees on their journey.

refs.note: They carry deseret, which means honey bee.

scholarship.text: Hugh Nibley compared an Egyptian word for the red crown, linked with the bee.
Other proposals compare Semitic words for bee. Jaredite roots remain speculative.

people.name: Nimrod (the mighty hunter)
people.summary: Nimrod was a mighty hunter in the Bible. The Jaredites passed through a valley named after him.

refs.note: The valley of Nimrod is named after the mighty hunter.
The Lord talks with the brother of Jared there.

people.name: Jaredite barges
people.summary: The Jaredites built eight barges to cross the sea. They were tight like a dish.
people.detail: Stones gave them light inside. A wind drove them for 344 days to the promised land.

refs.note: The Lord tells them to build barges.
The barges are tight like a dish.
They spend 344 days on the water.

people.name: Sixteen stones
people.summary: The brother of Jared made sixteen clear stones from a rock. He asked the Lord to touch them.
people.detail: The Lord touched them, and they shone. One went in each end of every barge.

refs.note: He moltens sixteen small stones on the mount.
The Lord touches the stones one by one.
The stones give light in the vessels.

people.name: Jacom
people.summary: Jacom was a son of Jared. He refused to become king.

refs.note: Jared’s four sons are named.
All the sons of Jared refuse but one.

people.name: Gilgah
people.summary: Gilgah was a son of Jared. He refused to become king.

refs.note: Jared’s four sons are named.

people.name: Mahah
people.summary: Mahah was a son of Jared. He refused to become king.

refs.note: Jared’s four sons are named.

people.name: Pagag
people.role: Firstborn son of the brother of Jared
people.summary: Pagag was the firstborn son of the brother of Jared. He refused to be king.

refs.note: Pagag refuses the kingdom.
His brothers refuse also.

people.name: Orihah
people.role: First Jaredite king, son of Jared
people.summary: Orihah was a son of Jared. He became the first Jaredite king.
people.detail: He walked humbly before the Lord. He had thirty-one children.

refs.note: Orihah is anointed king.
Orihah walks humbly before the Lord.
He has thirty-one children.

people.name: Kib
people.summary: Kib was a son of Orihah and became king. His son Corihor rebelled and took him captive.
people.detail: His son Shule won back the kingdom for him.

refs.note: Kib reigns after Orihah.
Kib dwells in captivity.
Kib gives the kingdom to Shule.

people.name: Corihor (son of Kib)
people.summary: Corihor was a son of Kib. He rebelled against his father and took him captive.
people.detail: His brother Shule defeated him. Corihor later repented.

refs.note: Corihor rebels and draws away many people.
Shule defeats Corihor.
Corihor repents.

people.name: Shule
people.summary: Shule was a son of Kib. He made steel swords and won back his father’s kingdom.
people.detail: Noah later took him captive, but his sons freed him. He punished those who reviled the prophets.

refs.note: Shule makes swords of steel.
His sons free him from Noah.
Shule judges those who revile the prophets.

people.name: Noah (Jaredite)
people.summary: Noah was a son of Corihor. He rebelled against King Shule and held him captive.
people.detail: Shule’s sons killed Noah by night.

refs.note: Noah rebels against Shule.
The sons of Shule slay Noah.

people.name: Cohor (son of Noah)
people.summary: Cohor was a son of Noah. He ruled one of two kingdoms.
people.detail: He led his people to battle against Shule. Shule won and killed Cohor.

refs.note: The land splits into two kingdoms.
Cohor gives battle to Shule.

people.name: Nimrod (son of Cohor)
people.summary: Nimrod was a son of Cohor. He gave his father’s kingdom to Shule.

refs.note: Nimrod gives up the kingdom of Cohor.

people.name: Omer
people.summary: Omer was a son of Shule and became king. His son Jared took him captive.
people.detail: The Lord warned him in a dream to flee. He later returned and anointed Emer.

refs.note: Omer reigns after Shule.
The Lord warns Omer in a dream.
Omer is restored to his land.

people.name: Jared (son of Omer)
people.summary: Jared was a son of Omer. He rebelled against his father to take the kingdom.
people.detail: His daughter suggested the old secret oaths. Akish later murdered him on the throne.

refs.note: Jared rebels against his father.
Jared offers his daughter to Akish.
Jared is murdered on his throne.

people.name: Daughter of Jared
people.role: Daughter of Jared, son of Omer
people.summary: The daughter of Jared revived the secret oaths of old. She danced to win Akish for her father.
people.detail: She became the wife of Akish. Her plan brought back the secret combinations.

refs.note: She asks her father about the old record.
She will dance before Akish.
She put it into his heart to search the old things.

people.name: Akish
people.summary: Akish was the son of Kimnor. He formed a secret combination to kill King Omer.
people.detail: He later murdered Jared and became king. His war with his sons nearly destroyed the kingdom.

refs.note: Akish gathers his kinsfolk.
They swear by the oath of the ancients.
Akish reigns after Jared is murdered.
War between Akish and his sons destroys the people.

people.name: Kimnor
people.summary: Kimnor was the father of Akish.

refs.note: Akish is called the son of Kimnor.

people.name: Esrom
people.summary: Esrom was a son of Omer. He and his brother Coriantumr fought their brother Jared.

refs.note: Omer’s sons include Esrom and Coriantumr.
They raise an army against Jared.

people.name: Coriantumr (son of Omer)
people.summary: This Coriantumr was a son of Omer. He is not the last Jaredite king.
people.detail: He and Esrom defeated their brother Jared in a night battle.

refs.note: Omer’s sons include Esrom and Coriantumr.
They spare Jared’s life.

people.name: Nimrah
people.summary: Nimrah was a son of Akish. Akish starved Nimrah’s brother to death.
people.detail: Nimrah fled with a few men to Omer.

refs.note: Nimrah is angry with his father.
He flees to Omer.

people.name: Emer
people.summary: Emer was a son of Omer. He reigned in righteousness.
people.detail: The text says he saw the Son of Righteousness before he died.

refs.note: Omer anoints Emer king.
Emer judges in righteousness.
He sees the Son of Righteousness.

people.name: Coriantum (son of Emer)
match: (?<!son of )\bCoriantum\b(?! was the son| was a descendant)
people.summary: Coriantum was a son of Emer. He walked in the steps of his father.
people.detail: He lived to 142 years old. His son Com reigned after him.

refs.note: Coriantum follows his father.
He marries a young maid in old age.

people.name: Com (son of Coriantum, in Ether 9)
match: (?<!son of )\bCom\b(?! was the son| was a descendant)
people.summary: Com was a son of Coriantum, son of Emer. His son Heth killed him.

refs.note: Com reigns after Coriantum.
Heth slays his father with his own sword.

people.name: Heth (son of Com)
match: (?<!land of |son of |begat )\bHeth\b(?! was the son|, who was the son| lived| begat)
people.summary: Heth was a son of Com. He took up the old secret plans and killed his father.
people.detail: He rejected the prophets. He died in a great famine.

refs.note: Heth embraces the secret plans.
He slays his father and reigns.
Heth perished by the famine.

people.name: Shez (son of Heth)
people.summary: Shez was the only survivor of Heth’s household. He built up a broken people.
people.detail: He remembered the Lord and built a righteous kingdom.

refs.note: Shez rebuilds a broken people.
He builds a righteous kingdom.
He lives to old age and begets Riplakish.

people.name: Shez (son of Shez)
people.summary: This Shez was the eldest son of King Shez. He rebelled against his father.
people.detail: A robber killed him because of his riches.

refs.note: The son Shez rebels and is killed.

people.name: Riplakish
people.summary: Riplakish was a son of Shez. He did not do what was right.
people.detail: He had many wives and taxed the people heavily. The people rebelled and killed him.

refs.note: Riplakish lays heavy taxes on the people.
He builds prisons for those who cannot pay.
Riplakish is killed.

people.name: Morianton (Jaredite king)
people.summary: Morianton was a descendant of Riplakish. He gathered outcasts and won the kingdom.
people.detail: He eased the burdens of the people. He was cut off from the Lord for his whoredoms.

refs.note: Morianton gains power over many cities.
He is just to the people but not to himself.

people.name: Kim
people.summary: Kim was a son of Morianton. He did not reign in righteousness.
people.detail: His brother rebelled and held him captive for life.

refs.note: Kim reigns after his father.
Kim lives in captivity and begets Levi.

people.name: Levi (Jaredite king)
people.summary: Levi was a son of Kim, born in captivity. He won back the kingdom by war.
people.detail: He did what was right in the sight of the Lord.

refs.note: Kim begets Levi in captivity.
Levi reigns and does right.

people.name: Corom
people.summary: Corom was a son of Levi. He did good all his days.

refs.note: Levi anoints Corom king.
Corom does good, and Kish reigns after him.

people.name: Kish
people.summary: Kish was a son of Corom. He reigned after his father.

refs.note: Kish reigns after Corom.
Kish dies, and Lib reigns.

people.name: Lib (son of Kish)
people.summary: Lib was a son of Kish. He did good in the sight of the Lord.
people.detail: In his days the poisonous serpents were destroyed. He was a great hunter.

refs.note: The poisonous serpents are destroyed.
The land southward is kept for game.
The people are richly blessed.

people.name: Hearthom
people.summary: Hearthom was a son of Lib. He lost the kingdom after twenty-four years.
people.detail: He lived the rest of his days in captivity.

refs.note: Hearthom reigns and loses the kingdom.

people.name: Heth (son of Hearthom)
match: \bHeth(?=, who was the son of Hearthom)
people.summary: This Heth was a son of Hearthom. He lived in captivity all his days.

refs.note: Heth is the son of Hearthom.
Heth lives in captivity.

people.name: Aaron (Jaredite)
people.summary: This Aaron was a descendant of Heth. He lived in captivity all his days.

refs.note: Aaron descends from Heth.
Aaron dwells in captivity.

people.name: Amnigaddah
people.role: Jaredite in captivity, son of Aaron
people.summary: Amnigaddah was a son of Aaron. He lived in captivity all his days.

refs.note: Amnigaddah is the son of Aaron.
Amnigaddah dwells in captivity.

people.name: Coriantum (son of Amnigaddah)
match: (?<!son of )\bCoriantum\b(?! was the son| was a descendant)
people.summary: This Coriantum was a son of Amnigaddah. He lived in captivity all his days.

refs.note: Coriantum is the son of Amnigaddah.
Coriantum dwells in captivity.

people.name: Com (son of Coriantum, in Ether 10)
match: (?<!son of )\bCom\b(?! was the son| was a descendant)
people.summary: This Com was a son of Coriantum, who lived in captivity. Com won back the whole kingdom.
people.detail: He fought robbers and protected the prophets. The Lord blessed him for it.

refs.note: Com defeats King Amgid.
The prophets flee to Com for protection.
Com is blessed.

people.name: Amgid
people.summary: Amgid was a Jaredite king. Com fought him for many years and won.

refs.note: Com gains power over Amgid.

people.name: Shiblom (Jaredite king)
people.summary: Shiblom was a son of Com. Ether 1 spells the name Shiblon.
people.detail: His brother had the prophets put to death. Shiblom was slain in a great war.

refs.note: Shiblom reigns, and his brother rebels.
His brother has the prophets killed.
Shiblom is slain.

people.name: Seth (Jaredite)
people.summary: Seth was a son of Shiblom. He lived in captivity all his days.

refs.note: Seth is the son of Shiblon.
Seth is brought into captivity.

people.name: Ahah
people.summary: Ahah was a son of Seth. He took the kingdom and did much iniquity.

refs.note: Ahah causes much bloodshed.

people.name: Ethem
people.summary: Ethem was a descendant of Ahah. He judged in wickedness all his days.
people.detail: Many prophets came in his time. The people did not listen.

refs.note: Ethem obtains the kingdom.
Many prophets come in his days.
Ethem judges in wickedness.

people.name: Moron (Jaredite king)
people.summary: Moron was a son of Ethem. He did wickedly as king.
people.detail: A descendant of the brother of Jared took his kingdom. He lived in captivity after that.

refs.note: Moron reigns and does wickedly.
Moron wins back the kingdom.
Moron loses it and dwells in captivity.

people.name: Coriantor
people.role: Son of Moron, father of Ether
people.summary: Coriantor was a son of Moron. He lived in captivity all his days.
people.detail: Prophets came in his days. He was the father of the prophet Ether.

refs.note: Ether is a descendant of Coriantor.
Prophets come in the days of Coriantor.
Coriantor begets Ether.

people.name: Ether
people.summary: Ether was the son of Coriantor and the last Jaredite prophet. He wrote the record that Moroni abridged.
people.detail: The people cast him out, so he hid in a cave. He watched the final war and finished his record.

refs.note: Ether wrote this record.
The Spirit moves Ether to prophesy in the days of Coriantumr.
He hides in the cavity of a rock.
Ether finishes and hides his record.

scholarship.text: One proposal links Ether to a Hebrew root meaning to pray. Jaredite roots remain speculative.

people.name: Cohor (Ether 13)
people.summary: This Cohor lived in the days of Coriantumr. His fair sons and daughters did not repent.

refs.note: The sons and daughters of Cohor do not repent.

people.name: Corihor (Ether 13)
people.summary: This Corihor lived in the days of Coriantumr. His fair sons and daughters did not repent.

refs.note: The sons and daughters of Corihor do not repent.

people.name: Shared
people.summary: Shared rose up against King Coriantumr. He captured Coriantumr for a time.
people.detail: He wounded Coriantumr in the thigh. Shared died in the wars that followed.

refs.note: Shared takes Coriantumr captive.
They fight in the valley of Gilgal.
Shared wounds Coriantumr in the thigh.

people.name: Gilead
people.summary: Gilead was the brother of Shared. He fought Coriantumr after Shared died.
people.detail: Secret combinations made his army strong. His own high priest murdered him on his throne.

refs.note: The brother of Shared fights Coriantumr.
His name is Gilead.
His high priest murders him.

people.name: Lib (Ether 14)
people.summary: This Lib was a man of great stature. He fought Coriantumr for the kingdom.
people.detail: Coriantumr killed him on the plains of Agosh. His brother Shiz took his place.

refs.note: Lib takes the kingdom.
Coriantumr kills Lib.

people.name: Shiz
people.summary: Shiz was the brother of Lib. He swore to avenge Lib and fought Coriantumr to the end.
people.detail: He refused to spare the people. Coriantumr killed him in the last battle.

refs.note: Shiz pursues Coriantumr and burns cities.
Shiz demands that Coriantumr give himself up.
Coriantumr smites off the head of Shiz.

people.name: Archeantus
people.summary: Archeantus was one of Mormon’s choice men. He died in battle with the Lamanites.

refs.note: Mormon reports that Archeantus has fallen.

people.name: Luram
people.summary: Luram was one of Mormon’s choice men. He died in battle with the Lamanites.

refs.note: Luram falls with Archeantus and Emron.

people.name: Emron
people.summary: Emron was one of Mormon’s choice men. He died in battle with the Lamanites.

refs.note: Emron falls with Archeantus and Luram.

people.name: Amoron
people.summary: Amoron told Mormon about the Lamanite prisoners from Sherrizah.

refs.note: Mormon writes what he learned from Amoron.

people.name: Zenephi
people.summary: Zenephi led an army in Mormon’s last years. His army took food from widows.

refs.note: The army of Zenephi carries away the provisions.

routes.title: Lehi’s family leaves Jerusalem
routes.text: The Lord told Lehi to leave Jerusalem. The family camped three days past the Red Sea borders.

research.text: The road down the Arabah valley is one common proposal. The text names no road.

routes.title: The sons return for the brass plates
routes.text: Nephi and his brothers went up to Jerusalem for the plates. They came back with the plates and Zoram.

routes.title: The sons bring Ishmael’s family
routes.text: The sons went up to Jerusalem again. Ishmael’s family came down with them to the valley.

routes.title: From the valley to Nahom
routes.text: The family traveled south-southeast near the Red Sea. Nephi’s bow broke on the way. Ishmael died at Nahom.

research.text: Researchers follow the old incense road east of the coastal mountains. The text names only Shazer and Nahom.

routes.title: Eastward to Bountiful
routes.text: From Nahom the family traveled nearly eastward. After eight years in the wilderness they reached the sea.

research.text: This line runs along the south edge of the great Arabian desert. The stops are not known.

routes.title: Lehi’s family reaches the promised land
routes.text: The ship crossed the sea and arrived at the promised land.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the landing was on the west coast, far south. It was the place of first inheritance.

routes.title: Nephi’s people move to the land of Nephi
routes.text: Nephi’s people fled into the wilderness for many days. They called the new place Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates 80 to 100 miles on foot. The straight line was much shorter.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla cross the sea
routes.text: The Lord brought Mulek’s people across the great waters into the land north.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they landed near the neck by the east sea.

routes.title: The people of Zarahemla go up the Sidon
routes.text: They came from the place of landing up into the south wilderness.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks quarrels slowly pushed some of them up the river to Zarahemla.

routes.title: Mosiah leads his people down to Zarahemla
routes.text: Mosiah fled out of the land of Nephi and came down into Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the text always says “down” for this direction. Zarahemla was lower than Nephi.

routes.title: Zeniff’s people go up to Nephi
routes.text: A group went up into the wilderness to return to the land of Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Zeniff’s people repaired the walls of Lehi-Nephi and Shilom.

routes.title: Ammon’s men search for Zeniff’s people
routes.text: Sixteen men wandered forty days. They did not know the way up.

sorenson.text: Sorenson points to Mosiah 7:4. The searchers knew they had to go up.

routes.title: Limhi’s explorers miss Zarahemla
routes.text: Forty-three men looked for Zarahemla. They found a land of bones and returned.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they passed through the neck without knowing it. He estimates about 400 straight-line miles.

routes.title: Alma’s people flee to Helam
routes.text: Alma’s people fled eight days’ journey into the wilderness.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates about 11 miles a day with families and flocks.

routes.title: Alma’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: One day to the valley of Alma, then twelve more days to Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson adds the trips for 22 or 23 days from Nephi to Zarahemla. That is about 250 miles walked.

routes.title: Limhi’s people escape to Zarahemla
routes.text: Limhi’s people went around the land of Shilom toward Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the regular road to Manti went through Gideon.

routes.title: A Lamanite army gets lost
routes.text: The army lost the trail. It found Amulon and then Helam.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says this shows very broken country. Both lands were within about 85 miles.

routes.title: The Amlicite battles
routes.text: The fight moved from Amnihu to Gideon, then back to the river crossing.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says all this took about 36 hours. So the area spanned only tens of miles.

routes.title: Alma goes over to Gideon
routes.text: Alma went over to the east of the river Sidon, into the valley of Gideon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Gideon was about one day from Zarahemla.

routes.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
routes.text: Alma went to Melek, then three days north to Ammonihah, then Sidom.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Alma circled the Sidon basin, where most Nephites lived.

routes.title: Lamanites strike Ammonihah from the west
routes.text: Lamanite armies came in upon the wilderness side and went over to Ammonihah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they went up the west coast unseen, then crossed a pass.

routes.title: The sons of Mosiah go up to Nephi
routes.text: They journeyed many days in the wilderness to reach the land of Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes the same hard climb as Ammon’s search party.

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Jershon
routes.text: The converted Lamanites left Nephi. The Nephites gave them the land of Jershon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes that travelers went over an upland to reach Jershon.

routes.title: The people of Ammon move to Melek
routes.text: The people of Ammon left Jershon and came over into the land of Melek.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says Melek was the safest place. Mountains guarded it on the west.

routes.title: Lamanites go “round about” to Manti
routes.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and went round about by the head of Sidon.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks this took weeks. The east wilderness was too rough to cross directly.

routes.title: Moroni marches to Manti
routes.text: Moroni left part of his army in Jershon and marched to the land of Manti.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes Moroni still had time to ask Alma, get an answer, and march.

routes.title: Morianton flees toward the land northward
routes.text: Morianton’s people fled toward the land northward. They were stopped by the narrow pass.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Morianton took the road nearer the coast.

routes.title: Teancum heads off Morianton
routes.text: Moroni sent an army to head off Morianton. They met him at the pass.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks Teancum took a different, inland road and got there first.

routes.title: Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
routes.text: Amalickiah took city after city on the east borders by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 3 shows the army staying down by the seashore. The text also lists Nephihah and Gid as taken.

routes.title: Teancum draws the Lamanites out of Mulek
routes.text: The Lamanites chased Teancum down by the seashore until they came near Bountiful.

sorenson.text: Sorenson estimates Bountiful to Mulek at about 12 miles in a straight line.

routes.title: Moroni retakes the east coast
routes.text: The Lamanites fled from city to city, then down to the seashore and Moroni.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks this was one day of marching. The southward part was 15 miles at most.

routes.title: Helaman’s young men march to Judea
routes.text: Helaman marched the two thousand young men to the city of Judea.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says they came south from their home in Melek.

routes.title: Helaman lures the army out of Antiparah
routes.text: They marched near Antiparah as if going to the city by the seashore.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the road went past the summit and down to the coast.

routes.title: Hagoth’s ships sail north
routes.text: Hagoth launched ships into the west sea. Some went to the land northward.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes most settlers went north overland. Two ships are not heard of again.

routes.title: Nephites spread into the land northward
routes.text: Many people went forth unto the land northward and spread out.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the main move went overland through the narrow pass.

routes.title: Coriantumr strikes the center
routes.text: A Lamanite army came into the center of the land and took Zarahemla.

sorenson.text: Sorenson calls this attack a mistake. It played to Nephite strength in the center.

routes.title: Nephites driven into Bountiful
routes.text: The Nephites were driven into the land of Bountiful and fortified a line.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they left by the west pass and fortified the west coast plain.

routes.title: Nephi and Lehi preach from Bountiful
routes.text: They began at Bountiful, then Gid and Mulek, then Zarahemla and Nephi.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the east coast held half of the Nephite lands of that time.

routes.title: People gather from the south
routes.text: The people came from all parts of the land into one place.

sorenson.text: Sorenson notes people came from the south and from colonies in the north.

routes.title: People gather from the north
routes.text: People in the land northward also came to the gathering place.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says this only makes sense for one joined territory north and south.

routes.title: Mormon’s army leaves the land southward
routes.text: The Nephites lost Angola and David. They moved to Joshua, then fled north.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks they held the western pass from Joshua for fourteen years.

routes.title: The last retreat to Cumorah
routes.text: The Nephites lost Desolation and Boaz. They held Jordan, then gathered at Cumorah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson thinks the last wars stayed within about 100 miles of the narrow pass.

routes.title: Lamanites cross the neck
routes.text: The Lamanites came down to the city of Desolation to battle.

sorenson.text: Sorenson’s map 17 shows the attacks coming north through the neck.

routes.title: Omer flees from Moron
routes.text: Omer passed by the hill Shim and Cumorah to a place called Ablom.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says “many days” suggests a winding route. Moron was near Desolation.

routes.title: The last Jaredite war
routes.text: The war moved east to the hill Comnor, north to Ripliancum, then to Ramah.

sorenson.text: Sorenson says the last Jaredite battles were in the eastern lowlands. They match the Nephite end.

distances.label: ~180 mi straight · 22–23 days
distances.text: Alma’s people took 8 days, then 13 days. At 11 miles a day, about 250 miles walked.

distances.label: ~75 mi up the river
distances.text: Manti was the farthest settled point upstream.

distances.label: ~160 mi to the Bountiful line
distances.text: About 100 miles downstream, plus two lands of about 30 miles each.

distances.label: ~400 mi straight
distances.text: Limhi’s explorers would not go much past double the expected trip.

distances.label: Day and a half · 60–125 mi
distances.text: The width depends on how far a Nephite went in a day.

distances.label: 2–3 days · ~50 mi
distances.text: “Took his journey over into” suggests more than one day.

distances.label: 3 days · ~50 mi
distances.text: Alma 8:6 gives three days’ journey north.

distances.label: ~1 day
distances.text: The Amlicite story limits these distances.

distances.label: ~12 mi
distances.text: The decoy march and return took one hot day.

distances.label: ~20 mi
distances.text: A guess of about one day’s walk.

distances.label: ~80 mi of Nephite coast
distances.text: Amalickiah had a short road here. The west coast road was over 250 miles.

distances.label: ~200 mi coast to coast
distances.text: Moroni, Nephihah, Aaron, and Ammonihah spread across the land.

distances.label: ≤10 mi
distances.text: Noah could see Shilom from his tower.

distances.label: ≤85 mi straight
distances.text: A lost army found Amulon and Helam.

distances.label: ≤~100 mi
distances.text: The last Nephites did not go much farther north.

figures.title: Overall shape
figures.text: Sorenson begins with Alma 22:32. The land southward is nearly surrounded by water. A small neck joins it to the land northward. The result looks like an hourglass. Both far ends stay unknown.

figures.title: Chief ethnic areas
figures.text: In Alma’s time, Lamanites held Nephi and both coasts. Nephites held the Sidon basin and Bountiful. The Jaredites were already gone. Sorenson says the Nephites sat like a cork in a bottle.

figures.title: Amalickiah’s attack by the east seashore
figures.text: Amalickiah drove up the east coast toward the narrow neck. Sorenson shows his army staying near the shore. The text names Nephihah and Gid among the cities taken.

figures.title: Teancum intercepts Morianton
figures.text: Morianton fled toward the land northward. Teancum knew he must use the narrow pass. Teancum took another road and got there first.

figures.title: Lamanites go “round about”
figures.text: The Lamanites left Antionum and circled through the wilderness to Manti. The trip took long enough for Moroni to set a trap.

figures.title: Some Jaredite locations
figures.text: Omer went from Moron past Shim and Cumorah to Ablom by the sea. Sorenson links these Jaredite places to the Nephite map. Higher land lay to the west.

figures.title: Limhi’s explorers
figures.text: The explorers missed Zarahemla and kept going north. They found Ether’s plates near Ramah. Sorenson uses this trip to estimate the size of the land.

figures.title: The Amlicite conflict
figures.text: All these moves took place in about 36 hours. So the area around Zarahemla covered only tens of miles.

figures.title: Alma’s preaching circuit
figures.text: Alma taught in Gideon, Melek, Ammonihah, and Sidom. Sorenson thinks he circled the Sidon basin, where most Nephites lived.

figures.title: Four cities across the land southward
figures.text: Moroni, Nephihah, Aaron, and Ammonihah touch one another in the text. Placed side by side, the land is about 200 miles wide.

figures.title: The flight of Alma’s and Limhi’s peoples
figures.text: These two escapes give the best clues to the distance from Nephi to Zarahemla. The online PDF copy is missing this map’s page. The steps here follow Sorenson’s text.

figures.title: Early spread of major groups
figures.text: The early groups stayed small and apart. Sorenson compares them to islands in a sea of wilderness.

figures.title: Expansion in the time of the two Almas
figures.text: By about 50 BC, the Lamanite king ruled from sea to sea. Nephites filled the Sidon basin and moved into Bountiful.

figures.title: Nephite expansion into the land northward
figures.text: Hagoth built a few ships. Sorenson thinks most settlers went north overland through the land Desolation.

figures.title: Possible places of the destroyed cities
figures.text: A few destroyed cities have known places. Sorenson sorts the rest by the order of the list. Many points here are guesses.

figures.title: Final flight from the land southward
figures.text: The Nephites left Zarahemla through Angola and David. They held Joshua by the west sea for years.

figures.title: Final wars in the land northward
figures.text: The last Nephite wars stayed near the narrow neck. They were in the same area as the last Jaredite wars.
